headline: Stevie Nicks reflects on writing 'Landslide' while unsure about her future with Lindsey Buckingham
description: “I wrote this song in Aspen, Colorado, when I was deciding whether or not Lindsey and I should continue,” Nicks said
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Stevie Nicks has looked back on the personal and professional uncertainty that inspired her to write Fleetwood Mac’s iconic song Landslide, recalling a time when she was unsure whether she and Lindsey Buckingham should continue their relationship and musical partnership.

The singer, 78, reflected on the song’s origins while attending the City of Hope 2026 Spirit of Life Gala on October 27, where she introduced the track and shared the story behind its creation.

“I wrote this song in Aspen, Colorado, when I was deciding whether or not Lindsey [Buckingham] and I should continue,” Nicks told the audience. “Well, it was a long time ago and 930,000 years later, we still continued.”

Nicks recalled being in a house in the mountains, looking out over snow-covered hills when she felt inspired to write. She explained that the people she was staying with had gone out to dinner, leaving her with the view and time to create.

“I’m like ok because I’m so poor that just sitting in this house when you’re looking out at this view is so fantastic, I’m going to write a fantastic song,” she said.

The singer also joked about the guitar she used to write the track, adding: “I just happened to bring my Goya [guitar], which I could hardly play, but I thought it looked good so I wrote this song.”

Nicks and Buckingham began dating in 1972 and released their album Buckingham Nicks in 1973. The record was not a commercial success, and the pair were dropped by their label, leaving them uncertain about their future in music.

They eventually joined Fleetwood Mac in 1975, with Nicks’ Landslide appearing on the band’s self-titled album that year.

Although their romantic relationship ended in 1976 as Fleetwood Mac recorded Rumours, their complicated history continued to shape their music and the band’s legacy.

Buckingham recently revealed that he and Nicks are now in frequent contact, crediting work on a Fleetwood Mac documentary with helping to heal past tensions.

Speaking to E! News in August, Buckingham said the documentary process had been a “circular healing process” for the band and that their relationship had improved.

Nicks has previously described her relationship with Buckingham as difficult and turbulent, but also “fantastic”, reflecting the lasting personal and creative connection between the two musicians.

headline: Kieran Culkin nearly turned down 'Hunger Games' before his wife convinced him
description: Kieran Culkin considered rejecting Caesar Flickerman's role until his wife helped him approach character differently
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Kieran Culkin has revealed that he nearly turned down the role of Caesar Flickerman in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping because he was concerned about following Stanley Tucci's performance in the original films.

Speaking at the film's London premiere on October 28, the Succession actor explained that he initially viewed accepting the part as a risk, given how popular Tucci's portrayal had become with audiences.

"It was already too much pressure," Culkin told The Hollywood Reporter. "To me, this was like a no-brainer: don't do it, because everyone loves what Stanley Tucci did with the role. So I was like, 'They're gonna hate [me].' I feel like I'm being set up for failure."

Culkin also told Deadline that he felt he had a different screen presence from Tucci and did not want to imitate his predecessor or disregard the original characterisation entirely.

Culkin discussed his concerns with his wife, Jazz Charton, who suggested that he incorporate one element of Tucci's performance while developing his own interpretation of Caesar.

"Why don't you do that but pick one thing that Stanley did?" she suggested.

Culkin praised the advice, describing it as the best guidance he received during the process. He has been married to Charton since 2013.

The actor also recalled that director Francis Lawrence reassured him during their first meeting that he did not need to recreate Tucci's portrayal.

Lawrence reportedly encouraged Culkin to avoid copying details such as the character's distinctive teeth and hairstyle, and instead approach Caesar as someone at an earlier stage of his career.

Set 24 years before Katniss Everdeen enters the arena, Sunrise on the Reaping follows the origins of future mentor Haymitch Abernathy while revisiting younger versions of familiar franchise characters.

Culkin explained that his version of Caesar is an ambitious, anxious presenter still trying to establish himself, unlike Tucci's more experienced television host.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on November 20 2026.

headline: Sindh govt-run tourist resorts struggle to turn a profit
description: Despite attracting thousands of visitors, STDC continues to incur losses, raising concerns over financial management
author: Razzak Abro
article_text:
Despite Sindh’s rich cultural heritage and numerous tourist attractions, several resorts and hotels operated by the Sindh Tourism Development Corporation (STDC) are reportedly running at a loss, raising questions about whether these facilities are generating revenue for the provincial government or placing an additional burden on the public exchequer.

According to the Auditor General of Pakistan’s audit report for 2024-25, seven hotels and resorts managed by the STDC incurred total expenses of Rs42.1 million during the year, while their combined revenue stood at just Rs19.7 million. The resulting loss to the Sindh government amounted to Rs22.3 million.

The highest loss was recorded at the resorts located near Keenjhar Lake in Thatta district. According to the report, the facilities generated Rs9.073 million in revenue against expenses of Rs22 million, leaving a substantial gap between earnings and operating costs.

The disparity is particularly striking given the popularity of Keenjhar Lake as a recreational destination. An estimated 10,000 to 12,000 people visit the lake every week, the majority of them from Karachi. Despite this steady flow of visitors, the resorts have reportedly struggled to generate sufficient revenue to cover their expenses.

The audit report also identified losses at several other facilities managed by the corporation, including Rooplo Kolhi Resort, Marvi Rest House, Haleji Lake Resort, Baqar Lake Resort, Ranikot Resort and Lal Shahbaz Resort in Sehwan.

Other properties operated by the STDC include Sambar Inn Hotel in Larkana and a motel in Garhi Khuda Bakhsh. However, details of their annual expenses and revenues were not available in the report cited.

The findings have raised questions about the commercial performance of tourism facilities that are intended to serve visitors while also generating income for the provincial government. Although these properties operate on commercial lines, the audit figures suggest that their earnings have not been sufficient to meet operating costs.

However, the STDC has disputed the claim that its resorts and hotels are still operating at a loss.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, STDC Managing Director Syed Fayyaz Shah said the facilities had previously faced financial difficulties, but the situation had changed after the introduction of a computerised management system. He said room bookings were now handled online, helping increase the corporation’s revenue.

Shah did not, however, provide figures to substantiate the claim that the facilities were no longer running at a loss, leaving the corporation’s current financial position unclear.

Sindh has considerable potential for tourism, with a wide range of historical, cultural and recreational destinations spread across the province. The performance of publicly managed resorts is therefore significant not only for the provincial exchequer but also for efforts to develop tourism and create employment.

The STDC was established in August 1991 and operates under the provincial tourism department. Following the 18th Constitutional Amendment in 2010, the management of several historical, cultural and tourist sites was transferred from the federal government to the provinces. The transfer also included properties associated with these sites, placing them under the Sindh government’s administration.

The corporation’s website states that it has around 100 registered tour operators working with it to promote tourism across the province. Yet the audit findings highlight a persistent question: why are publicly managed tourism facilities failing to generate enough revenue to cover their costs, despite the province’s tourism potential and the popularity of destinations such as Keenjhar Lake?

The absence of updated financial figures from the corporation makes it difficult to determine whether online booking and other administrative changes have improved profitability or whether the facilities continue to depend on public funds to meet their operating expenses.

article_html:
KARACHI:

Despite Sindh’s rich cultural heritage and numerous tourist attractions, several resorts and hotels operated by the Sindh Tourism Development Corporation (STDC) are reportedly running at a loss, raising questions about whether these facilities are generating revenue for the provincial government or placing an additional burden on the public exchequer.

According to the Auditor General of Pakistan’s audit report for 2024-25, seven hotels and resorts managed by the STDC incurred total expenses of Rs42.1 million during the year, while their combined revenue stood at just Rs19.7 million. The resulting loss to the Sindh government amounted to Rs22.3 million.

Read: STDC holds second meeting in 23 years since establishment

The highest loss was recorded at the resorts located near Keenjhar Lake in Thatta district. According to the report, the facilities generated Rs9.073 million in revenue against expenses of Rs22 million, leaving a substantial gap between earnings and operating costs.

The disparity is particularly striking given the popularity of Keenjhar Lake as a recreational destination. An estimated 10,000 to 12,000 people visit the lake every week, the majority of them from Karachi. Despite this steady flow of visitors, the resorts have reportedly struggled to generate sufficient revenue to cover their expenses.

The audit report also identified losses at several other facilities managed by the corporation, including Rooplo Kolhi Resort, Marvi Rest House, Haleji Lake Resort, Baqar Lake Resort, Ranikot Resort and Lal Shahbaz Resort in Sehwan.

Other properties operated by the STDC include Sambar Inn Hotel in Larkana and a motel in Garhi Khuda Bakhsh. However, details of their annual expenses and revenues were not available in the report cited.

The findings have raised questions about the commercial performance of tourism facilities that are intended to serve visitors while also generating income for the provincial government. Although these properties operate on commercial lines, the audit figures suggest that their earnings have not been sufficient to meet operating costs.

However, the STDC has disputed the claim that its resorts and hotels are still operating at a loss.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, STDC Managing Director Syed Fayyaz Shah said the facilities had previously faced financial difficulties, but the situation had changed after the introduction of a computerised management system. He said room bookings were now handled online, helping increase the corporation’s revenue.

Shah did not, however, provide figures to substantiate the claim that the facilities were no longer running at a loss, leaving the corporation’s current financial position unclear.

Read More: Sindh suffers without a viable tourism policy

Sindh has considerable potential for tourism, with a wide range of historical, cultural and recreational destinations spread across the province. The performance of publicly managed resorts is therefore significant not only for the provincial exchequer but also for efforts to develop tourism and create employment.

The STDC was established in August 1991 and operates under the provincial tourism department. Following the 18th Constitutional Amendment in 2010, the management of several historical, cultural and tourist sites was transferred from the federal government to the provinces. The transfer also included properties associated with these sites, placing them under the Sindh government’s administration.

The corporation’s website states that it has around 100 registered tour operators working with it to promote tourism across the province. Yet the audit findings highlight a persistent question: why are publicly managed tourism facilities failing to generate enough revenue to cover their costs, despite the province’s tourism potential and the popularity of destinations such as Keenjhar Lake?

The absence of updated financial figures from the corporation makes it difficult to determine whether online booking and other administrative changes have improved profitability or whether the facilities continue to depend on public funds to meet their operating expenses.

headline: Michael Douglas says Catherine Zeta-Jones had no 'veto power' over his bombshell memoir
description: “She would not have veto power, but I would not put anything in the book that she would not like,” Douglas said
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Michael Douglas has revealed that his wife, Catherine Zeta-Jones, did not have the power to veto any stories included in his memoir, One Helluva Ride, although he insisted he would not have written anything he knew she would dislike.

Speaking during an appearance on CNN's Coming Up, the 82-year-old actor discussed the book, which was released earlier in October, and explained why he did not give his wife editorial control over its contents.

“She would not have veto power, but I would not put anything in the book that she would not like,” Douglas said.

The actor also reflected on his life before meeting Zeta-Jones, describing it as “B.C. — Before Catherine”. The couple married in 2000 and share two children, Dylan and Carys.

Douglas specifically mentioned his affair with Romancing the Stone co-star Kathleen Turner, which took place while they were working on the 1984 film. At the time, Zeta-Jones was seven years old.

“When I was making Romancing the Stone and carrying on with Kathleen Turner, Catherine was 7 years old,” he said. “People have a life, and I'm very proud of the chapter on Catherine and speaking about my love for her. I think she understands me by now after 26 years.”

Douglas also spoke about the couple's age difference, joking that people initially doubted their relationship would last. He said they were both at a more experienced stage in their lives and careers when they got together.

The actor added that he has reached a point where he has largely stepped away from working and is more focused on his family, friends and memories. He said writing the memoir helped him recover stories and experiences he had forgotten over the years.

Zeta-Jones previously joked that she had no intention of reading her husband's memoir when she was tired at night. Speaking on the Today show on October 8, she said: “As much as I love my husband, when I'm tired at night, I have no intention of reading about him. But everyone else should.”

Douglas later responded to her comment during an appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, agreeing with the host that it was probably for the best that she had not read the book.

In the memoir, Douglas revisits his personal life and decades-long Hollywood career, including past relationships and his eventual marriage to Zeta-Jones.

headline: Fakhar: The man who delivers when it matters the most
description: Selfless team player and proven big-match performer
author: Saleem Khaliq
article_text:
KARACHI: Sri Lanka’s total had reached 325, and the general feeling in the Pakistani dressing room was that chasing such a massive target would not be easy. However, one player appeared completely unfazed. He had guided his team to victory in big matches before and was confident that he could deliver another such performance.

As he walked out to the crease, the scoreboard soon read 14-2. After Maaz Sadaqat, Babar Azam also lost his wicket, but there was not a wrinkle of concern on his forehead. He believed in himself and was determined to make something happen before returning to the pavilion. He then built a substantial partnership with young Saad Baig, putting Pakistan firmly on the path to victory.

You all know who I am talking about: Fakhar Zaman.

A selfless individual, Fakhar has never placed his personal performance above the interests of the team. He has no PR team, nor has anyone bestowed grand nicknames such as King, Cheetah or Lion upon him. He does not have an army of devoted social media followers or a group of former cricketers constantly singing his praises.

He has no obsession with becoming captain, nor does he possess the arrogance to consider anyone beneath him. Fakhar is an extremely simple and down-to-earth person. He leads an ordinary lifestyle and has never considered himself a superstar.

Perhaps his career statistics do not fully reflect his talent, but there is absolutely no doubt that he is a match-winner.

When many players realise that their team is in trouble, they either score a few runs and then step aside or try to protect themselves by pushing younger players into the spotlight. Fakhar has never done that. He has always put the team's interests first, and that is precisely why he has earned respect.

In our country, many cricketers continue to feel insecure even after becoming established stars. They fear that a young player might take their place, which is why they often hesitate to encourage emerging talent.

Fakhar Zaman is quite the opposite. Young cricketers regularly benefit from his advice and guidance.

A few months ago, Fakhar shared an interesting story with me. He told me how he had been impressed by Sahibzada Farhan's performances in the past and had contacted him through Facebook, inviting him to play for his domestic team.

Similarly, he has spent years with Lahore Qalandars in the PSL alongside Atif Rana and Sameen Rana and considers the franchise his family.

In the recent triangular series, Fakhar Zaman had failed to make an impact before the final. Some quarters even demanded that he be dropped from the team. However, the team management continued to back him, and Fakhar responded by scoring a century and guiding Pakistan to victory.

Players generally come under tremendous pressure in major contests, but Fakhar's performances tend to become even more impressive on such occasions. Without a doubt, he is a big-match player who rises to the occasion.

Today, while scrolling through social media, I came across a clip of Ahmed Shehzad. I generally avoid listening to such "brilliant" analysis, but the headline caught my attention, so I decided to watch it.

He was essentially saying something along the following lines:

"Fakhar has been given so many opportunities, and eventually he has played one big innings. The same will happen with Babar if we keep giving him chances."

Comments like these reek of jealousy.

Is there any player in our team who performs consistently in every match? If you believe that a player, when given four matches, is capable of winning you at least one of them, then you should never drop him.

Consider Shahid Afridi's example. Every few matches, he would produce an individual performance that won the game for Pakistan. That is why he remains the Pakistani cricketer with the highest number of Player of the Match awards.

Players like Fakhar are invaluable assets in World Cups. The next mega event will take place in Africa next year, and he could prove extremely useful there.

We are often critical of Mike Hesson, but in this instance, he deserves appreciation for maintaining his faith in Fakhar Zaman and refusing to give in to social media pressure.

Captain Shaheen Afridi, whether leading Lahore Qalandars or the Pakistan national team, always writes Fakhar Zaman's name first on the team sheet.

Fakhar's fitness concerns have also eased. He can comfortably represent the country for another two to three years. He should be rested against teams like Zimbabwe and Ireland and given opportunities in important matches. This approach could help prolong his career.

Fakhar has demonstrated how a single innings can breathe new life into an entire country's cricket.

The victory in the triangular series must also have eased some of the pressure on the PCB. Otherwise, questions were being raised about the very future of cricket in the country. This victory has restored hope that our team still has the strength and ability to compete.

Selectors Aaqib Javed and Sarfaraz Ahmed must also be breathing a sigh of relief.

The most encouraging aspect has been the impressive performances of the younger players. Saad Baig, Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz all performed well. The fast bowlers also showed signs of improvement.

However, Babar Azam has been extremely disappointing. He should learn from Fakhar and adopt a more positive approach. Playing with a positive mindset could help him regain his form.

Salman Ali Agha also needs to bring greater consistency to his performances.

The promising displays by young cricketers are certainly encouraging, but the presence of experienced players in the team is equally important. Fakhar, Babar and Salman could all play crucial roles in Pakistan's World Cup campaign.

Shaheen has established himself as captain and is also bowling well. The PCB should announce his appointment as captain until the World Cup so that other cricketers who dream of seeing themselves tossing the coin at the start of a match can concentrate solely on their cricket.

Here again, Fakhar Zaman sets an example. He has been playing international cricket for years but has never chased the captaincy or complained about not being appointed to the position.

These are the kind of players we need.

The nation is proud of you, Fakhar. Keep shining and continue bringing honour to Pakistan.

article_html:
KARACHI: Sri Lanka’s total had reached 325, and the general feeling in the Pakistani dressing room was that chasing such a massive target would not be easy. However, one player appeared completely unfazed. He had guided his team to victory in big matches before and was confident that he could deliver another such performance.

As he walked out to the crease, the scoreboard soon read 14-2. After Maaz Sadaqat, Babar Azam also lost his wicket, but there was not a wrinkle of concern on his forehead. He believed in himself and was determined to make something happen before returning to the pavilion. He then built a substantial partnership with young Saad Baig, putting Pakistan firmly on the path to victory.

You all know who I am talking about: Fakhar Zaman.

A selfless individual, Fakhar has never placed his personal performance above the interests of the team. He has no PR team, nor has anyone bestowed grand nicknames such as King, Cheetah or Lion upon him. He does not have an army of devoted social media followers or a group of former cricketers constantly singing his praises.

He has no obsession with becoming captain, nor does he possess the arrogance to consider anyone beneath him. Fakhar is an extremely simple and down-to-earth person. He leads an ordinary lifestyle and has never considered himself a superstar.

Perhaps his career statistics do not fully reflect his talent, but there is absolutely no doubt that he is a match-winner.

When many players realise that their team is in trouble, they either score a few runs and then step aside or try to protect themselves by pushing younger players into the spotlight. Fakhar has never done that. He has always put the team's interests first, and that is precisely why he has earned respect.

In our country, many cricketers continue to feel insecure even after becoming established stars. They fear that a young player might take their place, which is why they often hesitate to encourage emerging talent.

Fakhar Zaman is quite the opposite. Young cricketers regularly benefit from his advice and guidance.

A few months ago, Fakhar shared an interesting story with me. He told me how he had been impressed by Sahibzada Farhan's performances in the past and had contacted him through Facebook, inviting him to play for his domestic team.

Similarly, he has spent years with Lahore Qalandars in the PSL alongside Atif Rana and Sameen Rana and considers the franchise his family.

In the recent triangular series, Fakhar Zaman had failed to make an impact before the final. Some quarters even demanded that he be dropped from the team. However, the team management continued to back him, and Fakhar responded by scoring a century and guiding Pakistan to victory.

Players generally come under tremendous pressure in major contests, but Fakhar's performances tend to become even more impressive on such occasions. Without a doubt, he is a big-match player who rises to the occasion.

Today, while scrolling through social media, I came across a clip of Ahmed Shehzad. I generally avoid listening to such "brilliant" analysis, but the headline caught my attention, so I decided to watch it.

He was essentially saying something along the following lines:

"Fakhar has been given so many opportunities, and eventually he has played one big innings. The same will happen with Babar if we keep giving him chances."

Comments like these reek of jealousy.

Is there any player in our team who performs consistently in every match? If you believe that a player, when given four matches, is capable of winning you at least one of them, then you should never drop him.

Consider Shahid Afridi's example. Every few matches, he would produce an individual performance that won the game for Pakistan. That is why he remains the Pakistani cricketer with the highest number of Player of the Match awards.

Players like Fakhar are invaluable assets in World Cups. The next mega event will take place in Africa next year, and he could prove extremely useful there.

We are often critical of Mike Hesson, but in this instance, he deserves appreciation for maintaining his faith in Fakhar Zaman and refusing to give in to social media pressure.

Captain Shaheen Afridi, whether leading Lahore Qalandars or the Pakistan national team, always writes Fakhar Zaman's name first on the team sheet.

Fakhar's fitness concerns have also eased. He can comfortably represent the country for another two to three years. He should be rested against teams like Zimbabwe and Ireland and given opportunities in important matches. This approach could help prolong his career.

Fakhar has demonstrated how a single innings can breathe new life into an entire country's cricket.

The victory in the triangular series must also have eased some of the pressure on the PCB. Otherwise, questions were being raised about the very future of cricket in the country. This victory has restored hope that our team still has the strength and ability to compete.

Selectors Aaqib Javed and Sarfaraz Ahmed must also be breathing a sigh of relief.

The most encouraging aspect has been the impressive performances of the younger players. Saad Baig, Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz all performed well. The fast bowlers also showed signs of improvement.

However, Babar Azam has been extremely disappointing. He should learn from Fakhar and adopt a more positive approach. Playing with a positive mindset could help him regain his form.

Salman Ali Agha also needs to bring greater consistency to his performances.

The promising displays by young cricketers are certainly encouraging, but the presence of experienced players in the team is equally important. Fakhar, Babar and Salman could all play crucial roles in Pakistan's World Cup campaign.

Shaheen has established himself as captain and is also bowling well. The PCB should announce his appointment as captain until the World Cup so that other cricketers who dream of seeing themselves tossing the coin at the start of a match can concentrate solely on their cricket.

Here again, Fakhar Zaman sets an example. He has been playing international cricket for years but has never chased the captaincy or complained about not being appointed to the position.

These are the kind of players we need.

The nation is proud of you, Fakhar. Keep shining and continue bringing honour to Pakistan.

headline: Pakistan embassy rejects reports of attack on ambassador in Tehran as ‘baseless’
description: Pakistan's embassy in Tehran rejects reports of an attack on Ambassador Imran Ahmed Siddiqui as factually incorrect
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Embassy of Pakistan in Tehran categorically rejected reports circulating on social media and other forums concerning Ambassador Imran Ahmed Siddiqui, describing them as baseless and factually incorrect.

In a post on X, the embassy said it had taken note of reports concerning Siddiqui and categorically rejected them.

“The embassy categorically clarifies that these reports are baseless and factually incorrect,” it said.

Earlier, reports had emerged that Siddiqui was attacked in the Iranian capital, Tehran. According to these reports, he had been invited to attend a gathering when several individuals allegedly attacked him.

Pakistan is playing a leading role in mediation efforts between Iran and the United States to end the war that began on Feb 28 this year. The mediation efforts helped produce an interim peace agreement, known as the Islamabad MoU, in June, but the arrangement quickly unravelled.

Qatar, alongside Pakistan, has since led efforts to end the conflict, which has disrupted global shipping and oil supplies and recently spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

Washington wants Iran's decades-old nuclear programme to be part of negotiations to end the war from the outset. Tehran, however, maintains that its conditions, including an end to the US blockade of Iranian ports and the lifting of sanctions on its oil exports, must be met first.

Iran has rejected Western concerns that its nuclear programme is military in nature.

headline: ‘You Can See Everything’ and ‘Clayface’ battle for no 1 at Halloween box office
description: The two releases are heading into the weekend with projected takings of around $10 million or more each
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
A24’s You Can See Everything and Warner Bros.’ Clayface are competing for the top spot at the North American box office during the Halloween weekend, with the documentary emerging as an unexpected contender against the DC horror film.

The two releases are heading into the weekend with projected takings of around $10 million or more each. However, You Can See Everything is currently leading Friday’s box office estimates, taking in approximately $3.2 million compared with Clayface’s $3.1 million.

The documentary, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, is expected to earn between $10 million and $11 million in its third weekend. If it reaches the higher end of that projection, its domestic total could climb to $63.7 million.

Meanwhile, Clayface, directed by James Watkins, is targeting a second-weekend haul of more than $10 million. Its projected domestic total could reach $43.7 million by Sunday.

The competition marks an unusual Halloween box office race, as horror films typically benefit from the holiday's audience interest. However, You Can See Everything has developed considerable online attention, with memes and discussions surrounding the film helping sustain its theatrical run.

The documentary follows the story of former Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes and has become a surprising commercial success. After expanding from 855 to 2,655 theatres, it earned $19.5 million in its second weekend of wide release, bringing its 14-day domestic total to $52.7 million.

The film has also attracted attention for its awards-season prospects, with discussion growing around its potential Oscar recognition.

Clayface, meanwhile, marks a different kind of release for DC Studios, bringing a horror-focused take on the Batman villain to cinemas. The film opened with $33.7 million in its first week, according to the latest box office estimates.

Other films in the weekend's top five include Laika's Wildwood, which is projected to earn around $6.8 million in its second weekend, and Wicker, which is expected to take approximately $3.5 million.

The final weekend figures will determine whether You Can See Everything can hold on to its unexpected box office momentum or Clayface can claim the Halloween weekend's top position.

headline: Patrick Mahomes' family dresses as 'Toy Story' characters with Taylor Swift reference
description: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes shared their family's 'Toy Story' costumes, featuring Taylor Swift soundtrack
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and his family celebrated Halloween with a Toy Story-themed set of costumes, with Brittany Mahomes sharing photographs of their outfits on Instagram on Saturday.

Patrick dressed as Buzz Lightyear, wearing the character's signature purple hood and helmet, while Brittany took on the role of Jessie with a red cowgirl hat, long red braid and cow-print chaps.

Their three children also joined the theme. Three-year-old Bronze dressed as Woody, complete with a yellow plaid shirt, red bandana and brown cowboy hat.

Their youngest child, 21-month-old Golden, wore a green costume inspired by the franchise's three-eyed aliens.

Five-year-old Sterling chose Barbie, wearing hot pink flared trousers, a matching handbag and heart-shaped sunglasses.

Her pose attracted particular attention from fans, with one commenting, "Hahahaha SERVE it up, Sterling girl." Another wrote, "I love that Patrick always dresses up for the theme."

The family's photographs featured Taylor Swift's song "I Knew It, I Knew You" from Toy Story 5.

The track was written around the character Jessie, with Swift revealing that she composed it after watching an early version of the film. She said she "wrote this song as soon as I got home from the screening."

Toy Story 5 was released in cinemas on June 19, making the characters a timely choice for the family's Halloween outfits.

Mahomes previously admitted that he had almost forgotten about Halloween because of his football commitments. During an October 14 press conference, he recalled Brittany asking what the family would wear.

"It surprised me. I forgot about Halloween," Mahomes said. He added, "Brittany asked me, 'What are we going to be for Halloween?' I'm like, 'I didn't even think about that.'"

headline: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing from Afghan border posts: DC South Waziristan
description: Afghan Taliban personnel abandon several border posts after Pakistani forces respond to unprovoked firing
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Security forces responded to unprovoked firing from Afghan border posts near Angoor Adda in South Waziristan, forcing Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon their positions, Lower South Waziristan deputy commissioner said on Sunday.

In a statement on X, the deputy commissioner said Pakistani forces targeted several Afghan border posts, mortar positions and defensive positions in response to the firing.

He said Afghan Taliban personnel were forced to abandon their posts and flee following the intense response by Pakistani forces.

The deputy commissioner added that no casualties had so far been reported in the Pakistani border areas.

He further said Pakistani security forces were prepared to respond effectively to any form of aggression.

The latest development comes amid heightened tensions along the border in recent days.

Earlier this week, clashes near Angoor Adda along the South Waziristan border left one person dead and five members of a family injured.

Following the incident, the Pakistan Army said it had given an immediate, highly vigilant and strong response to the Afghan aggression by targeting Afghan Taliban checkposts.

It added that the military's response to the attack on civilians was continuing.

Earlier in September this year, Pakistan carried out “calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts near the Afghan border and conducted intelligence-based ground operations that killed a total of 37 terrorists following a series of deadly attacks in K-P.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, in a statement, said that three targets were destroyed in precision strikes, including a training centre for suicide bombers. It said 28 terrorists, along with several suicide bombers, were killed, while large quantities of weapons and ammunition stored at the centres and hideouts were also destroyed.

On September 24, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated that Pakistan had carried out “precision” aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan after drones launched from Afghan territory entered Pakistani airspace, describing the strikes as a response to a “deliberate and unlawful incursion”.

Pak-Afghan tensions

The development came amid fighting ​between Pakistan and Afghanistan that started in October 2025. Islamabad accuses the Afghan Taliban of harbouring ⁠militants ​who launch attacks in Pakistan, ​although Kabul denies this, calling the militancy its neighbour's domestic problem.

Amid continued tensions between the neighbours, Operation Ghazab Lil Haq was launched around the end of February following renewed clashes along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, after Afghan Taliban forces fired on multiple locations, prompting swift military retaliation by Pakistan.

The clashes intensified after Afghanistan launched a border offensive in response to Pakistani air strikes targeting terrorist positions. The two sides had agreed to a week-long ceasefire on the eve of Eidul Fitr on March 18, following requests from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

Pakistan in April put forth three core demands to the Afghan Taliban during peace talks in Urumqi, China, including Kabul formally declaring the TTP a terrorist organisation, dismantling its infrastructure, and providing verifiable proof of the action. These demands form the basis of Pakistan's negotiating position, which sources say has hardened amid persistent security concerns.

He said Afghan Taliban personnel were forced to abandon their posts and flee following the intense response by Pakistani forces.

The latest development comes amid heightened tensions along the border in recent days.

Earlier this week, clashes near Angoor Adda along the South Waziristan border left one person dead and five members of a family injured.

Following the incident, the Pakistan Army said it had given an immediate, highly vigilant and strong response to the Afghan aggression by targeting Afghan Taliban checkposts.

It added that the military's response to the attack on civilians was continuing.

Earlier in September this year, Pakistan carried out “calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts near the Afghan border and conducted intelligence-based ground operations that killed a total of 37 terrorists following a series of deadly attacks in K-P.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, in a statement, said that three targets were destroyed in precision strikes, including a training centre for suicide bombers. It said 28 terrorists, along with several suicide bombers, were killed, while large quantities of weapons and ammunition stored at the centres and hideouts were also destroyed.

On September 24, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated that Pakistan had carried out “precision” aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan after drones launched from Afghan territory entered Pakistani airspace, describing the strikes as a response to a “deliberate and unlawful incursion”.

Pak-Afghan tensions

The development came amid fighting ​between Pakistan and Afghanistan that started in October 2025. Islamabad accuses the Afghan Taliban of harbouring ⁠militants ​who launch attacks in Pakistan, ​although Kabul denies this, calling the militancy its neighbour's domestic problem.

Amid continued tensions between the neighbours, Operation Ghazab Lil Haq was launched around the end of February following renewed clashes along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, after Afghan Taliban forces fired on multiple locations, prompting swift military retaliation by Pakistan.

The clashes intensified after Afghanistan launched a border offensive in response to Pakistani air strikes targeting terrorist positions. The two sides had agreed to a week-long ceasefire on the eve of Eidul Fitr on March 18, following requests from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

Pakistan in April put forth three core demands to the Afghan Taliban during peace talks in Urumqi, China, including Kabul formally declaring the TTP a terrorist organisation, dismantling its infrastructure, and providing verifiable proof of the action. These demands form the basis of Pakistan's negotiating position, which sources say has hardened amid persistent security concerns.

headline: 'KPop Demon Hunters' returns to Netflix top 10 after new music video
description: 'KPop Demon Hunters' has returned to Netflix's top 10 nearly 500 days after its original release
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
'KPop Demon Hunters' has returned to Netflix's top 10 nearly 500 days after its original release

Netflix's KPop Demon Hunters has returned to the platform's top 10 films list nearly 500 days after its June 2025 release, setting a new record for the longest gap between a Netflix original's initial run and its return to the ranking.

The animated film previously spent 52 consecutive weeks in Netflix's top 10. It has now re-entered the chart at number seven, with renewed interest reportedly driven in part by a newly released music video featuring original animation.

The approximately 50-second video features choreography for "How It's Done", a song that played during a fight sequence in the original film without the characters performing the dance moves shown in the new footage.

The release therefore offers viewers new animated content rather than simply revisiting an existing scene.

According to Forbes contributor Paul Tassi, the video has attracted 19 million views and 170,000 likes on X, while its YouTube version has received 4.5 million views.

Netflix has also released live-action choreography videos featuring dancers performing routines to other songs from the film, which have collectively attracted millions of views.

Halloween may also have contributed to the film's renewed popularity. Tassi noted that costumes inspired by the film's characters, particularly Rumi's distinctive jackets and long purple braid, have been popular during this year's celebrations.

headline: 'Wednesday' Christina Ricci explains why she missed Halloween celebrations in childhood
description: Christina Ricci says her acting career limited childhood Halloween celebrations, but motherhood changed her experience
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Christina Ricci has revealed that her childhood acting career meant she missed out on many traditional Halloween celebrations, despite becoming widely associated with spooky films such as The Addams Family, Casper and Sleepy Hollow.

Speaking to TODAY, the 46-year-old actress explained that work commitments often prevented her from dressing up and going trick-or-treating with other children. She did, however, experience some celebrations when she was younger.

"I did a little bit, and certainly when I was really small I would go with my family," Ricci recalled.

Despite her association with Halloween-themed entertainment, the actress revealed that Christmas has always been her favourite holiday.

"But my favorite holiday is Christmas," she said, explaining that she does not necessarily identify her personal interests with the characters she has portrayed on screen.

Ricci also admitted that she enjoys seeing elaborate Halloween decorations, including oversized spiders and animated skeletons displayed around neighbourhoods.

Her relationship with the holiday has changed since becoming a mother to Freddie and Cleopatra. Ricci said her children have given her a new reason to participate in Halloween traditions.

"Halloween has been a thing ever since I had my own kids," she told TODAY. "So now I do Halloween because of my kids, and I've really learned to appreciate it," she added.

For Halloween 2026, the actress planned to take her children trick-or-treating around their neighbourhood before hosting a family gathering with a chilli cookout.

Ricci also recalled a childhood costume tradition involving a gorilla outfit passed down among her mother's four children.

As the youngest, she inherited the costume and wore it for several Halloweens, creating different variations, including a gorilla ballerina. Her mother eventually stuffed the outfit with rice and displayed it inside the family home.

The actress has also joined Hocus Pocus star Kathy Najimy in a Reese's campaign celebrating neighbourhoods with elaborate Halloween traditions.

headline: Qatar offers 30-day tourist visa on arrival to Pakistani travellers subject to conditions
description: Travellers must show 5,000 Qatari riyals, a return ticket, six months' valid passport & polio vaccination certificate
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Travellers must show 5,000 Qatari riyals, a return ticket, six months' valid passport & polio vaccination certificate

Pakistani nationals travelling to Qatar can obtain a 30-day tourist visa on arrival, provided they meet a set of requirements, Doha News reported on Sunday, citing the country's Ministry of Interior (MoI).

According to the ministry's website, applicants must have at least 5,000 Qatari riyals in cash or an equivalent amount available through a valid credit card to qualify for the visa.

"The applicant should hold the amount of (5000 QR) or the equivalent of a valid credit card," the ministry stated.

Visitors must also present a confirmed return ticket and hold a passport with at least six months' validity.

The ministry further specified that travellers arriving directly from Pakistan must provide a polio vaccination certificate.

"Those coming directly from Pakistan should receive a certificate of vaccination against polio," it said.

The visa is valid for 30 days and can be extended for a further 30 days, provided travellers have a confirmed return ticket before the extension is granted, according to the ministry.

Meanwhile, Pakistani nationals travelling to Qatar for business purposes can arrange visits only through accredited companies.

headline: ‘Heat’ director Michael Mann hospitalised after accidentally shooting himself at gun range
description: According to the Los Angeles Police Department, officers responded to a report of shots fired at around 4pm local time
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Filmmaker Michael Mann was taken to hospital after accidentally shooting himself in the leg at a Los Angeles gun range on Saturday, October 31.

The 83-year-old director, best known for films including Heat, Collateral and The Last of the Mohicans, suffered what his representative described as a superficial injury after a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered.

“On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered, resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann,” his spokesperson said in a statement. “He was treated and is being released.”

According to the Los Angeles Police Department, officers responded to a report of shots fired at around 4pm local time. The investigation determined that the shooting was accidental, and Mann was transported to a local hospital in stable condition.

The incident reportedly took place at The Range LA, where Mann had been practising target shooting. The director is said to have been an experienced shooter for decades.

Mann is currently developing a sequel to his acclaimed 1995 crime film Heat, which starred Al Pacino and Robert De Niro. The follow-up is expected to begin filming early next year.

The original Heat is widely regarded as one of Mann’s most influential works, known for its detailed portrayal of a Los Angeles bank robbery and its celebrated downtown shootout sequence.

Mann’s other film credits include Thief, The Last of the Mohicans, The Insider, Ali, Public Enemies and Ferrari. He also served as executive producer on the influential television series Miami Vice before directing its 2006 film adaptation.

The filmmaker has received four Academy Award nominations during his career, including for The Insider and The Aviator, and remains active in Hollywood.

headline: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ stars relive Hollywood ovation and fan chants at Tokyo Film Festival
description: Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe, who return in the sequel to Godzilla Minus One, appeared at the festival on Sunday
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
The stars of Godzilla Minus Zero have reflected on the enthusiastic reception they received at the film’s Hollywood premiere as they reunited for a special appearance at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival.

Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe, who return as Koichi Shikishima and Noriko in the sequel to Godzilla Minus One, appeared at the festival on Sunday, November 1, just days after attending the film’s premiere at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Los Angeles.

Kamiki described the response from the Hollywood audience as an unforgettable experience, with the screening receiving a standing ovation that continued throughout the 900-seat theatre.

“The energy was simply extraordinary,” Kamiki said. “Feeling that raw enthusiasm firsthand made me realize all over again just how deeply Godzilla is loved around the world. It was an invaluable experience.”

Hamabe recalled meeting audience members at the premiere’s after-party, where fans approached the cast to share their reactions. Some attendees had dressed in Godzilla-themed outfits or worn badges inspired by the iconic monster.

The actors also remembered the excitement surrounding director Takashi Yamazaki, who was met with loud chants from fans as he signed autographs.

Kamiki said the crowd’s enthusiasm went beyond simply calling out the director’s name.

“It wasn’t just a polite ‘Takashi,’” he recalled. “It was like: ‘TAKASHI! HEY, TAKASHI!’ It was roaring.”

The Tokyo event also marked the first stage appearance of child actor Sae Nagatani, who returns as Akiko Shikishima, the daughter of Koichi and Noriko.

Kamiki praised Nagatani’s performance, recalling that her character had very little dialogue in Godzilla Minus One, but was given a more substantial role in the sequel.

“We were like, ‘Really? Can she do this?’” he said. “But when we got on set, she had all her lines memorized perfectly and delivered them flawlessly.”

Hamabe said she was impressed by how much Nagatani had grown since the first film, describing her as a dependable young performer.

The sequel takes place approximately two years after the events of Godzilla Minus One, with the Shikishima family having settled into everyday life before Godzilla returns to threaten them once again.

Kamiki said he hoped audiences would imagine what the family experienced during the intervening years and see how they face the new threat together.

Godzilla Minus Zero is directed by Yamazaki and follows the success of Godzilla Minus One, which earned more than ¥7.65 billion at the Japanese box office and became the first Asian production to win the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects.

The sequel is also the first Japanese film to be certified as Filmed for IMAX.

The stars of Godzilla Minus Zero have reflected on the enthusiastic reception they received at the film’s Hollywood premiere as they reunited for a special appearance at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival.

Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe, who return as Koichi Shikishima and Noriko in the sequel to Godzilla Minus One, appeared at the festival on Sunday, November 1, just days after attending the film’s premiere at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Los Angeles.

Kamiki described the response from the Hollywood audience as an unforgettable experience, with the screening receiving a standing ovation that continued throughout the 900-seat theatre.

“The energy was simply extraordinary,” Kamiki said. “Feeling that raw enthusiasm firsthand made me realize all over again just how deeply Godzilla is loved around the world. It was an invaluable experience.”

Hamabe recalled meeting audience members at the premiere’s after-party, where fans approached the cast to share their reactions. Some attendees had dressed in Godzilla-themed outfits or worn badges inspired by the iconic monster.

The actors also remembered the excitement surrounding director Takashi Yamazaki, who was met with loud chants from fans as he signed autographs.

Kamiki said the crowd’s enthusiasm went beyond simply calling out the director’s name.

“It wasn’t just a polite ‘Takashi,’” he recalled. “It was like: ‘TAKASHI! HEY, TAKASHI!’ It was roaring.”

The Tokyo event also marked the first stage appearance of child actor Sae Nagatani, who returns as Akiko Shikishima, the daughter of Koichi and Noriko.

Kamiki praised Nagatani’s performance, recalling that her character had very little dialogue in Godzilla Minus One, but was given a more substantial role in the sequel.

“We were like, ‘Really? Can she do this?’” he said. “But when we got on set, she had all her lines memorized perfectly and delivered them flawlessly.”

Hamabe said she was impressed by how much Nagatani had grown since the first film, describing her as a dependable young performer.

The sequel takes place approximately two years after the events of Godzilla Minus One, with the Shikishima family having settled into everyday life before Godzilla returns to threaten them once again.

Kamiki said he hoped audiences would imagine what the family experienced during the intervening years and see how they face the new threat together.

headline: Bill Maher compares Donald Trump to Taylor Swift in response to president's criticism
description: Bill Maher responds to Donald Trump's criticism with Taylor Swift comparison during his latest monologue
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Bill Maher responds to Donald Trump's criticism with Taylor Swift comparison during his latest monologue

Bill Maher has responded to US President Donald Trump after the latter called the HBO host a “complete and total loser” in a lengthy post on Truth Social.

However, Maher's comeback also brought Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce and his wife, Taylor Swift, into the exchange.

The dispute followed a dinner attended by Maher, Trump and sports commentator Stephen A. Smith.

The meeting apparently prompted Trump to publish a 1,300-word rant about the Real Time host, in which he criticised Maher and described him as a “complete and total loser”.

During a recent episode of Real Time, Maher addressed Trump's comments in a monologue lasting more than four minutes.

One part of his response featured a comparison involving Swift, who is married to Kelce.

“Did you see the 1,300-word tweet he sent out? Longest ever. Kind of a flex. Eating with Trump is like dating Taylor Swift,” Maher said.

He continued, “It's a lot of laughs at the time, but later on, they're tearing you a new a______.”

headline: US judge dismisses Trump election lawsuit in Alaska
description: US judge Sharon Gleason blocks Trump's latest bid to expand federal control over state-run elections
author: Reuters
article_text:
US judge Sharon Gleason blocks Trump's latest bid to expand federal control over state-run elections

A federal judge on Sunday threw ​out a lawsuit by President Donald Trump's administration ‌seeking to block Alaska from certifying a loss by Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Tuesday's ​midterm elections if votes for a ​rival who shares his name could have ⁠changed the outcome.

The ruling by US ​District Judge Sharon Gleason in Anchorage was ​the latest blow to Trump's efforts to assert a greater federal role in elections, which under the ​US Constitution are administered by the ​states.

The race, in which Democratic former US Representative Mary ‌Peltola ⁠is challenging Sullivan, could prove critical for determining whether Trump's fellow Republicans can retain control of the Senate in the midterms.

The ​Trump administration ​has taken ⁠an increasingly aggressive approach to election oversight, pressing states for ​voter-registration data and arguing that stricter ​measures ⁠are needed to ensure public confidence in the vote. Critics, including Democratic and some ⁠Republican ​election officials, view the ​moves as federal overreach.

headline: 'SNL' pays tribute to Patrick Stewart with clip from his 1994 appearance
description: 'Saturday Night Live' honoured Patrick Stewart by revisiting his 1994 episode following actor's death at 86
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Saturday Night Live paid tribute to Patrick Stewart during its October 31 episode, honouring the late actor with an archival clip from his 1994 appearance on the NBC sketch comedy programme.

The tribute aired before the show's closing goodnights. It featured Stewart introducing musical guest Salt-N-Pepa during the episode, which originally aired in 1994. The programme also displayed a promotional photograph from his time as host.

Stewart, best known for his roles in Star Trek: The Next Generation and the X-Men films, died at the age of 86 on Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles. His wife, Sunny Ozell, was by his side, according to a statement released by his representative.

The statement confirmed that the actor had been living with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, describing his final days as a brief and poignant journey.

“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement read.

It also described how Stewart spent his final moments surrounded by family and friends.

“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” the statement continued.

The statement added that those close to him would remember his peaceful expression and the grace he displayed throughout his life.

headline: Mariah Carey launches 2026 Christmas season with new ‘It’s time’ video
description: Mariah Carey has released her 2026 ‘It’s time’ video, featuring reference to her mid-1990s music project
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Mariah Carey has officially signalled the start of the Christmas season with the release of her annual “It’s time” video, continuing a tradition associated with her hit song “All I Want for Christmas Is You”.

This year's video takes inspiration from a lesser-known part of Carey's musical history. It opens with the singer performing “Hermit”, a track from Someone’s Ugly Daughter, an album she wrote and produced during the mid-1990s.

The project was released under the band name Chick, in collaboration with her friend Clarissa Dane.

Carey also contributed backing vocals to the album but did not publicly reveal her involvement until the release of her 2020 memoir.

As “Hermit” comes to an end, the scene transitions into a winter wonderland. Carey appears dressed for the festive season as the topper on a Christmas tree.

She then sings “It’s time” in her signature whistle register, before “All I Want for Christmas Is You” begins playing.

The singer has used different concepts for her annual Christmas announcements in previous years.

Her 2025 video featured actor Billy Eichner as a disgruntled elf, while the 2024 instalment showed Carey transforming from Morticia Addams into Mrs Claus. In 2023, she appeared to defrost, while the 2022 video showed her preparing for Christmas on an exercise bike.

The annual release also arrives as Carey’s 1994 Christmas hit remains a major contender on the Billboard charts. The song previously reached 22 non-consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, setting a record for the most weeks at the top.

This year's video takes inspiration from a lesser-known part of Carey's musical history. It opens with the singer performing “Hermit”, a track from Someone’s Ugly Daughter, an album she wrote and produced during the mid-1990s.

The project was released under the band name Chick, in collaboration with her friend Clarissa Dane.

Carey also contributed backing vocals to the album but did not publicly reveal her involvement until the release of her 2020 memoir.

As “Hermit” comes to an end, the scene transitions into a winter wonderland. Carey appears dressed for the festive season as the topper on a Christmas tree.

She then sings “It’s time” in her signature whistle register, before “All I Want for Christmas Is You” begins playing.

The singer has used different concepts for her annual Christmas announcements in previous years.

Her 2025 video featured actor Billy Eichner as a disgruntled elf, while the 2024 instalment showed Carey transforming from Morticia Addams into Mrs Claus. In 2023, she appeared to defrost, while the 2022 video showed her preparing for Christmas on an exercise bike.

The annual release also arrives as Carey’s 1994 Christmas hit remains a major contender on the Billboard charts. The song previously reached 22 non-consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, setting a record for the most weeks at the top.

headline: Iran warns US of prolonged war after Trump signals more strikes
description: Iran's army spokesman says Trump will not be in a position to dictate 'timing, conditions' of a future war
author: AFP
article_text:
Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of more targets.

Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections.

“A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion,” said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television.

In the most intense phase of the war, which began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region.

Akraminia’s remarks followed Trump’s suggestion that the United States could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran.

“We still have to take care of, I would say, one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters at his Florida residence.

“You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex.

‘No geographical limitations’

Top military and political officials in Iran have warned against any new attack.

Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi on Sunday echoed a warning issued a day earlier in a written message by Iran’s new supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei.

“In a conflict with America, there are no geographical limitations; a vast theatre has been defined for inflicting damage upon the enemy,” Mohebbi said, according to state television.

The warnings came as Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei disclosed on Saturday that he had received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance seeking to revive talks.

Rezaei noted what he described as a positive change in “tone” from the US side but said he had yet to respond.

He said Tehran had previously told Washington that unless its conditions were met, “neither would the Strait of Hormuz be reopened nor would there be any negotiations”.

Those conditions include unfreezing Iranian assets abroad, ending the months-long US naval blockade of Iranian ports, lifting longstanding sanctions and ending the war on all fronts.

Since the war began, Iran has claimed control over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy conduit, and repeatedly targeted vessels attempting to cross without its authorisation.

The United States has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.

‘Braced for the worst’

Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the Emirati president, said on Sunday that the United Arab Emirates hoped the exchanges would yield a breakthrough but was preparing for the worst.

“We’re hoping that there is a diplomatic breakthrough,” he told a conference in Manama.

“It is not the interest of the region to go through another round… But I think we’re also, as we’ve shown before, braced for the worst.”

In Tehran, some residents described a sense of helplessness as threats of renewed fighting mount.

“The news coming in is truly worrying. However, no matter how much I, as an ordinary citizen, immerse myself in these reports, there is nothing I can actually do about it,” Mohadese, a 27-year-old health inspector, told AFP.

Others, including 48-year-old vendor Ebrahim, saw no reason to be concerned.

“We do not fear another war; we have been at war for 48 years now – we are always at war,” he said in downtown Tehran.

headline: Pakistan capable of intercepting any drones sent from Afghanistan, India: DG ISPR
description: Says military is incorporating AI and emerging technologies to counter evolving warfare threats, as per state media
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan is well ahead in operational readiness to counter drone threats from Afghanistan and India and has the capability to intercept any drones sent across its borders, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said, adding that the military was incorporating artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies to keep pace with the changing nature of warfare.

The remarks, made during a wide-ranging interview with an international outlet on Friday, were shared by state media on Sunday amid continuing tensions between Islamabad and Kabul.

During the interview on Friday, Lieutenant General Chaudhry said the Pakistan Army was adapting to developments in conventional and non-contact warfare, including drone operations, cyber capabilities and long-range munitions. He added that Pakistani forces had brought down dozens of sophisticated Indian drones during the previous conflict with India.

Asked whether Pakistan was concerned about the Afghan Taliban's use of drones, particularly in light of the Houthis' use of the technology against Saudi Arabia, DG ISPR said the character of warfare had changed and the military was adapting accordingly.

He stated that the army was preparing for developments in both contact and non-contact warfare, including cyber operations, drones and long-range munitions, while assessing the capabilities needed to address present and future challenges.

He added that the proliferation of non-contact warfare capabilities among non-state actors, including the Taliban, groups referred to as Khawarij and the Houthis, posed a threat to all countries. "These states will have to reconsider and re-evaluate their security architecture," he said.

Asked whether he feared a situation similar to that between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia developing between Afghanistan and Pakistan, he said Afghanistan's drone capabilities were not indigenous.

"There is no drone industry, there is no technology of that sort in Afghanistan. So it's been provided by the sponsors, the terror sponsors, because the biggest terror sponsor here is India," he said.

He alleged that the Afghan Taliban were acting as India's proxy in the context of terrorism in Pakistan.

Referring to the previous conflict with India, he said New Delhi had sent dozens of sophisticated drones, which Pakistani forces had brought down.

"So we are much ahead where we stand in our own operational readiness," he said, adding that Afghanistan could attempt to send drones but Pakistan had the capability to intercept them.

He also said Afghanistan could not absorb the retaliation Pakistan was capable of delivering.

Asked whether Pakistan's military used artificial intelligence to identify targets, as well as other emerging technologies, Lt Gen Chaudhry said the army was incorporating all technologies required to keep pace with the changing nature of warfare.

He said the rapid transformation of warfare and the pace at which new technologies were being introduced meant professional armies could not afford to fall behind.

However, he declined to discuss specific applications of artificial intelligence, quantum technology and cyber capabilities, saying he could not disclose how the military was using them.

"We use all technologies, absorbing all sorts of technologies that are essential in the changing character of war," he said.

"We are using all sorts of technologies. We are a technology-savvy army," he added.

He again alleged that the Afghan Taliban's drone capabilities had been provided by their sponsors, particularly India, arguing that Afghanistan had neither a drone industry nor technology of its own.

Lt Gen Chaudhry also described India as the "prime contractor" behind militant groups operating against Pakistan, with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) acting as its proxies.

Responding to reports that the Afghan Taliban had accused Pakistan of hosting anti-Taliban elements and coordinating former Afghan government generals and other groups opposed to the regime, he rejected the allegations and accused the Taliban of using non-state actors, militias and mercenaries to pursue their objectives.

"So that's how you play the victim card. They are apt in using non-state actors, militias, mercenaries for their objectives. So they think everyone does that," he said.

"We are a state. Afghanistan is not a state. Afghanistan is still being run by a non-state actor. It's a regime."

He said decades of foreign intervention by the Soviet Union and the United States had allowed multiple agencies and proxy groups to establish roots in Afghanistan. The country, he added, had experienced more than 40 years of foreign interventions, making its situation different from that of Pakistan and other states.

"The forces have gone physically, but still that front of Afghan Taliban is a proxy to multiple parties," he said.

He said the presence of these groups was not merely his assessment but was also reflected in United Nations reports and intelligence assessments by the United States and several other countries.

"How could so many terrorist organisations, the whole alphabet, thrive over there?" he asked.

Questioning the credibility of allegations made by the Afghan Taliban, he cited previous claims by the regime that a person picked up from a street in Kabul was a Pakistani pilot captured in Shalwar Kameez and that Pakistani tanks had been seized.

"It's the same regime which the world has seen, some day picked up a random person from the street in Kabul and said this is a Pakistani pilot that we have captured in Shalwar Kameez. It's the same regime that paraded its own tanks in the streets and said that we have captured Pakistani tanks," he said.

He said Pakistan had drawn conclusions from its experience and believed that armed groups, militias and mercenaries could not be tolerated in any state.

Asked whether isolating the Taliban would help Afghanistan, particularly amid concerns about the impact of the opium ban and reduced foreign assistance to farmers, Lt Gen Chaudhry said Pakistan was not advocating the country's isolation.

Instead, he said, the international community and regional countries should ask the Taliban authorities to act like a state and stop producing opium and supporting militant groups.

"Afghanistan is producing right now; it has only two products: terrorism and drugs. And both are not good for the world and the region and everyone," he said.

He stressed that engagement with Afghanistan was necessary and said Pakistan was also engaging with the authorities in Kabul. However, he said Islamabad demanded that Afghan territory should not be used to support terrorism inside Pakistan.

"We only ask you that don't support terrorism inside Pakistan. Stop harbouring the terrorist leaders," he said.

He alleged that militant groups operating inside Pakistan received their instructions and weapons from Afghanistan. He also claimed that Afghan citizens, including personnel of the Afghan Taliban regime, had been found among militant formations targeted by Pakistani forces.

"We ask them not to do it. If you do it, then there will be a cost, and we are capable of imposing that cost," he said, adding that Pakistan had a clear strategy for imposing such a cost.

The remarks came amid strained relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan due to recurring cross-border terrorism and security concerns. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban administration to prevent terrorist organisations, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), from using its territory to launch attacks inside Pakistan.

A day earlier, the Information Ministry maintained that the Taliban regime’s continued refusal to address terrorism was the principal barrier to normal relations and took issue with Kabul’s characterisation of the matter.

“The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad’s policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations: its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil,” the statement said.

Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.

Security officials estimate that up to 70 per cent of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.

The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan.

In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.

Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.

UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.
