article_html:
ISLAMABAD:

In a judgement that elaborates the scope of review as well as its appellate jurisdiction, the newly established Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has again asserted its superiority, stating that Supreme Court judgements are not binding on it, although they can carry "persuasive value".

"The judgments of the Supreme Court are not binding on us, but carry persuasive value and where the jurisprudence laid down by it appeals or seems to be in consonance with the law and the Constitution, may be followed," said an 8-page judgement authored by Justice Aamer Farooq.

A three-member bench led by Justice Farooq while hearing a review petition also said that Supreme Court jurisprudence evolved for leave to appeal from the decisions/orders of the high court under Article 199 of the Constitution is also not binding on it.

However, the FCC noted that it can draw wisdom from Supreme Court jurisprudence.

The judgement also noted that the crux of the jurisprudence on the subject is that the review jurisdiction of this court is quite limited and is circumscribed; being confined to the errors apparent on the face of the record or mistakes/shortcomings which would result in the miscarriage of justice.

"Recent trends show that litigants/lawyers treat review jurisdiction as another opportunity to reargue the case; by no means while hearing a review application the bench is rehearing the matter, it is only to see if there is an apparent error/mistake on the face of the record.

"Rule 4 of Order XXVII of the Rules clearly provides that the Advocate-on-Record (AOR) or the party, along with the review application shall append a certificate, in the form of a reasoned opinion, stating that, in the opinion of the AOR or the party, as the case may be, the application is maintainable and that a review is justified in accordance with the law and the practice of the court."

The order said that the party or the AOR should exercise utmost care in handing down the certificate or opining on the issue as wrong certificate can have grave repercussions.

It reiterated that the practice to file a review application as a matter of course, wherein the ground(s) for review are not attracted, does not find favour with this court and is deprecated inasmuch as mostly the review applications are nothing but a rehearing of the matter.

The FCC expected the litigants and legal community to exercise caution and file review applications only in cases where it is genuinely felt that the grounds are attracted.

"The reason we are expressing in lucid manner the caution which the party and AOR is to exercise is because of the ramifications provided in the Rules with respect to frivolous and vexatious review applications.

"In this behalf, under the Rules where the court comes to the conclusion that review application is frivolous or vexatious, it can impose costs of not less than Rupees 25,000 or the AOR can be susceptible to disciplinary proceedings, as well (Rule 5(a) of the Rules)"

Likewise, the judgement said that where there is no legal representation and the court comes to the conclusion that the application is vexatious or frivolous, the party shall be liable to costs of not less than Rs25,000.

"No application for review is to be entertained, as per Rule 6 of the Rules, unless the applicant deposits a sum of Rupees 50,000/- as security in the designated account of the court.

"Rule 6(2) empowers the court to forfeit the sum deposited as security, if the review application is dismissed or found to be frivolous or vexatious.

"Since review is an extraordinary jurisdiction in the sense that the grounds on which it can be filed are too restricted, this court, in appropriate cases, may dispose of a review application by circulation without oral hearing, unless it considers that a hearing is essential."

The court notes that the sole purpose of citing all the relevant rules pertaining to the review jurisdiction of this court is only to sensitize the litigants and the legal fraternity about its constricted scope and the consequences provided in the rules for frivolous and vexatious applications.

Regarding the concept of the jurisdiction under Article 175F(1)(c), the order said that the party has to obtain permission or leave of the court for its appeal to be heard.

"Prior to the incorporation of Article 175F(1)(c) in the Constitution through the 27th (Constitutional Amendment) Act, 2025, this jurisdiction was exercised by the Supreme Court under Article 185(3) of the Constitution.

"After the abovementioned constitutional amendment, this court was created and its appellate jurisdiction, inter alia, included hearing petitions for leave to appeal from the decisions/orders of the High Court under Article 199 of the Constitution.

"The jurisprudence which the Supreme Court of Pakistan evolved, in this regard, which is not binding on us but wisdom can be drawn from it, is that leave can only be allowed if there is any question of law in the matter or indulgence is required to prevent miscarriage of justice."

Comparing with Indian SC jurisprudence, the judgement noted that the jurisprudence evolved with respect to adjudicating the petitions for leave to appeal is perhaps different in Pakistan and definitely has parameters.

"By no means is a petition for leave to appeal an appeal as of right and only if leave is allowed then the petition acquires the status of appeal and is to be heard like one.

"When the court dismisses the application/petition for leave to appeal, it does not necessarily endorse the order against which leave is sought.

"While adjudicating a leave application, the court is not required to give reasons for its decision. If the court is of the view that no case for grant of leave is made out, it can hold so simply through a non-speaking order.

"Like-wise, while allowing leave to appeal the same can be done without a speaking order," the FCC stated.

headline: India top sponsor of terrorism: ISPR
description: India top sponsor of terrorism: ISPR
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Chief military spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has described India as the biggest sponsor of terrorism in Pakistan and alleged that the Afghan Taliban regime, the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the outlawed Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) were Indian proxies against Pakistan.

In an interview with Reuters on October 30, Lt Gen Chaudhry, the director general of the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), warned the Afghan Taliban regime that it would pay a heavy price if it failed to meet Pakistan's demands to stop supporting terrorist groups operating inside the country.

Pakistan's only demand from the Afghan Taliban was to end its support for terrorists, he said, adding that the Taliban regime was providing shelter to militant leaders and facilitating terrorist operations against Pakistan.

The DG ISPR said the Afghan Taliban used non-state actors and mercenaries to pursue its objectives, adding that Afghanistan remained under the influence of such elements.

He said several agencies and proxy groups had established roots in Afghanistan following Russian intervention in the country. International terrorist organisations, including Jaish al-Adl, Al-Qaeda and Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP), were also present there, he added.

According to him, the United Nations, the United States and several other countries had also highlighted the presence of these groups in Afghanistan.

He alleged that the Afghan Taliban regime had provided shelter to militant leaders, including Noor Wali Mehsud, Bashir Zeb and Gul Bahadur. Terrorist formations responsible for attacks in Pakistan travelled from Afghanistan and received weapons from there, he added.

The chief military spokesperson said the Afghan Taliban regime had no international credibility and urged the global community to exert pressure on it to behave like a normal state.

He also called on the international community to press the Afghan Taliban to stop the cultivation and production of narcotics, while asserting that Pakistan's armed forces were fully capable of countering all threats originating from Afghanistan, including drones.

headline: PM backs push for fairer global finance
description: PM backs push for fairer global finance
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The chairmanship of the Group of Twenty-Four (G-24) would provide Pakistan with an influential platform to advocate essential reforms in the global financial system, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Sunday, congratulating the Finance Ministry team for this "important diplomatic milestone".

Pakistan assumed the chairmanship of the G-24 on Sunday, reaffirming its commitment to strengthening the collective voice of developing economies and advancing a more responsive, fair and development-oriented international financial system.

According to a spokesperson, Shehbaz said Pakistan's election as chair of the intergovernmental group would further strengthen the country's voice and role in global economic affairs. He commended Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and his team for their tireless efforts and effective diplomacy.

He also appreciated the minister and his team for their proactive role during the annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), noting that their efforts had helped secure a prominent position for Pakistan in providing economic leadership to developing nations, the spokesperson said.

"The G-24 chairmanship will provide Pakistan with an influential platform to advocate for essential reforms in the global financial system, ensure equitable financial assistance to combat climate change, and foster sustainable development opportunities for emerging economies," Shehbaz added.

The intergovernmental group, established in 1971, is a coalition of developing countries that coordinates their positions on international monetary and financial issues, according to its website. Pakistan succeeded Nigeria as its chair.

Speaking after assuming the chairmanship, Aurangzeb called for renewed international cooperation, stronger multilateral institutions and reinforced global commitments to address climate shocks, development financing gaps and global economic fragmentation.

"The future of developing economies is not peripheral to the future of the global economy. It is central to it," Aurangzeb said, highlighting the potential of emerging and developing nations as drivers of investment, innovation, entrepreneurship and global growth.

Outlining Pakistan's agenda, he identified three strategic priorities for the chairmanship: placing development at the centre of global economic policymaking, strengthening multilateral frameworks for the collective benefit of members, and advancing a development-oriented international financial architecture.

"Our task is to ensure that the immense potential of developing economies is not constrained by an international financial architecture that has yet to fully adapt to a changing world," Finance Minister Aurangzeb said.

headline: Forces repulse cross-border attack
description: Forces repulse cross-border attack
author: News Desk
article_text:
Security forces targeted several Afghan border posts, mortar positions and installations after unprovoked firing from across the border on Pakistani positions in Angoor Adda, the deputy commissioner of South Waziristan Lower said on Sunday.

In a post on X, the deputy commissioner said that firing from the Afghan border posts targeting Pakistani border posts was continuing, prompting an immediate and effective response from Pakistani security forces.

He said the forces struck multiple Afghan positions, following which Afghan Taliban personnel were forced to abandon their posts and flee. He said that no casualties had so far been reported on the Pakistani side in the border areas, adding that Pakistani forces remained prepared to respond to any form of aggression.

Earlier on Thursday, the army had given a befitting reply to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban along the border in the Angoor Adda area, forcing the Taliban personnel to abandon their posts and flee. Several personnel of the Afghan Taliban regime were killed during the operation.

headline: Petrol pricing revised to shield consumers
description: Petrol pricing revised to shield consumers
author: Zaigham Naqvi
article_text:
The federal government has revised the petrol pricing mechanism, directing refineries to surrender the difference between import and ex-refinery prices as petroleum levy, with the resulting benefit to be passed on to consumers through a corresponding reduction in petrol prices.

The Petroleum Division issued separate notifications to the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) and oil refineries after the federal cabinet approved changes to the motor spirit (MS) pricing mechanism on October 30 to address price movements amid the continued Iran-US war.

Under the revised arrangement, petrol's import price will be determined on the basis of the actual import cost of the relevant Pakistan State Oil (PSO) cargo. If the actual import cost is unavailable for a particular day's pricing, the premium, incidentals and customs duty of the last available cargo may be used.

For the next 30 days, refineries will be entitled to an ex-refinery price calculated by fixing the premium, incidentals and customs duty at the levels applicable on March 7, 2026, before the war.

Ex-refinery price is the rate at which an oil refinery sells petroleum products to oil marketing companies before the addition of government taxes, duties, dealer commissions and other distribution costs.

Under the arrangement, the difference between the import price and the ex-refinery price will have to be surrendered by refineries under the petroleum levy head of account C03901. The resulting benefit will be passed on to petrol consumers exclusively through a corresponding reduction in the retail price.

The Petroleum Division has directed all oil refineries to deposit the differential amounts in accordance with the OGRA price and petroleum levy notifications issued from time to time. Refineries will also be required to submit daily reports of domestic petrol sales, along with computerised payment receipts and challans, to the Petroleum Division and OGRA for verification and reconciliation.

Sources said the revised formula was intended to prevent consumers from bearing the full impact of higher premiums and freight charges claimed by refineries. Passing these additional costs directly on to consumers could have resulted in a substantial increase in petrol prices.

OGRA has also directed refineries to deposit adjustments exceeding Rs49 under the revised mechanism. The prices announced on October 30 were determined under the new formula, which officials said had helped avert a major increase.

Meanwhile, speaking at a convocation on Sunday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said more than 12 to 13 million deserving people were being provided subsidised petrol at pre-war prices.

He said disruption around the Strait of Hormuz had affected countries worldwide, forcing families to make difficult choices as governments struggled to arrange foreign exchange to purchase increasingly expensive oil, gas, liquefied petroleum gas and other fuels.

Describing the crisis as unprecedented in its scale and duration, the minister said Pakistan was among the few countries to have shifted from blanket subsidies to targeted assistance supported by technology.

He said the government had avoided spending public resources on subsidising fuel for those who could afford it, including families owning expensive vehicles such as Land Cruisers, and had instead directed assistance towards people who needed it most.

The minister said the government had also ensured transparency in the fuel pricing process by making relevant information available to the public. Consumers, he added, would not need to approach him or the prime minister for relief when international oil prices declined, as the benefits of lower prices should be passed on to households.

For the next 30 days, refineries will be entitled to an ex-refinery price calculated by fixing the premium, incidentals and customs duty at the levels applicable on March 7, 2026, before the war.

Ex-refinery price is the rate at which an oil refinery sells petroleum products to oil marketing companies before the addition of government taxes, duties, dealer commissions and other distribution costs.

Under the arrangement, the difference between the import price and the ex-refinery price will have to be surrendered by refineries under the petroleum levy head of account C03901. The resulting benefit will be passed on to petrol consumers exclusively through a corresponding reduction in the retail price.

The Petroleum Division has directed all oil refineries to deposit the differential amounts in accordance with the OGRA price and petroleum levy notifications issued from time to time. Refineries will also be required to submit daily reports of domestic petrol sales, along with computerised payment receipts and challans, to the Petroleum Division and OGRA for verification and reconciliation.

Sources said the revised formula was intended to prevent consumers from bearing the full impact of higher premiums and freight charges claimed by refineries. Passing these additional costs directly on to consumers could have resulted in a substantial increase in petrol prices.

OGRA has also directed refineries to deposit adjustments exceeding Rs49 under the revised mechanism. The prices announced on October 30 were determined under the new formula, which officials said had helped avert a major increase.

Meanwhile, speaking at a convocation on Sunday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said more than 12 to 13 million deserving people were being provided subsidised petrol at pre-war prices.

He said disruption around the Strait of Hormuz had affected countries worldwide, forcing families to make difficult choices as governments struggled to arrange foreign exchange to purchase increasingly expensive oil, gas, liquefied petroleum gas and other fuels.

Describing the crisis as unprecedented in its scale and duration, the minister said Pakistan was among the few countries to have shifted from blanket subsidies to targeted assistance supported by technology.

He said the government had avoided spending public resources on subsidising fuel for those who could afford it, including families owning expensive vehicles such as Land Cruisers, and had instead directed assistance towards people who needed it most.

The minister said the government had also ensured transparency in the fuel pricing process by making relevant information available to the public. Consumers, he added, would not need to approach him or the prime minister for relief when international oil prices declined, as the benefits of lower prices should be passed on to households.

headline: Saudi strikes target Houthi 'resources'
description: Saudi strikes target Houthi 'resources'
author: agencies
article_text:
Yemen's Houthi media said on Sunday that Saudi airstrikes had targeted Hodeidah, a strategic port under Houthi control, hours after the Saudi-led coalition said it had carried out a military operation to "neutralise vital resources" used by the Houthi group to support its war effort.

The Houthi-aligned Al-Masirah TV said Saudi forces had launched two airstrikes on Ras Issa port, a major oil and fuel terminal on the Red Sea coast, approximately 55 kilometres north of Hodeidah city in Hodeidah Governorate.

Iran's state-run IRNA agency said a strike on an industrial complex in Saudi Arabia's Dammam had caused a huge fire on Sunday. "A Yemeni strike hit an industrial complex in Dammam, eastern Saudi Arabia, sparking a large fire at the facility," IRNA said in a post on X.

The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by the Houthis towards the kingdom's southern region. Residents also reported civil defence alerts warning of potential danger in Abha and Khamis Mushait for a brief period.

Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in a statement that the operation to neutralise Houthi resources had taken place in the morning, following continued Houthi attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

The coalition's joint forces command had monitored the Houthis' "continued use of vital resources to support their war effort and bolster their military capabilities, especially ballistic missiles and drones", he said. Al-Maliki did not identify the targeted locations or specify the nature of the resources.

In Geneva, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said more than 300,000 people had fled their homes in western Yemen because of intensifying fighting in the country. "Almost all were displaced in the last two months, and they urgently need shelter, food, clean water and health care," it said.

Separately, the UN human rights chief said a Yemeni staff member had died in Houthi custody after being arbitrarily detained for more than two years. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk called for an independent investigation and the release of other detained personnel.

headline: US judge dismisses Trump suit against WSJ over Epstein letter
description: US judge dismisses Trump suit against WSJ over Epstein letter
author: AFP
article_text:
A US judge on Saturday dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and media magnate Rupert Murdoch over a report that Trump sent a bawdy birthday letter to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper's story was published in July 2025 detailing the president's alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman.

Murdoch is the founder of News Corp. which owns the Wall Street Journal.

The report piled scrutiny on Trump from both Democrats and his own Republican party, who rejected the president's attempts to downplay the saga as a hoax and called for a full release of legal files on Epstein.

In Saturday's ruling, Judge Darrin Gayles dismissed Trump's lawsuit with prejudice, meaning Trump cannot file an amended version of the suit, as he did when Gayles turned down an initial version of it back in April.

The judge wrote that in bringing his defamation claim, Trump had both times failed to establish that the defendants "acted with actual malice."

The House Oversight Committee last year published a copy of Trump's alleged birthday note to Epstein, which consists of a short dialogue between "Donald" and "Jeffrey."

"We have certain things in common," says Donald, to which Jeffrey responds: "Yes, we do, come to think of it."

"Enigmas never age, have you noticed that?" asks Donald.

"As a matter of fact, it was clear to me the last time I saw you," says Jeffrey.

"A pal is a wonderful thing. Happy Birthday -- and may every day be another wonderful secret," the note ends, followed by Trump's signature, which takes the place of pubic hair on the nude outline.

Trump's supporters have been obsessed with the Epstein case for years and held as an article of faith that "deep state" elites were protecting a sex ring of Epstein associates, particularly in the Democratic Party and Hollywood.

headline: Longest truce of Ukraine war, in Kherson region, set to end
description: Longest truce of Ukraine war, in Kherson region, set to end
author: AFP
article_text:
The longest truce of the Ukraine war, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump and limited to just the Kherson region, was set to end on Sunday evening after neither side announced an extension.

The rare pause in fighting, which began early Tuesday, enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky and came as the Ukraine war grinds through its fifth year.

Neither side reported violations after the truce began, in what one Ukrainian lawmaker described as the "biggest de-escalation since 2022".

The conflict, sparked by Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion, has destroyed parts of eastern and southern Ukraine, left hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians dead, and forced millions to flee their homes.

AFP spoke to several Kherson residents, one of whom said the ceasefire had been a "breath of fresh air".

headline: A dozen children kidnapped in Nigeria
description: A dozen children kidnapped in Nigeria
author: AFP
article_text:
.

Armed men have kidnapped around a dozen children in central Nigeria, local and security sources told AFP Sunday, in the latest mass abduction in the country's troubled Niger state.

Gunmen on motorcycles seized the children on Saturday near the town of Maigujeri in Rafi district while they were returning from a farm where they had been helping their Quranic school teacher harvest maize, the sources said.

A security report seen by AFP said 18 children had been abducted, while local resident Mohammed Abdullahi said the number was closer to 12.

The kidnapping is the latest in a wave of attacks by heavily armed criminal gangs, known locally as bandits, who have intensified violent raids, abductions and cattle theft in Niger State in recent months.

headline: France probes attacks as attempted murder
description: France probes attacks as attempted murder
author: agencies
article_text:
France on Sunday launched an attempted murder probe after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during Paris protests, as footage of an officer in flames sparked outrage.

On Saturday, clashes erupted in Paris and other cities after hundreds of thousands of people staged a third weekend of protests against soaring living costs.

Separately, in Zurich and Basel, Switzerland, hundreds of people took to the streets, joining demonstrations inspired by the youth-led protest movement in France. The gatherings, held under the slogan "We've had enough – in Switzerland too", turned violent in both cities, prompting police to intervene. The demonstrations were unauthorised. According to reports, two young men were arrested.

The Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail.

While riots were less widespread than two weeks ago, when France experienced some of its worst unrest in years, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Saturday that the level of violence perpetrated by some was "extraordinary".

Dramatic images, including AFP photos and video, showed a

homemade incendiary device exploding at the feet of a security officer in protective gear, engulfing his lower body in flames.

Prosecutors that said an investigation had been opened for "attempted murder of persons vested with public authority".

"Explosive devices were thrown at around 15 gendarmes as well as police officers," the prosecutor's office said.

Gendarmes are military police officers who are part of the French armed forces.

An assessment of the injured was ongoing, prosecutors said, adding that the reported injuries included second-degree burns.

The gendarme struck by the Molotov cocktail said his unit was "under assault", with glass bottles, paving stones, shards of glass, and firebombs thrown at them.

"We were hit by several significant incendiary devices," he told broadcaster RTL on condition of anonymity.

"The flammable substance was so greasy that I could feel it spreading across my skin," he said. "I kept wondering when it would stop because I really felt as though I had been coated by the heat itself."

The officer, who received minor injuries, said the leg and shin protections on his riot uniform melted.

After watching the footage of the firebomb attack that injured him, he said he was surprised by "the intensity" of the incident. The video made him realise "that we may also have come close to a catastrophe".

His unit had been on leave but was recalled ahead of the protests.

headline: N Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads
description: N Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads
author: AFP
article_text:
.

North Korea test-fired cluster-bomb warheads, its state media reported Sunday, the latest in a slew of weapons drills aimed at training its military units on using them.

The test, conducted on Saturday, came after the nuclear-armed North recently trialled a range of weaponry including attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.

It also came against the backdrop of growing tensions over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border between the two Koreas that saw three South Korean soldiers wounded.

The North has denied responsibility and vowed to further fortify its border areas and resume its loudspeaker campaign.

Saturday's test was conducted to "assess adaptation to combat and power of a cluster-bomb warhead to be tipped on tactical ballistic missiles", the official Korean Central News Agency reported Sunday.

Officials said it confirmed the weapon "is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 12 to 13 hectares with its highest-density power".

headline: UK king to address Commonwealth on slavery with 'honesty'
description: UK king to address Commonwealth on slavery with 'honesty'
author: AFP
article_text:
King Charles III will confront "shameful aspects" of UK history with "unflinching honesty" when he addresses Commonwealth leaders next week, Buckingham Palace said Saturday, amid renewed scrutiny of Britain's role in historical transatlantic slavery.

The comments come after Prime Minister Andy Burnham revealed he was open to the UK formally apologising for its role in the trade, but ruling out paying the financial reparations demanded by some Caribbean countries.

The issues have resurfaced as Charles tours the Caribbean before delivering a speech Tuesday at the Commonwealth heads of government meeting

there, which Burnham is also set to attend.

"The King will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit," a palace spokesperson said.

"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue."

The palace noted the monarch, who arrived in Antigua and Barbuda late Friday ahead of the summit there, will be speaking in his role as head of the 56-member Commonwealth, composed mainly of former British colonies.

"It would not be appropriate for him to address matters of particular policy relating to the UK government's position," the spokesperson said.

They added that the king will "primarily focus on encouraging practical solutions and united efforts to address global challenges and opportunities".

Under pressure from Commonwealth countries over Britain's pivotal part in transatlantic slavery, Burnham penned a newspaper op-ed published earlier Saturday that argued: "We need to face up to the past." UK king to address Commonwealth on slavery with 'honesty'.

headline: Israeli strikes kill eight people in Gaza
description: Israeli strikes kill eight people in Gaza
author: Reuters
article_text:
Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians, including five police officers, in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Sunday, according to medics and the Hamas-run interior ministry.

Medics said three people were killed in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza City. The interior ministry said the five police officers were killed in another strike in western Khan Younis, in the south of the enclave.

The Israeli military said it struck several militants in Khan Younis, without giving further information. It did not immediately comment on the Gaza City strike.

Israel, which says Hamas has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of a year-old ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks.

Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal.

Last year's US-brokered ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made as negotiators have failed to agree on terms for Hamas to disarm or Israel to withdraw its troops, who control about two-thirds of the territory where they have ordered residents out.

Nearly all of the more than 2 million residents live in the remaining third of the enclave among war ruins, mostly in makeshift tents and damaged buildings, still under effective control of Hamas.

At least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire, according to the territory's health officials, while Israel says four soldiers have been killed.

Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on October 7, 2023.

headline: Drone-based smoke monitoring fails
description: Drone-based smoke monitoring fails
author: Qaiser Shirazi
article_text:
With the onset of the smog season, air pollution levels have reached alarming proportions in Rawalpindi, Islamabad and five major cities of Punjab.

The Air Quality Index (AQI) of Murree, the province's largest tourist destination, has also crossed the dangerous threshold.

Due to record air pollution, Lahore, the provincial capital, has been included among the world's most polluted cities. The provincial government has decided to keep brick kilns across Punjab completely closed from November 15 to December 15. The drone-based system for monitoring smoke emissions has also proved unsuccessful.

The word "smog" is a combination of two English words, smoke and fog. It refers to a thick, toxic layer formed when poisonous gases, smoke, dust and fog mix in the atmosphere.

According to a survey by the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department, Lahore's overall AQI has crossed 253, while the index in several areas of the city has exceeded 419. Nankana Sahib has recorded an extremely dangerous AQI of 371, Faisalabad 290, Rawalpindi 185 and Islamabad between 170 and 172.

The AQI in Murree has crossed 129, while Gujranwala has recorded 255 and Multan 296. The index stands at 116 in Attock, 104 in Chakwal, 156 in Jhelum and has reached 289 in Narowal.

Air pollution has triggered various ailments, including problems affecting the nose, ears and throat, as well as eye irritation. Doctors have advised citizens to wear protective masks to guard against smog and recommended consuming herbal drinks, soups, broth and tea during the season.

The burning of rice crop residues in Nankana Sahib and Gujranwala has also contributed to rising pollution levels. According to the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department, the smog season lasts from October to December.

Air pollution is increasing due to smoke-emitting vehicles, heavy black smoke from railway engines, factories and industrial units, the burning of scrap and garbage, and particularly emissions from brick kilns and stone-crushing plants.

Burning old and unserviceable vehicle tyres and plastic to extract black oil is also contributing to the problem.

Operations against smoke-emitting vehicles, scrap, garbage, tyres and the burning of crop residues have failed to produce the desired results. Despite challans and fines, the problem cannot be controlled unless these materials are disposed of through scientific methods, officials said.

Rawalpindi Deputy Commissioner Nadeem Nasir has ordered action, registration of FIRs and heavy fines against smoke-emitting vehicles, factories, industrial units, brick kilns, stone-crushing plants and those involved in burning tyres and garbage across the district.

The Regional Transport Authority secretary said 49 smoke-emitting vehicles had been impounded and fines amounting to Rs600,000 imposed.

A spokesperson for the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department said 21 brick kilns and five stone-crushing plants emitting smoke had been sealed.

Meanwhile, officials of the relevant departments have started praying for heavy rainfall to control smog. The Agriculture Department will arrange Salat-i-Istisqa (prayer for rain) next Friday.

Due to record air pollution, Lahore, the provincial capital, has been included among the world's most polluted cities. The provincial government has decided to keep brick kilns across Punjab completely closed from November 15 to December 15. The drone-based system for monitoring smoke emissions has also proved unsuccessful.

The word "smog" is a combination of two English words, smoke and fog. It refers to a thick, toxic layer formed when poisonous gases, smoke, dust and fog mix in the atmosphere.

According to a survey by the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department, Lahore's overall AQI has crossed 253, while the index in several areas of the city has exceeded 419. Nankana Sahib has recorded an extremely dangerous AQI of 371, Faisalabad 290, Rawalpindi 185 and Islamabad between 170 and 172.

The AQI in Murree has crossed 129, while Gujranwala has recorded 255 and Multan 296. The index stands at 116 in Attock, 104 in Chakwal, 156 in Jhelum and has reached 289 in Narowal.

Air pollution has triggered various ailments, including problems affecting the nose, ears and throat, as well as eye irritation. Doctors have advised citizens to wear protective masks to guard against smog and recommended consuming herbal drinks, soups, broth and tea during the season.

The burning of rice crop residues in Nankana Sahib and Gujranwala has also contributed to rising pollution levels. According to the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department, the smog season lasts from October to December.

Air pollution is increasing due to smoke-emitting vehicles, heavy black smoke from railway engines, factories and industrial units, the burning of scrap and garbage, and particularly emissions from brick kilns and stone-crushing plants.

Burning old and unserviceable vehicle tyres and plastic to extract black oil is also contributing to the problem.

Operations against smoke-emitting vehicles, scrap, garbage, tyres and the burning of crop residues have failed to produce the desired results. Despite challans and fines, the problem cannot be controlled unless these materials are disposed of through scientific methods, officials said.

Rawalpindi Deputy Commissioner Nadeem Nasir has ordered action, registration of FIRs and heavy fines against smoke-emitting vehicles, factories, industrial units, brick kilns, stone-crushing plants and those involved in burning tyres and garbage across the district.

The Regional Transport Authority secretary said 49 smoke-emitting vehicles had been impounded and fines amounting to Rs600,000 imposed.

A spokesperson for the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department said 21 brick kilns and five stone-crushing plants emitting smoke had been sealed.

Meanwhile, officials of the relevant departments have started praying for heavy rainfall to control smog. The Agriculture Department will arrange Salat-i-Istisqa (prayer for rain) next Friday.

headline: Fuel costs drive up school van fares
description: Fuel costs drive up school van fares
author: APP
article_text:
Following the recent surge in petrol prices linked to Middle East tensions, school van and private transport owners in the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad have unilaterally increased monthly fares by up to 40 per cent, putting an extra financial burden on parents. Parents alleged that van owners are demanding Rs2,000 to Rs4,000 extra per month without any regulatory check, despite most schools being located within a three to five kilometre radius.

A mother of two, Sidra said "My children go to a school in F-7, just 10 minutes away from our home in G-10, but the van driver has increased the fee from Rs6000 to Rs8,000, citing petrol hike."

She said even though the government is giving a petrol subsidy for 800cc vehicles, there is no justification for them to charge so much.

We are already paying heavy school fees. This additional transport cost is unbearable for a middle-class family, she added.

Another parent Abdul Hanan stated that "They are using the petrol hike as an excuse. They charge full fee even during summer and winter vacations and there is no one to ask them."

On the other hand, van owners defended the increase, calling it unavoidable. "Beside petrol, we have to pay for CNG, maintenance, and traffic challans. How can we operate in old fares? If we don't increase, we will have to park the vans," a van owner said.

headline: F-9 Park gala celebrates women-led businesses
description: F-9 Park gala celebrates women-led businesses
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
More than 200 women-owned businesses will showcase locally made Pakistani products at Islamabad Women Gala 2026, scheduled to be held at F-9 Park on November 07 and 08, featuring the nostalgic theme "Mere Bachpan Ke Din" alongside a range of family entertainment and cultural activities.

Organised by Let's Grow Together, the two-day festival will be providing a platform for women entrepreneurs to promote their businesses, display their products and contribute to the promotion of Made in Pakistan goods.

This year's theme, "Mere Bachpan Ke Din," will celebrate the memories and spirit of the 1980s and 1990s through traditional games, nostalgic settings, music, interactive activities and specially designed spaces, allowing visitors to revisit the experiences of their childhood.

The gala will feature more than 200 stalls run by women entrepreneurs, showcasing a variety of locally made products.

Dedicated stalls for children and student entrepreneurs will also provide young participants with opportunities to display their products, creativity and business ideas.

Visitors will have access to a food court offering diverse flavours, activity stalls and interactive experiences, while a kids' carnival and a dedicated Kids Arena will provide entertainment and recreational activities for younger visitors.

A special 80s and 90s Theme Arena, photo booths and live music will further enhance the nostalgic atmosphere, offering families opportunities to enjoy entertainment and capture memorable moments.

A dedicated Lok Artisan Arena will feature skilled artisans demonstrating traditional crafts and handmade work, highlighting Pakistan's rich cultural heritage, indigenous skills and craftsmanship.

The festival is designed as a family-oriented event, with male family members also welcome to attend alongside their families. It will combine shopping, food, cultural activities and entertainment in an environment that brings together entrepreneurs, artisans and visitors of different age groups.

headline: Adiala inmates complain of food restrictions
description: Adiala inmates complain of food restrictions
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Male and female prisoners brought daily from Central Jail Adiala to the Judicial Complex and District Courts for hearings have complained that facilities inside the jail are being curtailed.

They said restrictions had now been imposed on bringing tomatoes, spices, rice, lentils, packaged milk and juices from home.

According to the prisoners, the curry served in jail consists almost entirely of watery gravy, with two small potatoes and a bowl of bland broth. They used to bring tomatoes and spices from home to improve its taste, but these items had also been banned.

Packaged milk and juices are available inside the jail at three times their market price, they claimed, adding that no change was returned after payments. They said they had previously obtained packaged milk, juices and tomatoes from their homes, but this facility had now been discontinued.

They further complained that women prisoners accompanied by one or two young children were not provided food for the children.

Only one piece of bread was given to the mother, forcing her either to remain hungry or to ask other, better-off female prisoners for some of their bread.

Relatives of the prisoners, including Riaz Ali, Faisal Khan and Azhar Ali, demanded that facilities be improved for inmates.

headline: Buddhist sites captivate visitors
description: Buddhist sites captivate visitors
author: SHOAIB SABZWARI
article_text:
Danish Ambassador Maja Mortensen, accompanied by a delegation, visited the Taxila Museum, the Unesco World Heritage Site of Julian Stupa and Bhamala Stupa and hailed Gandhara Civilisation as one of finest civilisations in histroy.

During the visit, the delegation was given a detailed briefing on the Gandhara civilisation, the history of Buddhism and the religious, cultural and historical significance of the Julian and Bhamala stupas.

The delegation was informed that these historical sites in Taxila and its surrounding areas represented a great civilisation spanning several centuries and had played a prominent role in the spread of Buddhism, religious teachings, architecture and sculpture.

Danish Ambassador Maja Mortensen and members of her delegation expressed particular interest in Buddhist statues, ancient artefacts, masterpieces of stone carving and historical structures.

They also sought information about the ancient educational and religious system of the Julian monastery and the distinctive architectural features of Bhamala Stupa.

On the occasion, the delegation was informed that the Gandhara region had been an important centre for Buddhist education and preaching in the past.

The stupas, monasteries, Buddhist statues and other archaeological remains found in the area provided clear evidence of the religious, intellectual and artistic development of that era.

Officials of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Archaeology Department also briefed the delegation on measures being taken to protect, maintain and restore the historical sites.

They said the department was fulfilling its responsibilities through regular monitoring of the sites, protection and documentation of archaeological remains, and efforts to preserve their original historical significance so that this valuable heritage could be safely passed on to future generations.

During the visit, the delegation was given a detailed briefing on the Gandhara civilisation, the history of Buddhism and the religious, cultural and historical significance of the Julian and Bhamala stupas.

The delegation was informed that these historical sites in Taxila and its surrounding areas represented a great civilisation spanning several centuries and had played a prominent role in the spread of Buddhism, religious teachings, architecture and sculpture.

Danish Ambassador Maja Mortensen and members of her delegation expressed particular interest in Buddhist statues, ancient artefacts, masterpieces of stone carving and historical structures.

They also sought information about the ancient educational and religious system of the Julian monastery and the distinctive architectural features of Bhamala Stupa.

On the occasion, the delegation was informed that the Gandhara region had been an important centre for Buddhist education and preaching in the past.

The stupas, monasteries, Buddhist statues and other archaeological remains found in the area provided clear evidence of the religious, intellectual and artistic development of that era.

Officials of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Archaeology Department also briefed the delegation on measures being taken to protect, maintain and restore the historical sites.

They said the department was fulfilling its responsibilities through regular monitoring of the sites, protection and documentation of archaeological remains, and efforts to preserve their original historical significance so that this valuable heritage could be safely passed on to future generations.

headline: Murree rolls out winter safety plan for tourists
description: Murree rolls out winter safety plan for tourists
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The district administration, National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and Rescue 1122 have finalised an extensive winter tourism safety and disaster management plan for Murree to protect tourists and prevent any untoward incidents during the snowfall season.

The plan, titled 'Mission Safe Winter', has been activated following the first snowfall in the Galiyat region, with the official winter tourism season scheduled to run from December 15 to February 15. The administration has put comprehensive arrangements in place to ensure uninterrupted traffic flow and the safety of visitors during heavy snowfall.

Under the plan, 19 tourist facilitation centres have been established at various locations across Murree, Galiyat and the routes connecting Rawalpindi, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Azad Kashmir. These centres will provide immediate assistance and guidance to tourists during emergencies.

Round-the-clock surveillance of Murree's roads and entry points is being maintained through 181 high-tech Safe City cameras and thermal drones. A special Pakistan Army contingent will also remain deployed for continuous monitoring.

The Health Department has been directed to ensure the 24-hour availability of doctors and medicines at hospitals. Meanwhile, the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (PERA) will monitor hotels and petrol stations to prevent overcharging, profiteering and violations of officially prescribed rates. Uniform fare schedules and standardised food prices will also be enforced.

To keep roads clear during snowfall, more than 20 modern snow-clearing vehicles, cranes and loaders have been positioned at key locations. New Rescue 1122 stations have been made operational, while an air ambulance strip along the Murree Expressway has also been proposed to facilitate aerial assistance during serious emergencies.

headline: Teachers stretched thin by school events
description: Teachers stretched thin by school events
author: APP
article_text:
The teachers of leading private schools in the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad are under severe stress as their workload of non-academic and extracurricular activities has increased manifold, relegating their primary task of teaching to the background.

From daily themed activities like colour day, mango day, welcome parties, to week-long preparations for annual functions, sports galas and social media content creation, teachers say they are forced to work beyond their job descriptions without any extra compensation.

Many teachers believe these activities are now being used as a marketing strategy to attract admissions, while the entire burden is placed on the teaching staff.

A female teacher Noshaba at a prominent private school said "we were appointed to teach, but most of our time is now consumed by classroom decoration, event management, dance rehearsals and making videos for school pages."

She stated that they have to stay after school hours for preparations. If parents complain about a single picture, the management holds them responsible.

She remarked that earlier, competition among schools was based on academic results. Now it is based on who organises more colourful functions. In this race, real education is suffering.

headline: Cop surrenders in ATI employee's murder case
description: Cop surrenders in ATI employee's murder case
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Police Sub-Inspector Ahsan Khan, a key accused in the murder of Sardar Arif, a supervisor at Ayub Teaching Institution (ATI), surrendered before an additional sessions judge and was taken into custody by a heavy police contingent.

The hearing was scheduled before Additional Sessions Judge VI Asfandyar Yousafzai in connection with the proceedings on his pre-arrest bail application. Ahsan Khan, who had been suspended following the incident, appeared in court to surrender.

Strict security arrangements were in place during the proceedings. The victim's father expressed satisfaction over the arrest of the key accused.

Another accused, SHO Gunner Hamza Khan, has obtained interim pre-arrest bail but did not appear before the court after securing protective bail for travel. No arguments were exchanged between the lawyers during Saturday's proceedings following Ahsan Khan's surrender.

On October 5, Sardar Arif was allegedly shot dead in broad daylight following a dispute involving an Afghan neighbour. According to the case, Sub-Inspector Ahsan Khan, Gunner Hamza Khan and other suspects entered the victim's house and opened indiscriminate fire in front of his wife and child.

headline: Three cops booked for custodial death
description: Three cops booked for custodial death
author: Saleh Mughal
article_text:
A murder case was registered on Sunday against an assistant sub-inspector (ASI) and two constables of Taxila Police Station over the alleged torture and death of a man at Gangu check-post in Rawalpindi district.

The case was registered under Sections 302 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) on the complaint of the deceased's younger brother, Zahid Khan, who accused ASI Kashif and constables Sohail and Qadeer of subjecting his brother Akmal Ali Khan to brutal torture and deliberately killing him. Police officials said an investigation had been launched.

Meanwhile, video footage from inside the police check-post emerged, showing Akmal lying on a charpoy in a distressed and critical condition. The footage also shows police personnel filming visitors to the check-post, while a person could be heard urging them to give the injured man water. Another voice appears to object, saying that water should not be given to him and that the responsibility should instead be placed on the police personnel.

According to the complainant, his brother had gone to have his vehicle refuelled with compressed natural gas (CNG) when police personnel stopped him at Gangu check-post.

Zahid stated that Akmal called a resident of Dargahi, Farrukh Amir Khan, and informed him that personnel from Taxila Police Station had detained him at the check-post. Farrukh subsequently told the complainant that Mukhtar Khan was also with him at the time.

The three men then reached the check-post, where they allegedly saw police personnel assaulting Akmal inside a room. The complainant claimed that his brother was lying on the floor and pleading with the officers to spare him.

He said they repeatedly appealed to the police personnel to release Akmal, but their requests were ignored. According to the complaint, ASI Kashif instructed constables Sohail and Qadeer to beat Akmal, following which all three allegedly subjected him to further violence, punching and kicking him.

Zahid alleged that the officers eventually let his injured brother go after the assault. The three men took Akmal to the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital in Taxila, where a doctor examined him and declared him dead.

The complainant accused the three police personnel of abusing their authority and deliberately killing his brother. He called for legal action, the strictest possible punishment for the accused and justice for his family. He also sought the return of his vehicle documents, which he alleged had been taken by the police.

Separately, reports suggest that the incident stemmed from a minor dispute after a truck and Akmal's vehicle came face to face on the road, blocking the passage. The dispute reportedly escalated after Akmal's vehicle was removed and the truck driver left the scene, leading to a confrontation between Akmal and the police personnel.

The incident also triggered an angry protest during which demonstrators allegedly subjected police personnel to severe violence. A police officer was injured and is receiving treatment at a hospital.

article_html:
RAWALPINDI:

A murder case was registered on Sunday against an assistant sub-inspector (ASI) and two constables of Taxila Police Station over the alleged torture and death of a man at Gangu check-post in Rawalpindi district.

The case was registered under Sections 302 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) on the complaint of the deceased's younger brother, Zahid Khan, who accused ASI Kashif and constables Sohail and Qadeer of subjecting his brother Akmal Ali Khan to brutal torture and deliberately killing him. Police officials said an investigation had been launched.

Meanwhile, video footage from inside the police check-post emerged, showing Akmal lying on a charpoy in a distressed and critical condition. The footage also shows police personnel filming visitors to the check-post, while a person could be heard urging them to give the injured man water. Another voice appears to object, saying that water should not be given to him and that the responsibility should instead be placed on the police personnel.

According to the complainant, his brother had gone to have his vehicle refuelled with compressed natural gas (CNG) when police personnel stopped him at Gangu check-post.

Zahid stated that Akmal called a resident of Dargahi, Farrukh Amir Khan, and informed him that personnel from Taxila Police Station had detained him at the check-post. Farrukh subsequently told the complainant that Mukhtar Khan was also with him at the time.

The three men then reached the check-post, where they allegedly saw police personnel assaulting Akmal inside a room. The complainant claimed that his brother was lying on the floor and pleading with the officers to spare him.

He said they repeatedly appealed to the police personnel to release Akmal, but their requests were ignored. According to the complaint, ASI Kashif instructed constables Sohail and Qadeer to beat Akmal, following which all three allegedly subjected him to further violence, punching and kicking him.

Zahid alleged that the officers eventually let his injured brother go after the assault. The three men took Akmal to the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital in Taxila, where a doctor examined him and declared him dead.

The complainant accused the three police personnel of abusing their authority and deliberately killing his brother. He called for legal action, the strictest possible punishment for the accused and justice for his family. He also sought the return of his vehicle documents, which he alleged had been taken by the police.

Separately, reports suggest that the incident stemmed from a minor dispute after a truck and Akmal's vehicle came face to face on the road, blocking the passage. The dispute reportedly escalated after Akmal's vehicle was removed and the truck driver left the scene, leading to a confrontation between Akmal and the police personnel.

The incident also triggered an angry protest during which demonstrators allegedly subjected police personnel to severe violence. A police officer was injured and is receiving treatment at a hospital.

Police authorities are conducting a high-level inquiry into the incident and have obtained CCTV footage from the surrounding area as part of the investigation.

headline: MQM-P sounds marching call for new provinces
description: MQM-P sounds marching call for new provinces
author: Naeem Khanzada
article_text:
The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) on Sunday announced a nationwide movement for the creation of new provinces, with party Chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui declaring that a major rally would be staged towards Sharae Faisal on November 29.

Addressing a general workers' meeting at PIB Colony, Siddiqui said urban Sindh had the strongest case for a separate province and that the MQM-Pakistan would lead the campaign to secure the rights of the people.

"New provinces should be created wherever there is a demand and a need based on population," he said, adding that the time had come for people to take to the streets to achieve their rights.

Responding to questions about the proposed province's geographical boundaries, Siddiqui said the migrants had brought their share of land with them when they migrated to Pakistan after sacrificing their properties in India. He also claimed that properties left behind by non-Muslims in Pakistan legally belonged to the migrants.

Announcing the November 29 march, he said an MQM-Pakistan convoy would head towards Sharae Faisal, claiming that all routes leading to the main artery would be blocked once the procession set off. "People across Pakistan are looking towards MQM and telling us to move forward, assuring us of their support," he said.

Siddiqui warned those opposing the demand for new provinces against threatening his party, saying the MQM-Pakistan was prepared to confront resistance. Recalling the September 30, 1986 violence in Hyderabad, the Sohrab Goth incident and the Qasba-Aligarh tragedy, he said the movement had survived numerous challenges and would continue.

MQM-Pakistan leader Wasim Akhtar said the meeting comprised workers from District East alone and did not represent the entire city. "Bilawal should come and see that these are only workers from District East, not the entire Karachi," he said, claiming that the city was increasingly aligning itself with the MQM and that the slogan emerging from Karachi would reach Islamabad.

Dr Farooq Sattar said the MQM-P struggle concerned 260m people across Pakistan who, he alleged, continued to face injustice. He said the 18th Constitutional Amendment had failed to improve the country's economic growth, while education and healthcare facilities remained inadequate, roads were in poor condition and even basic municipal services such as garbage collection were lacking.

headline: Sharjeel lashes out over roadblock remarks
description: Sharjeel lashes out over roadblock remarks
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

Reacting to the statements of MQM-P leaders, Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon has said though the difference of opinion is every party's right, the era of holding citizens hostage is over.

In a statement, he said threatening to block Shahrah-e-Bhutto and Sharae Faisal and stopping people from passing is not democratic but a terrorist-like behaviour.

Sharjeel said it is ironic to talk about division in the name of democracy and then lament the fruits of the same democracy.

He said the Sindh Assembly has already given its stance on provinces through a resolution, and administrative units in the form of divisions already exist, calling MQM's demand childish. He said MQM's demand for new administrative units is an attempt to create political ambiguity and no political party has the right to block public roads.

headline: Temperature swings may affect health
description: Temperature swings may affect health
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
'Mercury likely to range between 21°C and 37°C over next three days'

As the metropolis gradually transitions towards winter, sharp fluctuations between daytime and nighttime temperatures are expected to create contrasting weather conditions, potentially affecting human health and the well-being of domestic animals, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has warned.

In its three-day weather forecast, the Met Office's Early Warning Centre said the considerable difference between daytime and nighttime temperatures could pose health risks, urging people to remain cautious amid changing weather conditions.

The PMD said Karachi would continue to experience the influence of sea breezes, alongside north-easterly and north-westerly winds originating from Balochistan and Tharparkar.

The minimum temperature in the city is expected to hover around 21 degrees Celsius over the next three days, while the maximum could climb to 37°C, indicating relatively hot afternoons despite the seasonal transition.

Meanwhile, central and upper parts of Sindh are likely to experience dry weather, with relatively cooler nights. Southern parts of the province, however, are expected to remain hot and dry.

According to the Met Office, Karachi recorded a maximum temperature of 35.3°C on Sunday, down 1.7 degrees from the previous day. The relative humidity stood at 29 per cent.

headline: PPP threatens to lay siege to KE, SSGC offices
description: PPP threatens to lay siege to KE, SSGC offices
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

With prolonged power and gas outages bringing daily life in Lyari to a grinding halt, the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) on Sunday staged a protest rally from Lyari Gate, Musa Lane, to the Karachi Press Club, warning of a siege of K-Electric and Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) offices if the crisis was not resolved.

The rally, organised by PPP District South, was attended by party leaders and local residents protesting against up to 18 hours of unannounced electricity and gas outages in the neighbourhood. PPP MNA Sardar Nabil Gabol urged Sindh CM to wield his authority and crack down on unannounced load-shedding. He said he had taken up the matter with KE, pointing out that residents had consistently paid their electricity bills but were still being denied power.

headline: Roadwork delay leads to traffic nightmare
description: Roadwork delay leads to traffic nightmare
author: Syed Ashraf Ali
article_text:
A road improvement project that has yet to get off the ground has turned Church Mor in Gulshan-e-Iqbal's block 13-D/2 into a traffic bottleneck, with construction material lying unattended at the narrow junction for the past three weeks.

Residents have blamed the town administration for poor planning, arguing that the construction material should have been dumped along the much wider Church Road, where the proposed roadwork is to be carried out, rather than at the already congested junction. The haphazard placement of the material has severely restricted traffic movement, resulting in persistent traffic jams and making passage difficult for pedestrians.

According to residents, repeated complaints have been lodged with both the relevant union council and town administrations, urging them either to begin construction work without further delay or remove the material from the junction. However, they said, the only action taken so far was the removal of some pipes that had been lying there for nearly six months, while the road construction material remains untouched.

Residents also pointed out that St Philip's High School is situated close to Church Mor, forcing schoolchildren to negotiate the congested junction on foot. The spot is also an important thoroughfare for neighbourhood residents, many of whom face considerable difficulty navigating the area on foot.

They urged the authorities to remove the material immediately and ensure that the long-awaited roadwork is started without further delay.

headline: Airline engineer shot dead in Karachi
description: Airline engineer shot dead in Karachi
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
54-year-old victim was out to buy bread when assailant opened fire

A routine trip to buy bread turned fatal for a Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) engineer, who was shot dead by an unidentified motorcycle-riding assailant in Gulistan-e-Jauhar on Sunday.

The 54-year-old victim, identified as Imtiaz Ahmed, was crossing a road when the armed attacker opened fire before speeding away. Police said the killing did not appear to be a robbery-related incident, as the victim's belongings were found intact.

According to police, Imtiaz was father of four children. His wife and daughters are currently residing in Germany. The victim sustained a bullet wound near his ribs, close to the arm, which proved fatal. Three bullets also struck a vehicle parked nearby.

Police obtained CCTV footage showing Imtiaz briskly crossing the road before collapsing near a vehicle. People in the vicinity can be seen fleeing for safety as gunshots ring out. Seconds later, a motorcyclist is seen speeding away from the scene.

headline: Two children crushed to death
description: Two children crushed to death
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Third child critically injured; driver held, police say the three minors were riding one bike

Two schoolchildren were killed and another critically injured when a tractor-trolley struck their motorcycle near the Mayor's Secretariat on Thandi Sarak in Hyderabad on Sunday.

According to police, the accident occurred the GOR police station when the tractor-trolley hit the motorcycle, throwing its occupants onto the road and bringing them under the wheels of the heavy vehicle.

The deceased were identified as Rayan, son of Ashiq Hussain Chandio, and Faheem, son of Saleem Chandio, while the injured child was identified as Azaan, son of Muhammad Shafi Chandio. Police said the three children, aged between nine and 13, were travelling on a single motorcycle, which was being driven by one of the minors. Faheem and Rayan were students of fourth and fifth grades, respectively, while Azaan was studying in eighth grade. Police arrested the tractor-trolley driver, identified as Jahanzeb Kandhro, and impounded the vehicle following the accident.

The injured child and bodies of the deceased were shifted to Civil Hospital Hyderabad, where the bodies were handed over to their families.

headline: Stray cattle add to Hyderabad's urban woes
description: Stray cattle add to Hyderabad's urban woes
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Already struggling with stray dogs, Hyderabad residents are now facing another menace as stray cattle roam busy roads, disrupting traffic and causing accidents, while municipal authorities have failed to sustain efforts to remove them.

The animals are frequently spotted across Latifabad, Badin General Bus StopAutobhan Road, Unit 8 and 12 routes, Khuda Hafiz Chowk and adjoining roads near Mazdoor Chowk. Residents say the animals often dart onto roads unexpectedly, forcing motorists, particularly motorcyclists, to brake suddenly, skid or collide with them. Traffic movement is also disrupted where cattle gather around garbage dumps in search of food.

Many of the animals appear malnourished, with visible wounds and insects attached to their bodies. Garbage heaps containing rotten fruit and vegetables, particularly near the Unit 12 fruit and vegetable market, have become their regular feeding grounds.

Municipal sources said that although the animals appeared ownerless, their owners often emerged when authorities attempted to impound them.

headline: Nehr-e-Khayyam in the line of fire
description: Nehr-e-Khayyam in the line of fire
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Opposition to the ongoing Nehr-e-Khayyam project gathered momentum on Sunday as Clifton Block 5 residents were joined by environmental activists, legal professionals and political representatives, demanding an immediate halt to construction until environmental approvals, technical studies and project details are made public.

The protest, part of the residents' continuing Sunday campaign, saw participants rally around concerns that the project could compromise the historic waterway's drainage capacity, increase urban flooding risks and pave the way for encroachment on public land.

The programme began with a Baithak at Karachi Urban Forest, followed by a walk to Nehr-e-Khayyam, where participants observed that construction work was continuing despite mounting objections from the neighbourhood.

Protesters maintained that work should not have commenced before completion of the mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), approval from the Sindh Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) and relevant technical studies. They demanded that all such documents be disclosed for public scrutiny.

Lawyer and Clifton resident Ahmer Jamil Khan stressed the need to involve local communities in decisions affecting their neighbourhoods. He also discussed possible legal avenues and called for sustainable solutions to Karachi's sewage and wastewater problems, including properly planned treatment plants and effective wastewater management.

Residents Rasha Tarek and Nusrat Khwaja warned that narrowing Nehr-e-Khayyam could undermine its drainage capacity and expose surrounding neighbourhoods to greater flooding risks during heavy rainfall. They called for hydrological assessments and sustainable engineering solutions before any changes to the waterway.

Ahmad Shabbar, representing the Pakistan Maholiyati Tahaffuz Movement (PMTM), expressed solidarity with the residents and said the movement was examining legal options to support their campaign.

Deputy Parliamentary Leader of the Opposition in the KMC Taimoor Ahmed raised concerns over alleged plans to encroach upon Nehr-e-Khayyam land through the creation of six flat sites and two multi-storey commercial plots. He claimed that a proposed map was already circulating in the builders' market.

The protesters reiterated their demand for an immediate suspension of construction until all environmental and technical concerns were independently examined, necessary approvals obtained and project details made public.

They stressed that urban development must not come at the expense of public land, essential drainage infrastructure, environmental protection and the safety of surrounding communities.

headline: CCD fears keep drug suspects behind bars
description: CCD fears keep drug suspects behind bars
author: KHALID RASHEED
article_text:
For some drug suspects in Punjab, freedom comes with fear. Thousands of undertrials facing drug-peddling charges are reportedly reluctant to seek bail over fears of alleged violence by the Crime Control Department (CCD) after their release. Their reluctance is adding to prison overcrowding and raising questions about access to justice and the safety of suspects outside jail.

According to data available to The Express Tribune, Punjab's 45 prisons housed 72,940 inmates, including around 53,000 undertrials. Of these, 15,390 faced drug-peddling charges, up from 13,000 in 2024 and 14,300 in 2025. More than 200 of the inmates were women.

Adiala Jail had the highest number of undertrials at 6,390, followed by Lahore's Camp Jail with 6,033 and Central Jail Gujranwala with 4,870. Other overcrowded facilities included Central Jail Faisalabad (2,770), District Jail Sialkot (2,480), District Jail Sheikhupura (2,285), District Jail Faisalabad (2,070) and District Jail Kasur (1,970). Drug-related cases accounted for over 23 per cent of undertrials. Around 17,000 were held for minor offences, while more than 2,200 awaited release in drug-use cases. Separately, 2,050 prisoners, including 140 women, had been convicted of drug peddling.

Former Punjab prisons chief Salahuddin Ahmed Khan Niazi said police and CCD personnel often wait outside jails with lists of inmates granted bail but wanted in other cases. Fearing immediate rearrest, he said, some suspects prefer to remain behind bars rather than seek release.

"The fear of the CCD keeps them from leaving prison," Niazi said, adding that the possibility of immediate rearrest had become a factor in some suspects' decisions to remain behind bars. Abdullah Malik, a legal expert and head of a human rights organisation, said allegations of police encounters involving the CCD had prompted widespread concern. He said some suspects accused of drug peddling were reluctant to seek bail because they feared being subjected to what is commonly described as a "quarter encounter" or "half encounter", terms used to refer to alleged police violence resulting in serious injuries, including broken arms or legs.

Malik said incidents involving drug suspects who had secured bail and were subsequently allegedly subjected to such violence in different cities had reinforced these fears. "Therefore, some detainees view prison as a safer alternative to returning to the outside world," noted Malik.

Inspector General of Prisons Punjab Mian Salik Jalal said judicial officers visited prisons to release undertrial prisoners involved in minor offences on personal surety. Delays could occur when judicial officers were unable to visit, adding to the number of detainees awaiting release.

Under the rules, he said, judicial officers of at least the rank of Additional Sessions Judge were required to visit prisons twice a month. With prison populations continuing to rise, authorities had to prioritise the production of prisoners accused of serious offences before courts, he added.

Jalal said that once a court granted bail and the necessary release order was issued, the prison administration processed the detainee's release. Responsibility for any subsequent arrest outside prison, he said, did not rest with the prison authorities. He expressed hope that the opening of the new Islamabad prison would help ease overcrowding in Punjab's jails.

Punjab Home Department spokesperson Tauseef Gondal said the department was monitoring prison overcrowding and regularly updating inmate records, with particular attention to drug-related and serious offences.

A CCD spokesperson said police arrested suspects only in registered cases and could rearrest them if they faced other pending cases despite securing bail. The spokesperson also claimed CCD measures had reduced crime in Punjab by 50 per cent.

However, rights advocates warn that fears of alleged police violence, alongside delays in judicial proceedings, may be discouraging suspects from seeking bail and adding to prison overcrowding.
