article_html:
LAHORE:

For some drug suspects in Punjab, freedom comes with fear. Thousands of undertrials facing drug-peddling charges are reportedly reluctant to seek bail over fears of alleged violence by the Crime Control Department (CCD) after their release. Their reluctance is adding to prison overcrowding and raising questions about access to justice and the safety of suspects outside jail.

According to data available to The Express Tribune, Punjab's 45 prisons housed 72,940 inmates, including around 53,000 undertrials. Of these, 15,390 faced drug-peddling charges, up from 13,000 in 2024 and 14,300 in 2025. More than 200 of the inmates were women.

Adiala Jail had the highest number of undertrials at 6,390, followed by Lahore's Camp Jail with 6,033 and Central Jail Gujranwala with 4,870. Other overcrowded facilities included Central Jail Faisalabad (2,770), District Jail Sialkot (2,480), District Jail Sheikhupura (2,285), District Jail Faisalabad (2,070) and District Jail Kasur (1,970). Drug-related cases accounted for over 23 per cent of undertrials. Around 17,000 were held for minor offences, while more than 2,200 awaited release in drug-use cases. Separately, 2,050 prisoners, including 140 women, had been convicted of drug peddling.

Former Punjab prisons chief Salahuddin Ahmed Khan Niazi said police and CCD personnel often wait outside jails with lists of inmates granted bail but wanted in other cases. Fearing immediate rearrest, he said, some suspects prefer to remain behind bars rather than seek release.

"The fear of the CCD keeps them from leaving prison," Niazi said, adding that the possibility of immediate rearrest had become a factor in some suspects' decisions to remain behind bars. Abdullah Malik, a legal expert and head of a human rights organisation, said allegations of police encounters involving the CCD had prompted widespread concern. He said some suspects accused of drug peddling were reluctant to seek bail because they feared being subjected to what is commonly described as a "quarter encounter" or "half encounter", terms used to refer to alleged police violence resulting in serious injuries, including broken arms or legs.

Malik said incidents involving drug suspects who had secured bail and were subsequently allegedly subjected to such violence in different cities had reinforced these fears. "Therefore, some detainees view prison as a safer alternative to returning to the outside world," noted Malik.

Inspector General of Prisons Punjab Mian Salik Jalal said judicial officers visited prisons to release undertrial prisoners involved in minor offences on personal surety. Delays could occur when judicial officers were unable to visit, adding to the number of detainees awaiting release.

Under the rules, he said, judicial officers of at least the rank of Additional Sessions Judge were required to visit prisons twice a month. With prison populations continuing to rise, authorities had to prioritise the production of prisoners accused of serious offences before courts, he added.

Jalal said that once a court granted bail and the necessary release order was issued, the prison administration processed the detainee's release. Responsibility for any subsequent arrest outside prison, he said, did not rest with the prison authorities. He expressed hope that the opening of the new Islamabad prison would help ease overcrowding in Punjab's jails.

Punjab Home Department spokesperson Tauseef Gondal said the department was monitoring prison overcrowding and regularly updating inmate records, with particular attention to drug-related and serious offences.

A CCD spokesperson said police arrested suspects only in registered cases and could rearrest them if they faced other pending cases despite securing bail. The spokesperson also claimed CCD measures had reduced crime in Punjab by 50 per cent.

However, rights advocates warn that fears of alleged police violence, alongside delays in judicial proceedings, may be discouraging suspects from seeking bail and adding to prison overcrowding.

headline: Govt College reverts to historic name
description: Govt College reverts to historic name
author: Adnan Lodhi
article_text:
The Government College University, an institution whose academic legacy stretches back more than 160 years, is set to revert to its historic identity as Government College Lahore under a legislative move by the Punjab government ordering six public sector higher education institutions to drop the word "University" from their official names wherever applicable.

The development follows the Public Sector Universities (Amendment) Act, 2026. Through a notification issued on October 23, the Punjab Higher Education Department directed vice chancellors and rectors of the government and private universities to implement the revised institutional names in accordance with the legislation.

The decision is particularly significant for the Government College University Lahore, which had acquired the university status in 2002 after more than a century of operating as Government College Lahore.

The university will be known as Government College Lahore, marking a symbolic return to its historical identity.

The other institutions covered by the notification are Government College Faisalabad, Government College for Women Faisalabad, Government College for Women Sialkot, Government Sadiq College Bahawalpur and Lahore College for Women.

However, the restoration of the old names will not alter the institutions' mandates and functions relating to higher education.

Established on January 1, 1864 with an initial enrolment of nine students, the Government College gradually developed into one of the country's prominent centres of higher learning. It attained degree awarding status in 1997 before being elevated to university in 2002.

Its history is associated with distinguished personalities, including philosopher and educationist Dr GW Leitner, national poet Allama Iqbal and Nobel laureate Dr Abdus Salam.

It is not yet clear how the transition will be reflected in academic certificates of current students and graduates. A change in the legal name requires consistent documentation to avoid discrepancies between the existing and future record.

The notification asks the concerned institutions to take necessary action in accordance with the provisions of the act but does not specify a completion deadline.

An old student, Nadeem Malek, said, "This is an excellent development as it was the wish of thousands of old graduates to restore the old name of this historic institution.

It was a top college once but has dropped in recent years. The government should also focus on restoring the historic standard of the college."

headline: Illegal construction faces crackdown
description: Illegal construction faces crackdown
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Worsening air pollution and smog in the city has brought the environmental impact of unregulated construction into focus as the metropolitan corporation has launched a month-long demolition campaign against illegal structures across Lahore

According to a notification, the demolition and follow-up operations are planned across the Wagha, Data Gunj Bakhsh, Nishtar, Allama Iqbal, Shalimar, Ravi, Samanabad, Gulberg and Aziz Bhatti zones.

Sources said unauthorised construction work under way across the city had been identified as among the major reasons of smog at a time when Lahore is in the grip of air pollution. The operations are planned in all zones of Lahore throughout the month.

Senior officers and building inspectors have been instructed to remain present during the action.

Officials said follow-up action was also intended to prevent illegal construction from resuming after demolition. Lahore had been ranked the world's most polluted major city on October 29 with an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 419 on IQAir's live ranking.

"November in past years was the peak season of smog in Lahore. Demolition, excavation, cement handling and the movement of sand, soil and rubble can release dust. Fine particles from these activities add to airborne particulate matter while uncovered construction material and debris left on roads or vacant plots can be lifted again by wind and traffic.

headline: Lahore hosts tree from dinosaur-era lineage
description: Lahore hosts tree from dinosaur-era lineage
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
A 176-year-old queen sago palm, a member of a plant lineage older than the dinosaurs, is in full leaf at Lawrence Garden, a spokesperson for the Punjab Horticulture Authority (PHA) said.

The tree predates the historic garden, which was developed in the 1860s as a botanical and leisure ground. The spokesperson said the garden was modelled on London's Kew Gardens.

Queen sago palms are cycads, an ancient group of seed-bearing plants whose fossil record dates to the Permian period, about 280 million to 300 million years ago. The world's oldest potted plant, a cycad, has been at Kew Gardens since 1775.

Cycads became particularly widespread during the Mesozoic era, when dinosaurs dominated the Earth. Plant-eating dinosaurs, including long-necked sauropods, are believed to have fed on the foliage, cones, and nutrient-rich seeds of cycads.

Cycads are also known for their exceptionally slow growth and longevity. According to horticulture experts, sago palms require four to five hours of sunlight daily and relatively little water once established. Their slow-growing nature allows them to survive in a range of growing conditions, including relatively dry and poor soils.

Their structure has changed little over hundreds of millions of years, so they are commonly called 'living fossils'. However, their numbers have declined considerably, and about 60 per cent of assessed species are now threatened with extinction in their natural habitats, according to the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List of Threatened Species, the global inventory of extinction risk.

The spokesperson said the PHA manages some of the world's oldest prehistoric trees. "The fact that the sago palm in Lahore is not only prehistoric but also belongs to a threatened variety makes it especially significant," he said.

The spokesperson said Lawrence Garden was regarded as one of Asia's largest botanical gardens, with around 150 varieties of trees, including 30 of palms. Its collection includes trees and plants introduced by the British from across the Indian Empire, as well as from Palestine, Syria, Austria and other parts of Europe, he added.

headline: Punjab govt aims to train a million youth in skills
description: Punjab govt aims to train a million youth in skills
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has set a target of providing skills training to one million youth.over the next three years.

Chairing a meeting on Sunday, the chief minister received a briefing on ongoing and proposed skill development projects and approved initiatives to expand technical and vocational training across the province.

A decision to establish Punjab's first modern Woodworking Centre of Excellence was approved. Centres of excellence of electrical work, vehicle technology and digital marketing will also be set up.

Certification programmes for agriculture and heavy machinery operators were also approved in the meeting.

The chief minister also approved the launch of a programme under which courses in 13 languages will be offered.

The province's first cleaning and cleaner academy will also be established to provide professional training in healthcare, hospitality and domestic services.

The participants were informed that skills training had been completed for 400,000 young people in the province, with more than 45 per cent securing employment, while many others had opted to continue their education. The trained youth who have secured employment include over 38,000 who have found jobs abroad. About 113,333 youths have completed training in manufacturing, with more than 50,000 securing immediate employment. In the IT sector, 111,607 young people received training, of whom 49,588 were earning through employment. Similarly, 23,269 people completed training in agriculture and livestock, with 10,033 securing jobs. In the construction sector, 27,069 received training and 12,026 found employment, while 35,227 were trained in the energy sector, of whom 15,651 secured jobs. A total of 15,319 trainees completed hospitality and tourism courses, with 6,807 securing immediate employment.

It was revealed that 90,029 trained youths had secured jobs in local industries, 53,509 had opted for self-employment and 38,557 had obtained employment abroad. Another 39,325 chose to continue their education.

Under the Empowering Women through Information Technology Programme, 3,000 women in rural areas are earning from home after completing training. The department had also provided industry-related, management, teaching and skills-upgradation training to 15,065 teachers and staff members.

headline: October pollution less than last year
description: October pollution less than last year
author: Asif Mehmood
article_text:
Air pollution in Lahore declined by 21 per cent in October as compared to the same month last year, but levels of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) remained above Pakistan's prescribed limit on all 30 days, according to a report by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI).

The city experienced 16 consecutive days of unhealthy air quality, while daily PM2.5 concentrations remained above the national standard throughout the month.

The report attributed part of the decline in pollution to favourable weather conditions, noting that data from the past nine years did not indicate a consistent improvement in air quality.

The average PM2.5 concentration in Lahore stood at 100.5 micrograms per cubic metre against Pakistan's permissible limit of 35 micrograms. The average Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 174.

The air quality remained unhealthy or worse from October 16 to 31.

October 23 was the most polluted day, with the PM2.5 concentration reaching 183.5 micrograms, while October 12 was the cleanest day.

The report showed that the average PM2.5 concentration in October last year was 127.4 micrograms per cubic metre, compared to 100.5 this year, representing a decline of around 21 per cent.

Favourable weather conditions contributed to the improvement. Wind speeds were 35% higher than last year.

The report estimated that weather factors reduced pollution levels by approximately 22%.

Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif stated in a social media post that last month was Lahore's cleanest October in the past five years. She said the average US AQI stood at 180.5, compared to 204.6 in 2025 and 213 in 2024.

The chief minister also noted that, for the first time in five years, an AQI above 300 had been recorded on no day during the month.

She attributed the improvement to the use of technology, environmental monitoring, coordination among government departments and enforcement of environmental regulations.

However, the PAQI report ranked October 2026 as the eighth most polluted October in the past nine years.

It also noted that pollution carried by winds from outside Lahore, along with smoke from fires along their path, contributed to the city's air pollution.

While pollution declined during the month, Lahore's air quality remained hazardous to public health.

Air pollution in Lahore declined by 21 per cent in October as compared to the same month last year, but levels of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) remained above Pakistan's prescribed limit on all 30 days, according to a report by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI).

The city experienced 16 consecutive days of unhealthy air quality, while daily PM2.5 concentrations remained above the national standard throughout the month.

The report attributed part of the decline in pollution to favourable weather conditions, noting that data from the past nine years did not indicate a consistent improvement in air quality.

The average PM2.5 concentration in Lahore stood at 100.5 micrograms per cubic metre against Pakistan's permissible limit of 35 micrograms. The average Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 174.

The air quality remained unhealthy or worse from October 16 to 31.

October 23 was the most polluted day, with the PM2.5 concentration reaching 183.5 micrograms, while October 12 was the cleanest day.

The report showed that the average PM2.5 concentration in October last year was 127.4 micrograms per cubic metre, compared to 100.5 this year, representing a decline of around 21 per cent.

Favourable weather conditions contributed to the improvement. Wind speeds were 35% higher than last year.

The report estimated that weather factors reduced pollution levels by approximately 22%.

Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif stated in a social media post that last month was Lahore's cleanest October in the past five years. She said the average US AQI stood at 180.5, compared to 204.6 in 2025 and 213 in 2024.

The chief minister also noted that, for the first time in five years, an AQI above 300 had been recorded on no day during the month.

She attributed the improvement to the use of technology, environmental monitoring, coordination among government departments and enforcement of environmental regulations.

However, the PAQI report ranked October 2026 as the eighth most polluted October in the past nine years.

It also noted that pollution carried by winds from outside Lahore, along with smoke from fires along their path, contributed to the city's air pollution.

While pollution declined during the month, Lahore's air quality remained hazardous to public health.

headline: ACE probes scam in Suthra Punjab
description: ACE probes scam in Suthra Punjab
author: Khawar Randhawa
article_text:
The Anti-Corruption Establishment has launched an inquiry into suspected financial irregularities in the Suthra Punjab Agency Faisalabad, involving monthly fuel and vehicle rental expenses.

Açcording to sources, officials have taken video recordings, documents and mobile phones of some employees for the investigation.

Legal action regarding the matter would depend on the outcome of the inquiry.

The sources said it wzs suspected that the agency had shown the Punjab government a fleet of 800 vehicles for sanitation operations, although only around 550 were allegedly in the field.

Approximately Rs15.6 million was being spent monthly on fuel for the declared fleet.

When the rental expenses of another 200 vehicles were included, the alleged irregularities amounted to nearly Rs17.5 million per month.

The suspected modus operandi involved the use of multiple fake number plates against a vehicle to obtain fuel.

Petrol station employees and other individuals reportedly worked together to attach fake registration plates to a vehicle and draw fuel against them.

After refuelling, the vehicle was allegedly taken to a workshop near the petrol station on Rajbah Road, where the fuel was drained.

The sources said an allegation was also being investigated that vehicle tracking devices had been deliberately damaged and CCTV cameras at the petrol station rendered dysfunctional to conceal the acts.

The sources said local ACE officials were examining the evidence and financial details to look into the responsibility and extent of the alleged fraud.

headline: Lazio pull clear at Serie A summit
description: Gattuso's men strengthen their grip on the summit with a 2-1 win over Cagliari
author: AFP
article_text:
Lazio coach Gennaro Gattuso warned his team not to get carried away after they surged three points clear of Inter Milan at the top of Serie A on Sunday with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari.

Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M'Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and

Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straight Serie A win.

With 28 points from 10 games, Lazio pulled clear of Inter after they lost the Milan derby. Unbeaten Roma sit third on 24 points and Como climbed back to fourth with a 1-0 win over rock-bottom Venezia.

Lazio last won Serie A in 2000 and this is the best start to a league campaign in the club's history, but the Roman outfit's ambitions remain modest according to Gattuso.

"Our target is to avoid relegation and we still need 12 more points," Gattuso said. "We need to get our heads down and work, and not look at the table."

Some Lazio fans aren't watching at all.

As has been the case in recent home matches, Lazio played in front of largely empty sections of the Stadio Olimpico, with many ultras and supporters continuing their boycott in protest against owner and president Claudio Lotito, whom they accuse of failing to invest sufficiently in the squad.

Juventus break Napoli resistance

Struggling giants Juventus got their fifth win of the season thanks to Bosnian wonderkid Kerim Alajbegovic producing a moment of magic. The teenager broke the deadlock on 70 minutes with a thumping left-footed drive from outside the box.

Napoli were then reduced to 10 men as Luca Marianucci earned a second yellow for kicking substitute Jeremie Boga, who added a second goal with a strike that rivalled that of Alajbegovic.

That result lifted Juventus to seventh. Napoli are eighth and host leaders Lazio next weekend. Como's victory at home over lowly Venezia on Sunday was a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions. The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. Como captain Lucas Da Cunha converted in the 43rd minute for the French international's first goal of the season.

"This is the type of match we found hard to win last season," Da Cunha told DAZN. Cesc Fabregas's side had slipped to fifth when AC Milan beat champions Inter 3-1 on Saturday. Como moved one point behind Roma, who beat Udinese 5-2 on Saturday. "This victory is really important in terms of our maturing process," said Fabregas.

"Our state of mind is irreproachable," added the 39-year-old Spaniard as Como prepare to resume their Champions League campaign against Lens on Wednesday.

Como have the best record of the Serie A clubs in the Champions League, sitting ninth in the 36-team standings, with six points from three games.

headline: Almgren wins debut marathon in New York
description: Chepkirui defends her women's title in 2:24:36
author: AFP
article_text:
Sweden's Andreas Almgren won the New York City Marathon, clocking 2hr 6min 1sec in a spectacular debut at the distance on Sunday.

The 31-year-old Almgren, in the spotlight after setting a European half-marathon record in Copenhagen in September, powered through the final mile to capture the victory over Italian Yemaneberhan Crippa.

Kenyan Sheila Chepkirui won the women's race for a second time, repelling the challenge of last year's winner Hellen Obiri -- who faded to finish third behind American Jessica McClain.

Almgren, who won his first international athletics title in August with 10,000m gold at the European Championships, ran comfortably in a large lead group that also included defending champion Benson Kipruto.

He broke away in the final mile, pulling away from Crippa who finished second in 2:06:14.

Lesotho's Kamohelo Mofolo was third in 2:06:26, narrowly holding off Kenya's Kipruto -- who had been trying to become the first back-to-back New York men's winner since compatriot Geoffrey Mutai in 2013.

"I mean, you can't ask for a better debut," Almgren, draped in a Swedish flag in the sunshine of Central Park, told ESPN. "I don't know what to say. I just feel like I'm about to start crying," he added after becoming the first Swede to win a major marathon.

"When Benson started picking up the pace with (five kilometers) left, I just felt like I've got the legs today."

For Chepkirui, who won in 2:24:36, it wasn't the first time she had dashed Obiri's dreams of successive wins. In 2024 she edged then-defending champion Obiri on the streets of the Big Apple.

It looked like it would again come down to the two of them as they powered together through the final mile, Chepkirui doggedly defending her place in front.

'Really tricky'

"The last mile was really tricky," Chepkirui said. "I had to be patient because I knew Hellen was really strong, so I have to really push up to the finish line."

As she did, McClain squeezed past Obiri to take second in 2:24:42, Obiri settling for third in 2:24:43.

"I don't think I have the words yet," McClain said after becoming the first US woman since 2018 to finish on the podium. "I honestly didn't feel amazing through like 18 (miles), just kind of had to stick in it and adjust. Top five was top of mind, then podium. I was, like, just stick with it, and all of a sudden Hellen was coming back to me and I don't really know what happened."

article_html:
NEW YORK:

Sweden's Andreas Almgren won the New York City Marathon, clocking 2hr 6min 1sec in a spectacular debut at the distance on Sunday.

The 31-year-old Almgren, in the spotlight after setting a European half-marathon record in Copenhagen in September, powered through the final mile to capture the victory over Italian Yemaneberhan Crippa.

Kenyan Sheila Chepkirui won the women's race for a second time, repelling the challenge of last year's winner Hellen Obiri -- who faded to finish third behind American Jessica McClain.

Almgren, who won his first international athletics title in August with 10,000m gold at the European Championships, ran comfortably in a large lead group that also included defending champion Benson Kipruto.

He broke away in the final mile, pulling away from Crippa who finished second in 2:06:14.

Lesotho's Kamohelo Mofolo was third in 2:06:26, narrowly holding off Kenya's Kipruto -- who had been trying to become the first back-to-back New York men's winner since compatriot Geoffrey Mutai in 2013.

"I mean, you can't ask for a better debut," Almgren, draped in a Swedish flag in the sunshine of Central Park, told ESPN.
"I don't know what to say. I just feel like I'm about to start crying," he added after becoming the first Swede to win a major marathon.

"When Benson started picking up the pace with (five kilometers) left, I just felt like I've got the legs today."

For Chepkirui, who won in 2:24:36, it wasn't the first time she had dashed Obiri's dreams of successive wins.
In 2024 she edged then-defending champion Obiri on the streets of the Big Apple.

It looked like it would again come down to the two of them as they powered together through the final mile, Chepkirui doggedly defending her place in front.

'Really tricky' 

"The last mile was really tricky," Chepkirui said. "I had to be patient because I knew Hellen was really strong, so I have to really push up to the finish line."

As she did, McClain squeezed past Obiri to take second in 2:24:42, Obiri settling for third in 2:24:43.

"I don't think I have the words yet," McClain said after becoming the first US woman since 2018 to finish on the podium.
"I honestly didn't feel amazing through like 18 (miles), just kind of had to stick in it and adjust. Top five was top of mind, then podium. I was, like, just stick with it, and all of a sudden Hellen was coming back to me and I don't really know what happened."

The race marked the 50th anniversary of the current incarnation of the NYC Marathon, which links the city's five boroughs of Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Manhattan.

The race was first run in 1970 when the course was confined to Central Park, becoming a city-wide event in 1976.

headline: Portuguese police clash with housing protesters, arrest 13
description: Portuguese police clash with housing protesters, arrest 13
author: AFP
article_text:
Riot police with dogs stormed protest camps in Lisbon and Porto early Sunday, charging demonstrators with batons, arresting 13 people and leaving dozens injured in the latest confrontation over Portugal's housing crisis.

Clashes quickly broke out as dozens of officers moved in on an encampment in Lisbon's Rossio Square and a smaller camp in Porto's Dom Joao I Square at around 4:30 am.

Protesters shouted "smells like a dictatorship", while police said some hurled bottles and paint at officers as they tried to take down the tents.

Police said in a statement that six people were arrested in Lisbon and seven in Porto for refusing orders to disperse. It said 13 police were injured in the process, with eight taken to hospital.

In Porto, police said three plain-clothes officers monitoring the protesters were assaulted after being spotted by a group.

An unspecified number of civilians were also injured during the operation, which was carried out "with rigour, balance and respect for citizens' rights", the statement read.

Activist group Acampada Lisboa said more than 30 protesters were injured, including 10 who required hospital treatment, and called a fresh rally in the capital on Sunday afternoon.

The camps had been set up late Saturday after peaceful marches through the two cities against soaring housing costs.

Officers have repeatedly dismantled encampments that have sprung up across Lisbon and Porto in recent weeks.

Protesters want the minority centre-right government to abandon plans to ease evictions and remove rent caps on new leases, warning the measures would push up housing costs and leave tenants more vulnerable.

Portuguese protesters have taken inspiration from a similar movement in neighbouring Spain, where tents have been set up in central Madrid and other cities for weeks.

headline: G-B marks 79th independence day
description: G-B marks 79th independence day
author: SHABBIR MIR
article_text:
Gilgit-Baltistan celebrated its 79th Independence Day on Sunday with traditional enthusiasm and patriotic spirit, as ceremonies and celebrations were held across all ten districts to commemorate the region's liberation from Dogra rule on November 1, 1947.

The main ceremony was held at Chinar Bagh Martyrs' Memorial in Gilgit, where Governor Syed Mehdi Shah hoisted the national flag in the presence of Chief Minister Amjad Hussain, the Force Commander Northern Areas, senior civil and military officials and families of martyrs. Police contingents presented a guard of honour, while the governor, chief minister and Force Commander laid floral wreaths at the memorial and offered fateha.

Addressing the gathering, the chief minister described November 1 as a landmark day symbolising freedom, sacrifice, unity and patriotism. He paid tribute to the local heroes who overthrew Dogra rule despite limited resources and subsequently decided to accede to Pakistan.

He stressed that unity, good governance and collective efforts were essential for the region's development, identifying education, healthcare, employment and equal opportunities for women as key priorities. He also paid tribute to the armed forces for their sacrifices in the fight against terrorism.

Governor Shah said the freedom enjoyed by the people was the result of the sacrifices of their forefathers. He urged citizens to protect this historic legacy and contribute actively to the region's development.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif separately congratulated the people of G-B, paying tribute to the freedom fighters. The president highlighted the region's contributions to Pakistan's defence and development, while the prime minister reaffirmed federal support for economic development, institutional reforms and improved public services.

The prime minister also highlighted development initiatives, including the 16MW Naltar hydropower project, the 100MW solar programme, four Danish Schools, laptop distribution and the proposed Maqpoon Das Special Economic Zone.

Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also extended greetings, describing the day as a symbol of courage and national unity. First Lady Asifa Bhutto Zardari congratulated the people, particularly women and youth, and called for greater opportunities for their empowerment.

A 21-gun salute, military parade, flag-hoisting ceremonies, national songs and student performances marked celebrations across the region, with people reaffirming their commitment to Pakistan's unity and G-B's prosperity.

Gilgit-Baltistan celebrated its 79th Independence Day on Sunday with traditional enthusiasm and patriotic spirit, as ceremonies and celebrations were held across all ten districts to commemorate the region's liberation from Dogra rule on November 1, 1947.

The main ceremony was held at Chinar Bagh Martyrs' Memorial in Gilgit, where Governor Syed Mehdi Shah hoisted the national flag in the presence of Chief Minister Amjad Hussain, the Force Commander Northern Areas, senior civil and military officials and families of martyrs. Police contingents presented a guard of honour, while the governor, chief minister and Force Commander laid floral wreaths at the memorial and offered fateha.

headline: Serbia marks tragedy that sparked student movement
description: Serbia marks tragedy that sparked student movement
author: AFP
article_text:
Thousands gathered in Novi Sad on Sunday to honour the victims of a railway station disaster that sparked the anti-government movement which toppled Serbia's right-wing ruling party a week earlier.

The commemoration marked two years since a concrete canopy at the newly renovated railway station in Serbia's second-largest city collapsed, killing 16 people, including two sisters aged six and 10.

Amid nationwide grief and mounting questions over the station's multi-million-euro renovation, the disaster sparked some of Serbia's largest protests since the fall of strongman Slobodan Milosevic in 2000.

"It's hard to go back to the place where it all happened," Dijana Hrka, whose 27-year-old son Stefan was killed in the collapse, told AFP.

"And each time, it gets harder and harder," said Hrka, who burst into tears as she approached a heart-shaped banner bearing her son's name, one of 16 displayed outside the station in memory of the victims.

Crowds filed past for hours, laying flowers and lighting candles.

At 11:52 am (1052 GMT), the exact time the concrete canopy collapsed two years ago, those gathered observed 16 minutes of silence -- one for each victim.

"The emotions are indescribable," Danijela, a 50-year-old Novi Sad resident, told AFP through tears.

"I think everyone who comes here today will feel an energy that is a mixture of positive and negative emotions."

headline: 'Air-con nation' Singapore eyes alternatives to cool down
description: 'Air-con nation' Singapore eyes alternatives to cool down
author: AFP
article_text:
Long dubbed an "air-conditioned nation", Singapore is experimenting with cooling alternatives from chilled beams to "passive displacement" to curb its thirst for energy-guzzling air conditioning.

The city-state has the highest per-capita air conditioner ownership rate in Southeast Asia, with about 99 percent of private residences equipped with cooling units.

Singapore's local building sector accounts for one-fifth of its emissions, while cooling itself accounts for 40 to 60 percent of a building's energy consumption, according to studies.

A stroll down renowned thoroughfare Orchard Road highlights that dependence. Shoppers are greeted by blasts of cool air that waft into the street as doors swing open -- a major draw given daytime highs hover between 31C and 33C year-round.

But air conditioning can make the heat problem worse. Compressor units belch hot air back out into the environment, and the electricity that powers the systems can contribute to climate change if generated from fossil fuels.

Alternative options

Some buildings in Singapore are looking at other options, including active chilled beams, which are perforated panels equipped with cooling coils that are mounted on ceilings.

A chiller plant on the building's top floor cools water down to 9C, then pumps it into the coils. Simultaneously, air is blasted through small nozzles inside the beams.

The jets of air create a low-pressure zone that sucks up warmer air from the room below so it passes over the coils and is cooled before recirculating.

The technology keeps the offices at the eight-storey Paya Lebar Green building in eastern Singapore at a comfortable 24C.

A visiting AFP team felt noticeably cooler air flowing from the sleek white panels on the ceiling of the building, described as one of Singapore's "greenest".

The system is also quiet, without the constant hum of air conditioning units.

When HR professional Renuga Shekar first moved into an office space at Paya Lebar Green last November, the 30-year-old and her colleagues just thought the exposed pipes and panels on the ceiling was a "warehouse kind of look".

"We didn't really think much about it. No one really commented about it," she told AFP.

It was only months later, after noticing how quiet the office was and hearing technicians mention "ACB" during maintenance, that they realised it was cooled by active chilled beams.

"We didn't even realise how different the air cooling system is because it was very seamless, and in terms of the temperature, ideal for everybody in the office," she said.

Together, the system cut energy use by more than 30 percent compared with conventional air conditioning, according to the building's designers, DP Architects.

A similar system is in use at Singapore's ports authority maintenance building at western Tuas harbour.

The building uses passive displacement cooling, which taps natural airflow to reduce reliance on mechanical fans.

Ceiling cooling coils chill the air, which sinks before naturally rising back to the coils as it warms. This continuous cycle reduces the need for fans, cutting energy use and noise.

'Mindset shift'

Another alternative is radiant cooling, where water chilled to between 14C and 18C flows through pipes or panels and absorbs heat radiating from people or objects to reduce ambient temperatures.

The push to find new cooling solutions has government backing.

A 2024 government study identified alternative cooling technologies (ACTs) as a key strategy which found they could save the city up to 48 percent in energy.

By mid-2026, at least 33 public and 14 private buildings had adopted ACTs, Singapore's building authorities said. The city-state has an ambitious goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.

The figures are still relatively small, and it can be challenging to find an ACT that is acceptable to users familiar with tried-and-tested air conditioners.

Supporters of alternative systems acknowledge that they cost more to install than conventional air?conditioning, but say they more than make up for it over time with much lower running costs thanks to big energy savings.

The most popular alternative method remains hybrid cooling -- simply turning up air conditioning to a higher temperature of 25.5C to 27C, and pairing it with fans.

"Everybody's more used to having air-conditioned office spaces, so for them to suddenly accept 26 degrees, I think the mindset shift has not reached a threshold where it's generally accepted yet," said Chua Zi Jun, director at DP Architects.

Demand for cooling is only increasing as climate change raises temperatures and humidity in Singapore and beyond.

Traditional air-conditioning systems rely on vapour compression, using refrigerants to move heat from one place to another.

ACTs use the same basic principle, but either spend less energy moving cool air or reduce run-time by leaning on people's ability to adapt to slightly higher temperatures.

"The technologies are a step in the right direction and should eventually incorporate more sophisticated controls, including predictive systems that adjust temperatures before rooms become too hot or cold," said Wan Man Pun, a cooling tech expert at Nanyang Technological University.

But "we still haven't found any alternative cooling methods that have a higher coefficient of performance, or efficiency, than vapour compression", Wan said.

A stroll down renowned thoroughfare Orchard Road highlights that dependence. Shoppers are greeted by blasts of cool air that waft into the street as doors swing open -- a major draw given daytime highs hover between 31C and 33C year-round.

But air conditioning can make the heat problem worse. Compressor units belch hot air back out into the environment, and the electricity that powers the systems can contribute to climate change if generated from fossil fuels.

Alternative options

Some buildings in Singapore are looking at other options, including active chilled beams, which are perforated panels equipped with cooling coils that are mounted on ceilings.

A chiller plant on the building's top floor cools water down to 9C, then pumps it into the coils. Simultaneously, air is blasted through small nozzles inside the beams.

The jets of air create a low-pressure zone that sucks up warmer air from the room below so it passes over the coils and is cooled before recirculating.

The technology keeps the offices at the eight-storey Paya Lebar Green building in eastern Singapore at a comfortable 24C.

A visiting AFP team felt noticeably cooler air flowing from the sleek white panels on the ceiling of the building, described as one of Singapore's "greenest".

The system is also quiet, without the constant hum of air conditioning units.

When HR professional Renuga Shekar first moved into an office space at Paya Lebar Green last November, the 30-year-old and her colleagues just thought the exposed pipes and panels on the ceiling was a "warehouse kind of look".

"We didn't really think much about it. No one really commented about it," she told AFP.

It was only months later, after noticing how quiet the office was and hearing technicians mention "ACB" during maintenance, that they realised it was cooled by active chilled beams.

"We didn't even realise how different the air cooling system is because it was very seamless, and in terms of the temperature, ideal for everybody in the office," she said.

Together, the system cut energy use by more than 30 percent compared with conventional air conditioning, according to the building's designers, DP Architects.

A similar system is in use at Singapore's ports authority maintenance building at western Tuas harbour.

The building uses passive displacement cooling, which taps natural airflow to reduce reliance on mechanical fans.

Ceiling cooling coils chill the air, which sinks before naturally rising back to the coils as it warms. This continuous cycle reduces the need for fans, cutting energy use and noise.

'Mindset shift'

Another alternative is radiant cooling, where water chilled to between 14C and 18C flows through pipes or panels and absorbs heat radiating from people or objects to reduce ambient temperatures.

The push to find new cooling solutions has government backing.

A 2024 government study identified alternative cooling technologies (ACTs) as a key strategy which found they could save the city up to 48 percent in energy.

By mid-2026, at least 33 public and 14 private buildings had adopted ACTs, Singapore's building authorities said. The city-state has an ambitious goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.

The figures are still relatively small, and it can be challenging to find an ACT that is acceptable to users familiar with tried-and-tested air conditioners.

Supporters of alternative systems acknowledge that they cost more to install than conventional air?conditioning, but say they more than make up for it over time with much lower running costs thanks to big energy savings.

The most popular alternative method remains hybrid cooling -- simply turning up air conditioning to a higher temperature of 25.5C to 27C, and pairing it with fans.

"Everybody's more used to having air-conditioned office spaces, so for them to suddenly accept 26 degrees, I think the mindset shift has not reached a threshold where it's generally accepted yet," said Chua Zi Jun, director at DP Architects.

Demand for cooling is only increasing as climate change raises temperatures and humidity in Singapore and beyond.

Traditional air-conditioning systems rely on vapour compression, using refrigerants to move heat from one place to another.

ACTs use the same basic principle, but either spend less energy moving cool air or reduce run-time by leaning on people's ability to adapt to slightly higher temperatures.

"The technologies are a step in the right direction and should eventually incorporate more sophisticated controls, including predictive systems that adjust temperatures before rooms become too hot or cold," said Wan Man Pun, a cooling tech expert at Nanyang Technological University.

But "we still haven't found any alternative cooling methods that have a higher coefficient of performance, or efficiency, than vapour compression", Wan said.

headline: Teacher shortages close seven Bara schools
description: Teacher shortages close seven Bara schools
author: Khadim Afridi
article_text:
A severe shortage of teachers, compounded by security concerns, has forced the closure of seven government girls' primary schools in Bara, while 101 teaching posts and 34 non-teaching positions remain vacant across the sub-division.

According to figures from the Sub-Divisional Education Office (Female) Bara, of the 310 sanctioned teaching posts in government primary schools in Bara tehsil, only 209 are filled. Non-teaching staff sanctioned strength stands at 270, of which 236 posts are occupied. Primary School Teacher (PST) positions number 145 sanctioned with 81 filled and 64 vacant; Primary School Head Teacher (PSHT) posts total 143 with 106 filled and 37 vacant. All 22 Trained Teacher (TT) posts are occupied. Among non-teaching staff, 142 of 143 chowkidar posts and 94 of 127 Class-IV caretaker posts are filled.

Documents from the education department show that of Bara's 142 government girls' primary schools, seven are closed, four for lack of teachers and three because of the law-and-order situation. Schools closed due to teacher unavailability include Government Girls Primary School Haji Mina Dar Khan Kalay Akakhel, Government Girls Primary School Tangi Nazar Khel Bargambar Khel, Government Girls Primary School Ham Kalay Tarkhuks Upper Bara and Government Girls Primary School Khuga Jan Bara. Those shut over security issues are Government Girls Primary School Zale Khan Tirah, Government Girls Primary School Muhammad Din Shah and Government Girls Primary School Khwaja Kalay Tirah. The closures are affecting local girls' education, while staff shortages are also disrupting teaching in functioning schools.

Sub-Divisional Education Officer (Female) Bara Shakeela Hussain told The Express Tribune that rising student numbers have deepened the crisis. Most primary schools in the sub-division have only one or two permanent female teachers, yet some now enrol as many as 500 girls. Through the Parent-Teacher Council (PTC), 282 local candidates have been selected against 300 female teacher posts; they will serve until the end of the current academic session. Their appointment has already boosted admissions. Hussain said permanent recruitment through the Educational Testing and Evaluation Agency (ETEA) remains essential, and a request has been submitted for 333 additional PTC teachers. Government girls' primary schools in Bara currently have 24,500 students, with admissions continuing until December.

The temporary Sub-Divisional Education Office (Female) itself faces practical problems. Housed in a single room inside the Bara Tehsil Building, near district administration, sub-jail and police offices, the location creates access difficulties for female teachers and parents. The office also lacks a washroom for women. Local elders and parents have urged the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa governor to shift the office immediately to the Municipal Building in Bara for the convenience of women teachers and girls' parents.

District-wide figures underline the scale of the challenge. Khyber has 747 government schools, 406 for boys and 341 for girls, comprising 588 primary, 87 middle, 51 high, six higher secondary, six mosque and six DSS schools. The district employs 1,149 female and 1,586 male teachers. Twenty-five government primary schools operate with a single teacher: 16 in Bara, seven in Landi Kotal and two in Jamrud. Of these, seven are boys' schools and 18 girls' schools (Bara: three boys' and 13 girls'; Jamrud: one each; Landi Kotal: three boys' and four girls').

Education circles say filling vacant posts, reopening closed schools and ensuring permanent teaching staff are essential to raise standards in government schools. Officials are expected to produce a clear action plan.

Housed in a single room inside the Bara Tehsil Building, near district administration, sub-jail and police offices, the location creates access difficulties for female teachers and parents. The office also lacks a washroom for women. Local elders and parents have urged the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa governor to shift the office immediately to the Municipal Building in Bara for the convenience of women teachers and girls' parents.

District-wide figures underline the scale of the challenge. Khyber has 747 government schools, 406 for boys and 341 for girls, comprising 588 primary, 87 middle, 51 high, six higher secondary, six mosque and six DSS schools. The district employs 1,149 female and 1,586 male teachers. Twenty-five government primary schools operate with a single teacher: 16 in Bara, seven in Landi Kotal and two in Jamrud. Of these, seven are boys' schools and 18 girls' schools (Bara: three boys' and 13 girls'; Jamrud: one each; Landi Kotal: three boys' and four girls').

Education circles say filling vacant posts, reopening closed schools and ensuring permanent teaching staff are essential to raise standards in government schools. Officials are expected to produce a clear action plan.

headline: Police van damaged in two IED blasts
description: No casualties reported; one police mobile van partially damaged
author: Nasruminallah
article_text:
No casualties reported; one police mobile van partially damaged

Two separate explosions involving improvised explosive devices (IEDs) planted on motorcycles rocked Bannu near Merian Gate Police Post and Degree One College, causing no casualties but partially damaging a police mobile van.

According to police sources, unidentified terrorists had planted explosives on a motorcycle near Merian Gate Police Post. The device detonated with a powerful blast, completely destroying the motorcycle and partially damaging a nearby police mobile van. However, no police personnel or civilians were injured.

In the second incident, another explosion occurred near Degree One College while police personnel were conducting routine patrols in the area. Additional Station House Officer (SHO) of Cantt Police Station, Jameel Khan, was also present at the time.

headline: Three Zhob jail officials arrested
description: Three Zhob jail officials arrested
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The Crime Branch Quetta has arrested three officials of Zhob Jail, including its superintendent and deputy superintendent, for their alleged involvement in the release of two convicted prisoners on the basis of forged Supreme Court orders.

According to prison department officials, two prisoners, Abdul Salam and Amanullah, who were serving sentences in narcotics cases, were released from Zhob Jail on May 30 last year after jail authorities received fake release orders purportedly issued by the Supreme Court.

Following departmental investigations ordered by Inspector General Prisons Asim Khan, cases were registered against Jail Superintendent Habibullah, Deputy Superintendent Muhammad Rafiq and jail clerk Sada Gul. The matter was subsequently handed over to the Crime Branch for further investigation.

Acting on the case, Crime Branch officials arrested all three accused over their alleged role in the unlawful release of the convicts.

headline: Women entrepreneurs showcase talent
description: Women entrepreneurs showcase talent
author: SHOAIB RAISANI
article_text:
.

Balochistan's women possess abundant entrepreneurial skills and creative talent; what they need are proper platforms, financial support and access to national and international markets.

This was stated by Adviser to the Chief Minister on Women's Development, Dr Rubaba Khan Balidi, while addressing the inaugural ceremony of the Women Entrepreneurs Network Exhibition (WEXNET) 2026 at Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences (BUITEMS) as chief guest.

She described WEXNET not merely as an exhibition but as a historic step towards introducing Balochistan's women entrepreneurs at the national level and linking their products to global markets. The two-day event has been organised by the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP) Quetta in collaboration with the Balochistan Board of Investment and Trade (BBoIT) and the Department of Women's Development. More than 100 women entrepreneurs from across the province are participating with their products and business ideas.

headline: K-P challenges PTI worker releases
description: K-P challenges PTI worker releases
article_text:
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government has challenged in the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) the Peshawar High Court's decisions that set aside preventive detentions of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leaders and workers under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance and directed that they not be arrested. The provincial government, acting through the chief secretary, has filed petitions against the PHC orders that declared the detentions under the MPO illegal and restrained authorities from making further arrests. It has also decided to approach the FCC against the high court's directions for the release of those already detained under the ordinance. A bench headed by Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan will hear the petitions.

Sources said petitions have been filed in cases involving 51 PTI workers. Sources added that the provincial government formed under governor's rule also plans to approach the FCC against PHC rulings that set aside the detention of a further 150 PTI workers and cancelled their sureties.

headline: Trump could launch nuclear strike on Iran within days, claims Tucker Carlson
description: Trump says he is not 'in much of a hurry' to restart strikes
author: Reuters
article_text:
US commentator Tucker Carlson claimed late on Sunday that the Trump administration could be days away from launching a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressuring President Donald Trump to authorise an attack on a suspected nuclear site in central Iran.

In a lengthy post on the US social media company X, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believes Iran has resumed its nuclear enrichment program.

Carlson is a conservative political commentator and former Fox News host whose program, Tucker Carlson Tonight, aired from 2016 to 2023.

He now hosts an independent political show on X, where he regularly comments on US foreign policy and international affairs.

Carlson claimed conventional US weapons could not penetrate the estimated 300 feet of solid granite protecting underground tunnels at the site, leaving a nuclear strike as the only military option.

"Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day," Carlson quoted an unnamed informed observer as saying.

Carlson argued that Netanyahu's political survival is driving his push for further military action. He claimed Netanyahu needs Trump's intervention to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset following the latest election results, warning that otherwise he could lose power and face investigations and possible imprisonment.

He also alleged that Netanyahu has been pressing senior US officials, including Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper, to resume major combat operations.

Carlson also claimed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were following Netanyahu's lead.

He further said former President Barack Obama had also opposed the Iran peace agreement being drafted in Doha.

Fears of regional escalation

Carlson said US allies in the Middle East were increasingly concerned about renewed fighting. He claimed Netanyahu secretly travelled to Abu Dhabi on September 27 to persuade the UAE to support a final attack on Iran, but Emirati officials refused.

Warning of the economic consequences, Carlson said eight months of conflict had severely affected Gulf economies, as well as global energy and fertiliser markets. He claimed 11 of the world's approximately 850 oil supertankers were badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October alone.

He also warned that a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Gulf and threaten the water supply of around 100 million people.

Carlson argued that a US nuclear strike could establish a dangerous precedent, potentially encouraging Russia to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine, triggering renewed nuclear tensions between India and Pakistan, and prompting North Korea to attack Seoul.

"After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final," he wrote.

He further alleged that the Trump administration had quietly revised US nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier and more likely.

Vance, Witkoff urge Trump to pursue diplomacy

Carlson said Trump could decide by Nov. 7 whether to authorise the use of nuclear weapons, adding that Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff were urging him to pursue a diplomatic agreement with Tehran.

Although acknowledging that negotiations would be difficult, Carlson said people who had spoken with Iranian decision-makers believed there was a consensus that further conflict would benefit no one and that an agreement was worth pursuing.

He concluded by warning that the consequences of a nuclear strike would extend far beyond Iran, arguing that the international public had been excluded from decisions that could threaten millions of lives.

"Now would be the time for them to speak up," Carlson wrote.

US could strike remaining Iranian nuclear sites 'within 10 minutes'

Carlson's claims follow Trump's remarks to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday that one or two Iranian nuclear facilities remained potential targets and that the US could strike them within 10 minutes.

Trump specifically mentioned Pickaxe Mountain, saying he had military plans for the area, but did not indicate that a nuclear strike had been authorised.

"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain; you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added.

In an Oct. 16 interview with Newsmax, he explicitly ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran.

A White House official said the administration does not comment on sensitive military plans, adding that Trump is keeping all options open to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

Secretary of State Rubio has also said no final decision has been made on resuming strikes.

Iran, meanwhile, denies any nuclear activity at the Pickaxe Mountain complex. Its supreme leader has warned Washington and Tel Aviv against launching further attacks.

Trump renews threat of military strikes on Iran, says US may have to 'give them the hammer'

US President Donald Trump renewed his threat of military action against Iran on Sunday, saying Washington might have to "give them the hammer," even as diplomatic efforts continued to avert another escalation.

"The only reason why I'm not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can," Trump told supporters at a rally in Iowa.

"But at some point we're going to have to give them the hammer," he added.

Trump had previously told reporters that the US still had one or two targets left to strike in Iran, suggesting further military action could be imminent.

Iranian negotiators left Doha talks on Sunday, draft proposal is being circulated, official says

Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday that Tehran does not expect a new US after the US midterm elections, and that the negotiators did not leave Doha due to difficulties during negotiations.

Baghaei said that messages with the US continued on Sunday, and that Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi was present in Doha to facilitate the process.

A draft proposal was being circulated for feedback, and a follow-up meeting is possible, the official added.

UAE energy minister says course of Iran war cannot be predicted but we will be more prepared

The UAE's energy minister said on Monday that what will happen in the US-Israeli war on Iran cannot be predicted, but the UAE will be more prepared than before.

Suhail al-Mazrouei told Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference (ADIPEC) that at certain times his country's exports were better than prior to the war.

Trump favours diplomacy with Iran as Netanyahu urges strikes immediately after Tuesday's US midterms: Axios

US President Donald Trump is prioritising diplomatic engagement with Iran despite pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to launch military strikes immediately after Tuesday's US midterm elections, the Axios news site reported on Sunday.

In a phone conversation Saturday, the Israeli leader pressed Washington to resume military action against Iran shortly after the ballot, but Trump favoured allowing ongoing diplomatic tracks to play out, according to American and Israeli sources familiar with the exchange. Netanyahu is concerned about Trump’s approach, according to sources.

An Israeli source characterised the discussion as "tough," while a US source described it as "direct."

Trump confirmed Sunday that he had spoken with Netanyahu by phone, describing the conversation as “a very good talk.” He said the two discussed Iran but offered no further details.

He told reporters Saturday that talks with Iran were progressing well, adding that he is not "in much of a hurry" to resume strikes, though in previous remarks he has suggested a resumption after the November 3 midterms.

The exchange follows correspondence sent by US Vice President JD Vance to Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, on the potential resumption of formal negotiations.

Qatari mediators are holding discussions with Iranian representatives to broker a return to direct negotiations.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi cautioned that an agreement has yet to be reached, saying Tehran is awaiting answers from the United States on outstanding issues.

The White House and the Israeli prime minister's office declined to comment on the report, according to Axios.

Vessel reportedly struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz: UK maritime agency

A vessel was reportedly struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, said the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre.

In a warning notice, the agency said the master of a merchant vessel had relayed a Mayday distress call received over VHF Channel 16, reporting that another vessel had been hit.

The notice listed the incident time as 2009PKT on November 1.

UKMTO advised vessels to “transit with caution and report any suspicious activity” while authorities investigate.

The agency did not identify the vessel reportedly struck or provide details on casualties, damage or the source of the projectile.

article_html:
US commentator Tucker Carlson claimed late on Sunday that the Trump administration could be days away from launching a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressuring President Donald Trump to authorise an attack on a suspected nuclear site in central Iran.

In a lengthy post on the US social media company X, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believes Iran has resumed its nuclear enrichment program.

Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its…

— Tucker Carlson (@TuckerCarlson) November 2, 2026

Carlson is a conservative political commentator and former Fox News host whose program, Tucker Carlson Tonight, aired from 2016 to 2023.

He now hosts an independent political show on X, where he regularly comments on US foreign policy and international affairs.

Carlson claimed conventional US weapons could not penetrate the estimated 300 feet of solid granite protecting underground tunnels at the site, leaving a nuclear strike as the only military option.

"Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day," Carlson quoted an unnamed informed observer as saying.

Carlson argued that Netanyahu's political survival is driving his push for further military action. He claimed Netanyahu needs Trump's intervention to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset following the latest election results, warning that otherwise he could lose power and face investigations and possible imprisonment.

He also alleged that Netanyahu has been pressing senior US officials, including Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper, to resume major combat operations.

Carlson also claimed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were following Netanyahu's lead.

He further said former President Barack Obama had also opposed the Iran peace agreement being drafted in Doha.

Fears of regional escalation

Carlson said US allies in the Middle East were increasingly concerned about renewed fighting. He claimed Netanyahu secretly travelled to Abu Dhabi on September 27 to persuade the UAE to support a final attack on Iran, but Emirati officials refused.

Warning of the economic consequences, Carlson said eight months of conflict had severely affected Gulf economies, as well as global energy and fertiliser markets. He claimed 11 of the world's approximately 850 oil supertankers were badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October alone.

He also warned that a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Gulf and threaten the water supply of around 100 million people.

Carlson argued that a US nuclear strike could establish a dangerous precedent, potentially encouraging Russia to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine, triggering renewed nuclear tensions between India and Pakistan, and prompting North Korea to attack Seoul.

"After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final," he wrote.

He further alleged that the Trump administration had quietly revised US nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier and more likely.

Vance, Witkoff urge Trump to pursue diplomacy

Carlson said Trump could decide by Nov. 7 whether to authorise the use of nuclear weapons, adding that Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff were urging him to pursue a diplomatic agreement with Tehran.

Although acknowledging that negotiations would be difficult, Carlson said people who had spoken with Iranian decision-makers believed there was a consensus that further conflict would benefit no one and that an agreement was worth pursuing.

He concluded by warning that the consequences of a nuclear strike would extend far beyond Iran, arguing that the international public had been excluded from decisions that could threaten millions of lives.

"Now would be the time for them to speak up," Carlson wrote.

US could strike remaining Iranian nuclear sites 'within 10 minutes'

Carlson's claims follow Trump's remarks to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday that one or two Iranian nuclear facilities remained potential targets and that the US could strike them within 10 minutes.

Trump specifically mentioned Pickaxe Mountain, saying he had military plans for the area, but did not indicate that a nuclear strike had been authorised.

"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain; you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added.

In an Oct. 16 interview with Newsmax, he explicitly ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran.

A White House official said the administration does not comment on sensitive military plans, adding that Trump is keeping all options open to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

Secretary of State Rubio has also said no final decision has been made on resuming strikes.

Iran, meanwhile, denies any nuclear activity at the Pickaxe Mountain complex. Its supreme leader has warned Washington and Tel Aviv against launching further attacks.

Trump renews threat of military strikes on Iran, says US may have to 'give them the hammer'

US President Donald Trump renewed his threat of military action against Iran on Sunday, saying Washington might have to "give them the hammer," even as diplomatic efforts continued to avert another escalation.

"The only reason why I'm not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can," Trump told supporters at a rally in Iowa.

"But at some point we're going to have to give them the hammer," he added.

Trump had previously told reporters that the US still had one or two targets left to strike in Iran, suggesting further military action could be imminent.

Iranian negotiators left Doha talks on Sunday, draft proposal is being circulated, official says

Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday that Tehran does not expect a new US after the US midterm elections, and that the negotiators did not leave Doha due to difficulties during negotiations.

Baghaei said that messages with the US continued on Sunday, and that Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi was present in Doha to facilitate the process.

A draft proposal was being circulated for feedback, and a follow-up meeting is possible, the official added.

UAE energy minister says course of Iran war cannot be predicted but we will be more prepared

The UAE's energy minister said on Monday that what will happen in the US-Israeli war on Iran cannot be predicted, but the UAE will be more prepared than before.

Suhail al-Mazrouei told Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference (ADIPEC) that at certain times his country's exports were better than prior to the war.

Trump favours diplomacy with Iran as Netanyahu urges strikes immediately after Tuesday's US midterms: Axios

US President Donald Trump is prioritising diplomatic engagement with Iran despite pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to launch military strikes immediately after Tuesday's US midterm elections, the Axios news site reported on Sunday.

In a phone conversation Saturday, the Israeli leader pressed Washington to resume military action against Iran shortly after the ballot, but Trump favoured allowing ongoing diplomatic tracks to play out, according to American and Israeli sources familiar with the exchange. Netanyahu is concerned about Trump’s approach, according to sources.

An Israeli source characterised the discussion as "tough," while a US source described it as "direct."

Trump confirmed Sunday that he had spoken with Netanyahu by phone, describing the conversation as “a very good talk.” He said the two discussed Iran but offered no further details.

Read: Iran warns US of prolonged war after Trump signals more strikes

He told reporters Saturday that talks with Iran were progressing well, adding that he is not "in much of a hurry" to resume strikes, though in previous remarks he has suggested a resumption after the November 3 midterms.

The exchange follows correspondence sent by US Vice President JD Vance to Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, on the potential resumption of formal negotiations.

Qatari mediators are holding discussions with Iranian representatives to broker a return to direct negotiations.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi cautioned that an agreement has yet to be reached, saying Tehran is awaiting answers from the United States on outstanding issues.

The White House and the Israeli prime minister's office declined to comment on the report, according to Axios.

Vessel reportedly struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz: UK maritime agency

A vessel was reportedly struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, said the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre.

In a warning notice, the agency said the master of a merchant vessel had relayed a Mayday distress call received over VHF Channel 16, reporting that another vessel had been hit.

UKMTO WARNING 191-26

Click here to view the full warning⤵️https://t.co/6GC5YjtGp6#MaritimeSecurity #MarSec pic.twitter.com/9aM1J3gZyA

— UKMTO Operations Centre (@UK_MTO) November 1, 2026

The notice listed the incident time as 2009PKT on November 1.

UKMTO advised vessels to “transit with caution and report any suspicious activity” while authorities investigate.

The agency did not identify the vessel reportedly struck or provide details on casualties, damage or the source of the projectile.

headline: Martha Stewart apologises for homeless person Halloween costume after backlash
description: Stewart posted images with a dirty face, ripped jeans and a beanie, holding a sign reading: 'I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!'
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Martha Stewart has apologised after facing criticism for dressing as a homeless person for Halloween, admitting that her costume was insensitive and inappropriate.

The 85-year-old American lifestyle personality shared photographs of her costume on Instagram on October 31.

The images showed Stewart with a dirty face, ripped jeans and a beanie, holding a sign reading: “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” The post also promoted her candle range.

The costume quickly attracted criticism, with social media users questioning her decision to portray homelessness as a Halloween outfit.

One commenter asked: “Why do you think poor people who are dying on the side of the road are a costume?” Another wrote: “Read the room Martha, people are struggling out here.”

Stewart initially defended her costume in a statement shared with Page Six and People magazine, saying it was intended to raise awareness of homelessness.

“I am distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention,” she said.

However, Stewart later issued a further statement on Instagram, acknowledging that her earlier response had not gone far enough.

“It’s hard to admit when you’ve really screwed up. My earlier statement didn’t go far enough,” she wrote.

“I know many people are economically struggling. Wearing a costume like I did was insensitive and not funny. I’m very sorry.”

Official figures indicate that at least 770,000 people are homeless across the United States, highlighting the wider social issue behind the controversy.
