headline: Antonelli becomes Formula One's youngest king
description: He becomes Italy's first F1 champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953
author: AFP
article_text:
Twenty-year-old Kimi Antonelli ripped up the record books to become the youngest Formula One champion on Sunday in Mexico, emphasising his domination by collecting the title with four races still scheduled for the season.

The young Italian finished third, following two great champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton across the line, to put himself clear of Mercedes teammate George Russell and seven-time world champion Hamilton, the only ones who might possibly catch him. The fresh-faced prodigy, who was in tears as he crossed the line, has brought a breath of fresh air to the paddock, which he has completely won over with his performances and personality, as he became the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari 73 years ago. At 20 years and 68 days old, he is by far the youngest ever champion: the previous record holder Sebastian Vettel was 23 years and 133 days old when he won his first title in 2010. Flung into Formula One in 2025 at just 18, he has dazzled in his second season. His Mercedes team has dominated but the Italian has emphatically outperformed his British team-mate Russell.

After finishing second to Russell in the opener in Australia, Antonelli won the next five races. Coming into Mexico, he had won nine of the 18 races, displaying his consistency with six other podium finishes. His ability and chutzpah were best illustrated in Monza when, after starting 19th, he weaved his way through the pack - and past Russell who had started on pole - to win his home grand prix comfortably. It was one of the all-time great race performances. The son of Elisabetta, who stays out of the spotlight, and Marco, a former driver and team principal, Andrea Kimi Antonelli started karting at seven, although his father, surprisingly, opposed a career in the sport. "He didn't want me to become a driver because motorsports can be very cruel at times, especially financially, since it's very hard to succeed without the support of the right people," said Antonelli before the US Grand Prix. "He taught me everything he knew, first about racing, and now about life. It's really important to have him by my side during races." Antonelli was spotted and, at the age of 11, recruited by Frenchman Gwen Lagrue, head of the Mercedes junior driver programme, where Hamilton was his mentor. "He's incredibly impressive and deserves to be world champion," said the Englishman, whose record of seven world titles may one day come under threat from his protege.

'Handle the pressure'

Antonelli began in karting, dominating the sport in 2020 and 2021. He was Italian and German F4 champion in 2022, and champion in Formula Regional, in F3 cars, in 2023. He skipped F3 and went straight into F2 in 2024. Although he only finished sixth, another leap followed when Hamilton left Mercedes for Ferrari. There were a few bumps and brushes in his rookie year in F1 but he still managed a second place in Sao Paulo and two other podiums, finishing seventh in the championship. "I said from the start that he had tremendous talent and a great personality, but that he would need a season in F1 to grow and learn through both great moments and setbacks," Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff told AFP. "He was catapulted into F1, and it wasn't easy, even though he had always driven very well. He had to handle the pressure, the media, and the expectations. "And it's all the more satisfying to see just how good he's been this year. It was a bit of a surprise that he performed at such a high level." After Antonelli became the second-youngest Formula One winner with his first victory in China in March, Lagrue sent an emotional message. "It's hard to put into words the feelings we experienced during the final laps of the Chinese Grand Prix, watching you attack every corner that brought you closer to your first F1 victory. Speed is one thing. Mental toughness is another. On Sunday, you demonstrated both." Always cheerful, smiling, and full of jokes, Antonelli has become the life and soul of the paddock. Every press conference is laced with humour with other drivers joining in the fun. Peter Bonnington, his race engineer who previously worked with Hamilton, has lost count of the jokes the Italian has played on him this year - or the cream pies the youngster has thrown in his face.

Behind the jokes, however, lies a brilliant, deserving world champion.

headline: LHC orders meeting between Noreen and her daughters, summons DC over detention extension
description: The hearing of the petition challenging the extension of Aleema Khanum's detention was adjourned until next week
author: Rana Yasif
article_text:
The Lahore High Court on Monday ordered jail authorities to arrange a one-hour meeting between Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan's sister Noreen Niazi and her two daughters at 10am on Tuesday, while summoning the Lahore Deputy Commissioner in person to explain the extension of detention orders against Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khanum.

Imran’s sisters were detained in September under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, 1960, as the PTI prepared for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Aleema was detained on September 20, while Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody on September 21. Their initial detention orders were issued for 30 days. The orders were later extended another 30 days.

Justice Abher Gul Khan issued the directions while hearing petitions filed by Sakina Niazi and Shahraiz challenging the extension orders in detention of three sisters of Imran Khan and further seeking permission for the detained sisters to meet their family members.

The court directed the petitioners' counsel to submit an application to the Lahore DC seeking permission for the meeting and ordered the deputy commissioner to ensure that the daughters were allowed to meet their mother at the jail for one hour.

The court also summoned the DC Lahore in person on November 4 in connection with the extension of detention orders against Noreen and Uzma.

Meanwhile, the hearing of the petition challenging the extension of Aleema Khanum's detention was adjourned until next week.

During the proceedings, the Punjab Home Secretary submitted a report in compliance with the court's earlier directions. The Punjab government's counsel informed the court that Noreen had received medical treatment at a hospital and was subsequently shifted back to jail on the advice of doctors.

The government lawyer further submitted that Noreen's daughter, Hajra Niazi, had already been allowed to meet her mother on October 29 during her hospital treatment.

Earlier, the court had sought reports from the Punjab home secretary and jail authorities on the continued detention of the three sisters, as well as Noreen's reported illness and the denial of family meetings with the detained women.

Justice Abher Gul Khan, while hearing petitions filed by Sakina Niazi and Shahraiz, directed the home secretary to submit a report on the extension. The court also sought a report from jail authorities on Noreen's health and directed the Inspector General of Prisons Mian Salik Jalal to submit a report on permission for the detained sisters to meet their family members.

The court had adjourned further proceedings on all petitions until 2pm today.

During the hearing, the petitioners' counsel Rana Mudassar Umar informed the court that Noreen was seriously ill and had been admitted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC). He also filed an application seeking the court's intervention over her medical condition.

The petitions stated that the deputy commissioner had issued a notification on October 7 extending the detention of the three women after the completion of their initial 30-day detention. The petitioners challenged the notification as illegal, arguing that the extension had been issued unlawfully. They further alleged that the detained women had not been allowed to meet their family members or legal counsel.

They asked the court to declare the October 7 notification extending their detention illegal.

Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, speaking to the media at the LHC, alleged that Aleema and her driver had been arrested before the detention notification was issued. He said even the driver, who had been working on daily wages, had been taken into custody.

Expressing concern over the difficulties in securing meetings with the detained women through court intervention, Raja said he was compelled to acknowledge that access to detainees had become increasingly difficult.

"Anyone can be picked up at any time, and courts are unable to deliver justice," he said, adding that colonial-era laws were being used to curtail citizens' freedoms. He maintained that courts were helpless under the prevailing circumstances, despite earlier judgements delivered by an independent judiciary.

Raja also said the PTI did not control social media activities but would continue to hold protests and inform the public about political and national issues. Alleging that people taking to the streets were being fired upon, he said his party would continue to raise its voice for the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.

He said highlighting issues such as inflation and unemployment was the responsibility of every political party, adding that political parties should raise their voices for the protection of constitutional rights. Raja maintained that PTI founder Imran Khan was behind bars for seeking protection of these very public rights.

Last week, the LHC summoned the Punjab home secretary and the superintendent of Kot Lakhpat Jail over the continued detention of Imran’s sisters despite the expiry of their 30-day detention orders. The Lahore deputy commissioner issued the 30-day detention orders citing police reports alleging that the women’s activities posed a threat to public safety and the maintenance of public order.

The sisters subsequently challenged their detention in the Lahore High Court, seeking the annulment of the orders and their immediate release. On September 25, the court declined to suspend the detention notifications against Uzma and Noreen at that stage and sought responses from the relevant authorities.

The court also summoned the DC Lahore in person on November 4 in connection with the extension of detention orders against Noreen and Uzma.

Meanwhile, the hearing of the petition challenging the extension of Aleema Khanum's detention was adjourned until next week.

During the proceedings, the Punjab Home Secretary submitted a report in compliance with the court's earlier directions. The Punjab government's counsel informed the court that Noreen had received medical treatment at a hospital and was subsequently shifted back to jail on the advice of doctors.

The government lawyer further submitted that Noreen's daughter, Hajra Niazi, had already been allowed to meet her mother on October 29 during her hospital treatment.

Earlier, the court had sought reports from the Punjab home secretary and jail authorities on the continued detention of the three sisters, as well as Noreen's reported illness and the denial of family meetings with the detained women.

Justice Abher Gul Khan, while hearing petitions filed by Sakina Niazi and Shahraiz, directed the home secretary to submit a report on the extension. The court also sought a report from jail authorities on Noreen's health and directed the Inspector General of Prisons Mian Salik Jalal to submit a report on permission for the detained sisters to meet their family members.

The court had adjourned further proceedings on all petitions until 2pm today.

During the hearing, the petitioners' counsel Rana Mudassar Umar informed the court that Noreen was seriously ill and had been admitted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC). He also filed an application seeking the court's intervention over her medical condition.

The petitioners challenged the notification as illegal, arguing that the extension had been issued unlawfully. They further alleged that the detained women had not been allowed to meet their family members or legal counsel.

They asked the court to declare the October 7 notification extending their detention illegal.

Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, speaking to the media at the LHC, alleged that Aleema and her driver had been arrested before the detention notification was issued. He said even the driver, who had been working on daily wages, had been taken into custody.

Expressing concern over the difficulties in securing meetings with the detained women through court intervention, Raja said he was compelled to acknowledge that access to detainees had become increasingly difficult.

"Anyone can be picked up at any time, and courts are unable to deliver justice," he said, adding that colonial-era laws were being used to curtail citizens' freedoms. He maintained that courts were helpless under the prevailing circumstances, despite earlier judgements delivered by an independent judiciary.

Raja also said the PTI did not control social media activities but would continue to hold protests and inform the public about political and national issues. Alleging that people taking to the streets were being fired upon, he said his party would continue to raise its voice for the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law.

He said highlighting issues such as inflation and unemployment was the responsibility of every political party, adding that political parties should raise their voices for the protection of constitutional rights. Raja maintained that PTI founder Imran Khan was behind bars for seeking protection of these very public rights.

Last week, the LHC summoned the Punjab home secretary and the superintendent of Kot Lakhpat Jail over the continued detention of Imran’s sisters despite the expiry of their 30-day detention orders. The Lahore deputy commissioner issued the 30-day detention orders citing police reports alleging that the women’s activities posed a threat to public safety and the maintenance of public order.

The sisters subsequently challenged their detention in the Lahore High Court, seeking the annulment of the orders and their immediate release. On September 25, the court declined to suspend the detention notifications against Uzma and Noreen at that stage and sought responses from the relevant authorities.

headline: Vacherot beats Lehecka to clinch Basel title
description: The 27-year-old fights back from a set down to defeat Lehecka 2-6, 6-3, 6-3
author: AFP
article_text:
Valentin Vacherot won his first title of the season Sunday when he beat Jiri Lehecka 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 in the final of the ATP event in Basel.

After dropping serve three times as he lost the first set, the 27-year-old from Monaco gradually gained control of the match to claim his second title on the main tour, following his surprise victory at the Shanghai Masters in 2025. For Lehecka, 24, the loss extended his poor record in finals to seven defeats from nine appearances. He has lost each of the past five. The Czech had completely dominated Vacherot in a two-set victory in their last meeting in early October, in the semi-finals in Tokyo. The first set on Sunday suggested that result might be repeated. Lehecka conceded only one point on his first three service games and proved superior in every aspect of the game.

Lehecka put pressure on Vacherot's serve throughout the match but the Monegasque saved all five break points he faced over the next two sets. In both a single break was enough for Vacherot, who closed out the match on his first championship point. "I ended up playing a really solid second and third set," Vacherot said. "I had to hold tight in the second set because even until the last game he had break points. Then I started serving much better in the third set and that helped me a lot." "I hit really good shots at the right moments," he said. "Sometimes it's about not playing perfect for the whole match and just playing good when it matters."

The victory over Lehecka, who entered the tournament ranked No. 21 in the world, was Vacherot's third against a top-25 opponent in Basel, where he also saw off 11th-ranked Rafael Jodar after a three-hour battle and world number 13 Taylor Fritz in the semi-finals.

headline: 'The Bachelor' alum Melissa Rycroft arrested for second DWI while on probation for previous offence
description: She got famous on the 13th season of the show before competing on 'DWTS', where she won the 2012 All-Stars season
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Former The Bachelor contestant Melissa Rycroft has been arrested on suspicion of driving while intoxicated (DWI), just months after receiving a sentence for a previous offence.

Rycroft was booked on Sunday, November 1. Records from Tarrant County jail obtained by TMZ indicate that she faces several charges, including driving while intoxicated, driving with an invalid licence following a previous conviction or suspension, and causing vehicle damage in a collision involving less than $200.

Details surrounding the latest incident have not been disclosed, and Rycroft has not publicly commented on the reports.

The arrest comes while the reality television personality is reportedly serving probation for her previous DWI case.

She was arrested in late 2025 following a car accident and subsequently charged with driving while intoxicated.

In August 2026, Rycroft accepted a plea agreement that allowed her to avoid 280 days in jail in exchange for 20 months of probation.

According to court documents obtained by Us Weekly, she was also ordered to pay approximately $2,000 in fines, complete 36 hours of community service and attend a DWI education programme.

The agreement additionally prohibited her from consuming alcohol or drugs and required monthly check-ins with Texas's Community Supervision and Corrections Department.

Rycroft rose to prominence on the 13th season of The Bachelor before competing on Dancing with the Stars, where she won the 2012 All-Stars season alongside professional dancer Tony Dovolani.

headline: Mbappe scores as Real Madrid beat Santander
description: Bellingham and Diomande also score as Madrid secure a 3-0 victory
author: AFP
article_text:
Kylian Mbappe moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.

The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d'Or to Bayern Munich's Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Real Madrid's match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout. Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande were also on target to keep third-place Madrid within three points of leaders Barcelona, who thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday. Jose Mourinho's side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind city rivals Atletico Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.

"In the first half we were very strong, we came out to play well," Mourinho told reporters. "The team is growing, playing well, I think we should have scored even more goals with the chances we had." Mbappe won a soft penalty as he went down under little pressure from Matteo Prati, smashing it home to put Madrid ahead at the Sardinero stadium in the 11th minute. It was the 27-year-old's 12th league goal of the season, trailing only Barcelona's Raphinha with 15 in the scoring charts. Madrid had control of the game and a fine pass from Arda Guler sent Bellingham through on goal for the second. The England international knocked the ball past the goalkeeper and rolled home for his 50th goal since joining Madrid in 2023. "Reaching 50 goals with Real Madrid is very special," Bellingham told Real Madrid TV. "We played very well. It was very important to win after the victory at Camp Nou (against Barca last weekend), so we are very happy." Guler spurned a good opportunity for the third after being set up by Mbappe, before Madrid's record signing Diomande lashed home from the edge of the box. The hosts started the second half well, pushing Madrid back, much to the chagrin of Mourinho, who yelled at his players. Madrid regained their control and racked up several more chances, with Mbappe hitting the post and Bellingham denied by Racing goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala.

'A great Madrid'

Racing won a penalty after Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni handled in the box, but the award was cancelled after a VAR review. Bellingham had a second goal ruled out in stoppage time after he strayed offside before finding the net and Endrick bent an effort narrowly wide from distance. Hosts Racing, 16th, back in La Liga for the first time in 14 seasons, fell to their first home defeat of the campaign. Earlier Sevilla, sixth, suffered a 3-1 loss at Getafe, who moved into mid-table. "(Madrid's penalty award) annoys me," Racing coach Jose Alberto told DAZN. "Evidently we came across a great Madrid, who put us under a lot of pressure in the first half hour, and were much better than us, but what conditions everything was the first goal and the penalty." Valencia, 19th, beat Elche 1-0 with a well-taken goal from Umar Sadiq to move to within a point of safety after a bad start to the season. Elsewhere Athletic Bilbao, seventh, edged fifth-place Real Sociedad 2-1 in an entertaining Basque derby clash at San Mames stadium. Inaki Williams lobbed Athletic ahead early on before Luka Sucic drilled home from the edge of the box to level. Alex Berenguer controversially restored Athletic's advantage just before half-time from the penalty spot, after Jon Aramburu was adjudged to have fouled Nico Williams, although he appeared to win the ball. "I think it's incredible that a penalty like that is given when I touched the ball, even Nico said it," complained Aramburu to DAZN.

Spanish World Cup-winning goalkeeper Unai Simon made several fine saves to ensure Los Leones claimed the three points.

headline: Alcaraz crushes De Minaur in Vienna final
description: The Spaniard beats De Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to collect his 28th career title
author: AFP
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz completed an unbeaten season in ATP 500-level events when he cruised past Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 in the Vienna Open on Sunday.

Alcaraz closed out the victory on his first match point on De Minaur's serve, in 1 hour and 27 minutes to beat the Australian for the seventh time in as many meetings. De Minaur battled hard.

He took seven games in the first set to deuce but only won one.

In the second set, De Minaur, who entered the final on a ten-match indoor unbeaten streak, saved break points in three of his first four service games. Alcaraz forced the break he needed in the 10th and final game.

"His style is really dangerous," said Alcaraz. "He's really fast, so you have to earn every point. You might hit a winner against everybody, except him. I had to be really focused on that."

"I tried to be aggressive and show him that if he wants to win, he has to play better, more aggressive, more solid, and be smarter than me."

Alcaraz did not drop a single set in five matches in Vienna as he claimed the 28th title of his career.

The victory followed his title in Tokyo four weeks ago.

Alcaraz also won in Doha in February before he was sidelined for almost five months with a wrist injury. All three 500 titles came on hard courts

The seven-time Grand Slam champion made his return to the courts at the US Open in New York, where he was eliminated in the quarterfinals.

Alcaraz said his form in Vienna had been encouraging.

"Obviously it has been a really emotional and amazing week for me. I learned a lot, to keep going forward, step by step, playing on indoor courts, and trying to gain more confidence playing on this surface," he said.

headline: Dave Bautista gains 20 pounds of muscle for 'God of War' role
description: Dave Bautista reveals 20-pound muscle gain as he prepares to portray Kratos in Prime Video's 'God of War' series
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Dave Bautista has revealed that he has gained 20 pounds of muscle while preparing to play Kratos in Prime Video's upcoming God of War television series.

The actor shared the update in a video posted to his Instagram story, accompanied by the text "Gained 20 lbs for GOW" and a “250” sticker indicating his current weight. Bautista was also wearing a God of War T-shirt in the post.

Bautista was officially cast as Kratos in August, replacing Ryan Hurst, who had to leave the production after tearing a bicep while filming a stunt. Hurst's expected recovery period meant he could no longer continue with the role.

In early September, Bautista shared another video showing his physical training progress. At the time, he revealed that he had been weight training for three weeks and had two months to "get where he needs to be."

The latest update suggests that the actor has made significant progress towards his physical transformation for the part.

During his WWE wrestling career, Bautista maintained an average weight of around 290 pounds. In recent years, however, he deliberately reduced his muscle mass to pursue a wider range of acting roles and feel more comfortable on camera.

His slimmer appearance prompted some God of War fans to question whether he would suit the physically imposing video game character.

The Prime Video adaptation will be based on the Norse mythology era of the PlayStation game franchise.

It will follow Kratos and his son Atreus, played by Callum Vinson, as they travel across the nine realms to spread the ashes of their wife and mother, Faye, at the highest peak.

headline: Nine people dead in Learjet crash in south Florida, officials say
description: Crash leaves 'massive crater' ​by road, around 600 people being relocated as investigation underway
author: Reuters
article_text:
A Learjet crashed on Sunday afternoon in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, ‌killing all nine people on board, United States transportation officials said.

The private jet had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a statement. Videos on social ​media showed the jet slamming into the ground next to a road and exploding.

"It was a ​big-time tragedy that happened," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said at a press conference near ⁠the crash site in Lake Worth Beach. "When you see that video, it's a jarring thing. It was like ​a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere."

The National Transportation Safety Board said it had ​launched an investigation into the crash, which Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called a "horrific tragedy."

FAA records list the Bombardier-made Learjet 60's owner as a Delaware corporation. Canada-based Bombardier said it would fully support the investigation and cooperate as needed.

The crash left a "massive crater" ​by the road near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores ​said at the news conference. About 600 people were being evacuated from the area and relocated to two shelters in the ‌county, ⁠Flores said.

Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms were occurring in the area at the time, forecaster AccuWeather said in a statement.

An audio recording from a Miami air traffic control centre posted on LiveATC, a site that broadcasts air traffic control communications, captured the plane's final moments before the crash in unusual detail.

At first, someone in the plane's ​cockpit reported to an ​air traffic controller that ⁠they were "managing the ice" but faced "moderate" turbulence and were seeking "better rides". Less than a minute later, the person said "Mayday, mayday," reporting that the plane was suddenly descending at a ​rate of 10,000 feet per minute.

Seconds later, the person said they were declaring ​an emergency, ⁠with the rate of descent accelerating to 20,000 feet per minute. Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: "We're going to crash into the ground" before saying that the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the ⁠plane started ​banking.

About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last thing ​heard from the cockpit was a rapidly spoken "We're out of time."

Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said data showed the vertical descent rate at ​one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.

headline: Hamza’s two-year ban lifted after two months
description: PCB overturns suspension following apology
author: Saleem Khaliq
article_text: Hamza Nazar, who was handed a two-year ban for providing incorrect information in a visa application, has had his suspension lifted just two months after it was imposed. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) overturned the all-rounder’s ban after he admitted his mistake and expressed regret. He has also been included in Sialkot’s squad for the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. The PCB announced a two-year ban on Hamza on August 6, along with a fine of Rs1 million. In its statement, the board had said the disciplinary action followed an investigation into information provided by the cricketer during his visa application process through the PCB. The Board stated that Hamza had failed to provide complete and accurate information, submitted misleading details and concealed important facts during the application process. The PCB had formed a three-member inquiry committee to investigate the matter. The committee reviewed the available evidence, gave Hamza an opportunity to present his defence and subsequently submitted its report and recommendations. After reviewing the findings, the PCB imposed a two-year suspension on Hamza from all formats of domestic and international cricket, along with a fine of Rs1 million. Hamza had been among the leading contenders for selection in Pakistan’s squads for the tours of the West Indies and England. However, the visa-related controversy had ruled him out of contention. According to sources, Hamza later approached the board, admitted his mistake and expressed regret, requesting a review of his punishment. He appealed to the PCB, stating that cricket was his livelihood and asking the board not to deprive him of the opportunity to continue playing. The PCB accepted his appeal and lifted the ban, while advising him to exercise greater caution in the future. Hamza has now been named in Sialkot’s squad for the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. He is also currently training at the National Cricket Academy in Lahore. It is worth mentioning here that the 27-year-old has scored 748 runs and taken 26 wickets in 16 first-class matches.

headline: Binance sees outflows stabilising as exchange returns online after $6.3 billion heist
description: Cryptocurrency exchange moves to reassure investors, says withdrawals stabilising
author: Reuters
article_text:
Binance customers pulled $3.64 billion, or 2.1% of its assets, as the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange resumed service after a security breach linked to North Korea saw $6.3 ​billion stolen from the platform last week.

The exchange moved to reassure crypto investors and said withdrawals were stabilising after an initial spike and deposit volumes had remained "substantial" after, what ‌analysts believe, may be the world's biggest financial robbery ever.

After hitting a six-week low on Friday, bitcoin prices recovered slightly through the weekend to trade above $78,000 on Monday. Ether hit a two-month low on Friday and also recovered a little to $2,287.

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally. It said on Sunday it had $171 billion in total assets under management as of October 28.

The Binance theft adds to a string ​of recent crypto thefts. Attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 incidents last year, according to researchers at TRM Labs

Withdrawal levels are an early test of whether customers ​still trust Binance with their money after the attack. The exchange said it had covered 95% of the assets stolen in the heist.

Stablecoin market capitalisations ⁠tend to fall when money is leaving cryptocurrencies and they have dropped since Friday. The combined capitalisation of the two largest stablecoins, USDT and USDC, has dropped by about $1.2 billion since Friday, according to ​Coinmarketcap.com.

Spot bitcoin ETFs shed $643 million on Friday, the largest daily outflow of October, and more than $1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, said Ari Redbord, global head of policy at US blockchain analysis firm ​TRM Labs.

"I get why, for conservative institutional investors, this is unsettling," Redbord said. "A hack at a financial institution means stolen usernames and passwords. A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people’s capital."

headline: Minhas credits mindset and hard work for tri-series success
description: Player of the series reflects on match-winning knock against Sri Lanka, partnership with Hasan Nawaz and adapting to different formats
author: Sports Desk
article_text: Pakistan all-rounder Arafat Minhas has credited his positive mindset, consistent work ethic and ability to adapt to match situations for his impressive performances in the recently concluded ODI tri-series, which Pakistan won after beating Sri Lanka by three wickets in a thrilling final at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday. The 21-year-old left-handed batter and left-arm spinner was named player of the series after scoring 149 runs in five matches, including two half-centuries, and taking nine wickets. In the final, Arafat scored a crucial 61 off just 31 balls and shared a match-winning 94-run partnership for the sixth wicket with Hasan Nawaz, who remained unbeaten on 37, to help Pakistan successfully chase down a target of 326. Speaking to former Pakistan captain Salman Butt on Straight Drive with Salman Butt, Arafat said his primary focus during the chase was to build a partnership and take the game deep after Pakistan had lost two wickets in quick succession. “When I went in to bat, we needed another partnership as wickets had fallen in quick succession. Hasan and I knew each other's strengths and our ability to hit boundaries. We wanted to build a partnership and take the game deep because we knew their frontline bowlers had almost completed their spells. “We were clear about our intent and knew that whoever got the opportunity to hit a boundary would take it. Hasan was finding it difficult to get going initially, but I felt the ball was coming nicely on to my bat, so I decided to take my chances. Once we started finding boundaries, the pressure eased and Hasan supported me well.” Arafat, who made his ODI debut against Australia in Rawalpindi earlier this year, also explained how a change of ball in the closing stages of the innings helped Pakistan regain momentum during the chase. “The ball had become heavy because of the dew and was staying low, which made hitting difficult. When the ball was changed around the 44th or 45th over, it started coming on to the bat much better. I told Hasan that we should look to attack deliveries in our hitting areas. “We needed a big over as the required run rate was around nine or 10. We managed to get that big over, which shifted the momentum in our favour and helped us complete the chase.” Reflecting on the atmosphere at a packed Gaddafi Stadium, Arafat said playing in front of a passionate home crowd provided additional motivation, although remaining composed under pressure was equally important. “I personally enjoy playing in front of big crowds. When you hit a boundary and the entire stadium erupts, it gives you goosebumps and a lot of motivation. But the real challenge in those situations is to control your nerves, remain calm and make the right decisions.” The youngster, who has represented Pakistan in eight ODIs and seven T20Is, said winning the player of the series award had boosted his confidence but would not change his approach to the game. “Winning the player of the series award definitely gives you confidence and improves your mindset. However, I believe your work ethic, hard work and routine should remain the same. I try to maintain the same mindset whether I perform well or not and continue to back myself. “When you receive such recognition, expectations naturally increase. I take those expectations positively because they motivate me to improve further and give my best for Pakistan in every match.” Discussing the challenge of switching between formats, Arafat said mental preparation and maintaining a disciplined routine were essential to adapting quickly. “Switching formats is largely about your mindset. If you are mentally strong, you can adapt to different challenges. Your routine and hard work remain the same, but you have to prepare yourself mentally for the demands of each format and practise accordingly.” Following the tri-series, Pakistan are set to face Sri Lanka in a two-match Test series, which forms part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27. The first Test will be played at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium from November 9-13, while the second will take place at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore from November 17-21. Arafat and his younger brother, Sameer Minhas, have both been named in Pakistan's squad for the Test series.

We wanted to build a partnership and take the game deep because we knew their frontline bowlers had almost completed their spells.

“We were clear about our intent and knew that whoever got the opportunity to hit a boundary would take it. Hasan was finding it difficult to get going initially, but I felt the ball was coming nicely on to my bat, so I decided to take my chances. Once we started finding boundaries, the pressure eased and Hasan supported me well.”

Arafat, who made his ODI debut against Australia in Rawalpindi earlier this year, also explained how a change of ball in the closing stages of the innings helped Pakistan regain momentum during the chase.

“The ball had become heavy because of the dew and was staying low, which made hitting difficult. When the ball was changed around the 44th or 45th over, it started coming on to the bat much better. I told Hasan that we should look to attack deliveries in our hitting areas.

“We needed a big over as the required run rate was around nine or 10. We managed to get that big over, which shifted the momentum in our favour and helped us complete the chase.”

Reflecting on the atmosphere at a packed Gaddafi Stadium, Arafat said playing in front of a passionate home crowd provided additional motivation, although remaining composed under pressure was equally important.

“I personally enjoy playing in front of big crowds. When you hit a boundary and the entire stadium erupts, it gives you goosebumps and a lot of motivation. But the real challenge in those situations is to control your nerves, remain calm and make the right decisions.”

The youngster, who has represented Pakistan in eight ODIs and seven T20Is, said winning the player of the series award had boosted his confidence but would not change his approach to the game.

“Winning the player of the series award definitely gives you confidence and improves your mindset. However, I believe your work ethic, hard work and routine should remain the same. I try to maintain the same mindset whether I perform well or not and continue to back myself.

“When you receive such recognition, expectations naturally increase. I take those expectations positively because they motivate me to improve further and give my best for Pakistan in every match.”

Discussing the challenge of switching between formats, Arafat said mental preparation and maintaining a disciplined routine were essential to adapting quickly.

“Switching formats is largely about your mindset. If you are mentally strong, you can adapt to different challenges. Your routine and hard work remain the same, but you have to prepare yourself mentally for the demands of each format and practise accordingly.”

Following the tri-series, Pakistan are set to face Sri Lanka in a two-match Test series, which forms part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27.

The first Test will be played at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium from November 9-13, while the second will take place at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore from November 17-21.

Arafat and his younger brother, Sameer Minhas, have both been named in Pakistan's squad for the Test series.

headline: Quaid-e-Azam Trophy begins tomorrow
description: Babar Azam, Shaheen and Rizwan among prominent players set to feature as Gold and Silver competitions run simultaneously
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
The 69th edition of Pakistan’s premier first-class competition, the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, will begin on Tuesday with eight teams competing in the Gold tier across Islamabad, Abbottabad and Rawalpindi. The 12-team Silver tier will run simultaneously, serving as a qualification pathway to the Gold competition for the next season.. Defending champions Karachi Blues, Faisalabad, FATA, Lahore Whites, Islamabad, Peshawar Blues, Multan and Sialkot Blues will compete in the Gold tier, which runs from November 3 to December 12. The five-day final, featuring the top two teams, is scheduled for December 15-19. The Silver competition will feature 12 teams divided into two groups of six. Lahore Blues, Rawalpindi, Larkana, Quetta, Bahawalpur and Peshawar Whites form Group A, while Karachi Whites, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Hyderabad, Dera Murad Jamali, Abbottabad and Sialkot Whites make up Group B. Group A matches will be played at three venues in Karachi: KCCA Stadium, SBP and UBL Sports Complex. Group B fixtures will take place at Multan Cricket Stadium, Sports Complex Rahim Yar Khan and Dring Stadium in Bahawalpur. The Silver-tier group stage will run from November 3-30, with the five-day final between the two group winners scheduled for December 3-7. A total of 29 first-class matches will be played in the Gold tier and 31 in the Silver competition. Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam is set to represent Lahore Whites in the opening round, when they face FATA, led by Shaheen Shah Afridi, at Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad. The tournament will also feature several other prominent Pakistan internationals, including Saud Shakeel, Saim Ayub, Imam-ul-Haq, Mohammad Rizwan, Sahibzada Farhan, Iftikhar Ahmed, Abdullah Shafique and Hasan Ali.

article_html:
The 69th edition of Pakistan’s premier first-class competition, the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, will begin on Tuesday with eight teams competing in the Gold tier across Islamabad, Abbottabad and Rawalpindi.
The 12-team Silver tier will run simultaneously, serving as a qualification pathway to the Gold competition for the next season..
Defending champions Karachi Blues, Faisalabad, FATA, Lahore Whites, Islamabad, Peshawar Blues, Multan and Sialkot Blues will compete in the Gold tier, which runs from November 3 to December 12. The five-day final, featuring the top two teams, is scheduled for December 15-19.
The Silver competition will feature 12 teams divided into two groups of six. Lahore Blues, Rawalpindi, Larkana, Quetta, Bahawalpur and Peshawar Whites form Group A, while Karachi Whites, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Hyderabad, Dera Murad Jamali, Abbottabad and Sialkot Whites make up Group B.
Group A matches will be played at three venues in Karachi: KCCA Stadium, SBP and UBL Sports Complex. Group B fixtures will take place at Multan Cricket Stadium, Sports Complex Rahim Yar Khan and Dring Stadium in Bahawalpur.
The Silver-tier group stage will run from November 3-30, with the five-day final between the two group winners scheduled for December 3-7.
A total of 29 first-class matches will be played in the Gold tier and 31 in the Silver competition.
Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam is set to represent Lahore Whites in the opening round, when they face FATA, led by Shaheen Shah Afridi, at Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad.
The tournament will also feature several other prominent Pakistan internationals, including Saud Shakeel, Saim Ayub, Imam-ul-Haq, Mohammad Rizwan, Sahibzada Farhan, Iftikhar Ahmed, Abdullah Shafique and Hasan Ali.

headline: Pakistan assumes SCO Interbank Consortium chairmanship for 2026-27
description: Chairmanship demonstrates Pakistan's growing role in promoting regional trade, investment, financial connectivity
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan on Monday assumed the chairmanship of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Interbank Consortium (SCO-IBC) for 2026-27, with Sultan Ali Allana taking over as chairman, the Ministry of Finance said on Monday.

In a post on X, the ministry said the development coincided with Pakistan's chairmanship of the SCO for the same period. HBL Chairman Sultan Ali Allana assumed the consortium chairmanship for the 2026-27 term.

“The Ministry of Finance congratulates Allana on assuming this important responsibility and reaffirms Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening economic partnerships among SCO member states, facilitating cross-border trade and investment, and advancing regional integration and shared prosperity,” the ministry said.

It added that the two chairmanships underscored Pakistan's “growing role in promoting regional trade, investment, financial connectivity and economic cooperation”.

The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Interbank Consortium (SCO-IBC) is a platform for cooperation among banks from SCO member states. Established in 2005, it aims to support investment projects, facilitate financing and strengthen banking ties across the region. Pakistan is represented by Habib Bank Limited (HBL), whose chairman, Allana, has now assumed the consortium's chairmanship for 2026-27.

Pakistan became a full member of the SCO in 2017, having held observer status since 2005. It has since hosted several events under the organisation, including a joint anti-terrorism exercise with China at the National Counter-Terrorism Centre in Pabbi in 2021, an SCO member states' seminar on military medicine in Rawalpindi in March 2024, and the 23rd meeting of the Council of Heads of Government in Islamabad in October 2024.

The Islamabad summit brought together delegations from all 10 member states, with eight countries represented by their prime ministers. Pakistan has also hosted meetings on regional transport connectivity and poverty alleviation under the SCO framework.

headline: South Africa boost WTC final hopes with Australia series win
description: Proteas need five wins from seven remaining tests to reach second straight WTC final
author: REUTERS
article_text:
South Africa’s series victory over Australia has put them top of the world rankings and greatly enhanced their chances of returning to the World Test Championship final but they must still navigate a home series against England at the end of the year.

The top two teams in ⁠the WTC points table for the 2025-27 cycle, which ends in March, advance to the final in London in June and South Africa are well placed after completing a come-from-behind 2-1 home series win over Australia at the weekend.

They are on a points percentage of 71.43, narrowly behind New Zealand (72.22), but have overtaken Australia who, after their 176-run loss at Newlands on Saturday, dropped to 69.23.

South Africa need five ⁠wins from seven remaining tests in the 2025-27 cycle -- two at home to Bangladesh later this month, a three-test tour by England over Christmas and New Year and two away in Sri Lanka in February -- to qualify for a second successive final and a chance to retain their title.

They will be wary of the threat England pose as they begin a new era with ⁠Stephen Fleming as coach and Joe Root back as captain. England have won three of ⁠their last four series in South Africa, drawing the other.

TOUGH GOING

Even if South Africa lose points, their closest rivals will effectively be cancelling each other out, starting later this month when India (51.52) play two tests in Wellington and Christchurch against New Zealand, who then go to Australia in December for a four-test series, after which the Australians hit the road and go to India in January at the start of a five-test series. A win is worth 12 points, a tie six points each and a draw four points and there can be points deducted for ⁠a slow over rate. But key is that the final ranking is based on the percentage of total points won out of total points contested. ⁠Teams generally need a win percentage above 60% to qualify.

South Africa’s place in the last WTC final, where they beat Australia by five wickets at Lord’s in another dramatic rescue act, was controversial given that they played only 12 tests against moderate opposition while England played 22 tests and Australia and India 19 each over the same qualifying period. South Africa will again play fewer tests in this cycle than Australia, England and India but their credentials are greatly enhanced by beating India 2-0 away late last year and now securing the home success over Australia.

'ICONIC SERIES'

“I think ⁠to go from 10 months of no test cricket to something like that, I think that will be remembered as one of the iconic test series, at least in this century," said South Africa captain Temba Bavuma. "I’d like to believe two quality sides came up against each other and really forced each other to play their best cricket." Next year’s final has been confirmed for The Oval from June 9-13. The first three editions have each produced a different champion.

New Zealand won the inaugural title in 2021, Australia took the mace in 2023 and South Africa ended their long wait for a major trophy last year.

headline: Saudi Arabia gives all-clear after security alert in Jazan amid tensions with Houthis
description: Air defences destroyed a missile launched by Yemen’s Houthis, says coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence announced that a security threat had passed in the southern Jazan region following an alert issued through the National Early Warning Platform, amid escalating tensions with Yemen’s Houthi group.

In a statement on US social media company X, the Civil Defence urged residents to continue following safety instructions and avoid gatherings and filming.

The agency did not specify the nature of the threat or report any casualties or damage.

Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi ballistic missile targeting southern region

The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government said on Monday that its air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthi group toward Saudi Arabia’s southern region.

Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki announced the interception in a statement, without providing further details about the missile’s intended target or possible casualties.

The incident comes amid escalating cross-border attacks by the Houthis against Saudi Arabia.

In recent days, the coalition has reported intercepting several ballistic missiles targeting the capital Riyadh and eastern Saudi Arabia, as well as drones launched toward the country’s southern region.

The attacks come amid renewed fighting between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis in Yemen, where years of conflict have caused a severe humanitarian crisis.

headline: Eisenkot says Netanyahu's bid to discredit Israeli election results has 'failed'
description: Eisenkot says Netanyahu’s bid to discredit Israeli election results has ‘failed’
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Israel’s Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot said a day earlier that efforts by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party to discredit the results of last week’s parliamentary elections and steer the country toward another election had “failed.”

In a post on the US social media platform X, Eisenkot described the attempt as “despicable and malicious.”

“The despicable and malicious attempt to disown the election results, challenge the public’s will, smear an entire community and drag Israel into new elections has failed,” Eisenkot wrote.

“Only someone who realises he has lost would be prepared to wage such a crude delegitimisation campaign, even at the cost of further damaging public trust in state institutions,” he added.

Eisenkot said the results of the elections for the 26th Knesset were “firm and clear,” welcoming remarks by Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg affirming the integrity of the vote.

Read Also: Netanyahu’s bloc projected to win 53 seats, Eisenkot’s 48 in Israeli elections

“Ignore the background noise and the political manoeuvres that change every hour. The people are sovereign, and they have spoken: The government of failure has no majority and has lost the election,” he said.

Netanyahu and Likud have alleged Qatari interference through funding intended to increase turnout among Arab voters and influence the results.

Likud claimed to possess recordings and other materials documenting bribes, including cash and fuel vouchers offered in exchange for votes, describing the alleged activity as “election theft.”

The party has not publicly presented evidence establishing Qatari interference or widespread electoral fraud.

Qatar rejected the accusations on Thursday, calling them a “new disinformation campaign” aimed at drawing it into Israel’s internal political disputes.

United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas also denied allegations of attempts to unlawfully influence the election through foreign funding.

Earlier Sunday, Sohlberg said that voting had proceeded properly and that the results reflected the electorate’s will.

Israel’s Yedioth Ahronoth daily quoted him as saying that claims that the available material and evidence could cast doubt on the election results as a whole were “incorrect.”

He said potential irregularities and suspicions were being examined, stressing that even if substantiated, they would not undermine the overall integrity of the election or its results.

Sohlberg spoke in the presence of Shin Bet chief David Zini and Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara.

With all votes counted, Netanyahu’s bloc secured 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset compared with 48 for the opposition camp led by Eisenkot and 19 for Arab parties. Neither main bloc reached the 61 seats needed for a governing majority.

Final turnout stood at 77.9 per cent, the highest since 1999, according to the elections committee.

The results leave Israel facing a political impasse, with the government’s formation dependent on agreements between blocs and opposition parties divided over the possibility of relying on Arab parties’ support.

The official results are due to be submitted to President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday, ahead of consultations with parties represented in the Knesset on whom to task with forming a government.

headline: Australia name white-ball squads for England series
description: Host of fresh faces are included for the series
author: AFP
article_text: Australia named a host of fresh faces in new-look white-ball squads Monday to face England with exciting young quick Mahli Beardman and allrounders Jack Edwards and Liam Scott among those getting call-ups. Batting prospects Ollie Peake and Jake Fraser-McGurk were also included, as were wicketkeepers Lachlan Shaw and Sam Harper with Mitchell Marsh captaining both the one-day and Twenty20 sides. "These ODI and T20 matches provide several players, many of whom have had opportunities on recent tours, with a great chance to further demonstrate their ability against very strong opposition," said chairman of selectors George Bailey. Beardman, Peake, Edwards, Scott, Nikhil Chaudhary, and Joel Davies made their white-ball debuts in recent times. Harper and Shaw are the two uncapped players. "They are good examples of players who have had an opportunity at the international level and have continued working on their game from what they learnt from those experiences," added Bailey. Australia play three home ODIs against England between November 13-18 followed by five T20s. They will provide an opportunity for Australia's next generation to stake their claims ahead of the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. With a home Test series against New Zealand to follow, star fast bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood are being rested after playing their part in Australia's 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa. Fellow Test players Travis Head, Alex Carey, Matt Renshaw, Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and Cameron Green were named in the ODI squad, but will not play the T20s. Following the New Zealand series, Australia travel to India for five Tests before a 150th anniversary clash in Melbourne against England then an Ashes campaign. "We are in the middle of a highly demanding phase of our schedule," said Bailey, referring to Australia's Test players. "To manage this workload, each player's build-up to the New Zealand series will be carefully planned and focussed on individual's physical and mental preparation." One-day squad: Mitchell Marsh (capt), Xavier Bartlett, Mahli Beardman, Alex Carey, Cooper Connolly, Jack Edwards, Cameron Green, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Spencer Johnson, Ollie Peake, Matt Renshaw, Liam Scott, Adam Zampa T20 squad: Mitchell Marsh (capt), Xavier Bartlett, Mahli Beardman, Nikhil Chaudhary, Tim David, Joel Davies, Jack Edwards, Nathan Ellis, Jake Fraser-McGurk, Sam Harper, Spencer Johnson, Mitch Owen, Lachlan Shaw, Adam Zampa

headline: Michael Che calls Israel’s violence in Gaza ‘genocide’ on ‘SNL’, co-host Colin Jost stunned
description: The moment came during the programme’s Weekend Update segment on Saturday, ahead of Halloween
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Colin Jost was visibly surprised after Michael Che made a joke about Israel and the ongoing conflict in Gaza during the latest episode of Saturday Night Live.

The moment came during the programme’s Weekend Update segment on Saturday, October 31, 2026, when the co-hosts discussed political developments ahead of Halloween.

Alongside jokes about US politicians and election controversies, Che turned his attention to Israel’s October 27 elections.

Commenting on voter participation, Che said: “This week, a record number of people voted in Israel’s election — which is great to see, regardless of if you’re on the right side, or the left side, or the genocide.”

The camera immediately cut to Jost, whose mouth dropped open in an exaggerated expression of shock.

He briefly looked around before continuing with the segment and moving on to a joke about an election controversy involving Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska.

Che’s remark appeared to target Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s political position and the country’s military campaign in Gaza against Hamas.

The joke referenced the wider international controversy surrounding the conflict, with several international bodies, human rights organisations, legal experts and governments describing Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide.

The political exchange was among the most talked-about moments of the Weekend Update segment, which also featured Ben Marshall appearing as a reformed Pennywise the Clown.

Che and Jost have regularly used the segment to address political developments through satire, although this particular remark prompted an especially striking on-camera reaction from Jost.

headline: CDA appoints three retired military officers as DGs in different departments
description: Retired brigadiers appointed to land, civic management, planning and development
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Retired brigadiers appointed to land, civic management, planning and development

The Capital Development Authority (CDA) appointed three retired military officers as directors general (DGs) in Grade 20 across various departments.

The CDA's Human Resource Directorate has also issued notifications confirming the appointments. According to the notifications, Brigadier (Retired) Muhammad Azhar Khan was appointed DG Land, Brigadier (Retired) Muhammad Javed Iqbal was appointed DG Civic Management, and Brigadier (Retired) Rashid Manzoor was appointed DG Planning and Development.

Last month, the Islamabad High Court suspended, until the next hearing, the cancellation of the recruitment process for several posts in the CDA, including assistant director and building inspector.

The court issued notices to the CDA chairman and other respondents and sought their responses. The CDA had also been barred from issuing fresh advertisements for the posts.

Justice Khadim Hussain Somroo issued a two-page written order following the hearing, restraining the CDA from filling the posts through promotions or transfers as well.

headline: Pakistan plans to explore Eurobond tokenisation after cabinet approval: finance minister
description: Says financial innovation should lower business costs, expand financial inclusion and deliver economic benefits
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Monday said that the government was reviewing the possibility of tokenising Pakistan’s existing Eurobond debt and was seeking cabinet approval before inviting proposals for the initiative.

“We are in discussions at this point in time, and we are looking forward to the Cabinet approval on this before we move ahead with issuing the RFP on this front,” he said while delivering a virtual keynote address at the “Dialogue on Digital Assets and the Future of Banking”, organised by the Pakistan Banks’ Association (PBA) in collaboration with LUMS.

Aurangzeb also identified remittances as another potential use of tokenisation, saying Pakistan had received $41.6 billion in remittances during the previous fiscal year, while inflows in the first quarter of the current fiscal year suggested the figure could exceed $44 billion this year.

“Therefore, having this as a use case makes a lot of sense from a tokenisation perspective,” he said.

The finance minister said Pakistan needed "financial innovation" that reduced the "cost of doing business and brings more people into the formal economy," adding that digital assets should be assessed based on the economic benefits they could deliver.

“Can a family receive money from abroad at a lower cost? Can a business get paid sooner? Can an entrepreneur obtain financing on reasonable terms? Can we attract productive investment while protecting the stability of our financial system?” he asked. “These are the outcomes that I would suggest should guide this discussion,” he added.

Aurangzeb said Pakistan was moving from macroeconomic stability towards sustainable growth, a transition that required fiscal discipline, stronger exports and greater private investment.

“Digital innovation should therefore support these priorities with its value demonstrated through results and impact,” he said.

Referring to international developments, he cited JPMorgan's use of deposit tokens to facilitate money transfers for institutional clients over blockchain networks and the Bank for International Settlements' Project Agora, which is examining how tokenised commercial bank deposits and central bank reserves could improve cross-border settlements.

He said banks had a critical role in the development of digital finance, as their responsibilities for safeguarding money, managing risk and serving customers would remain central as technology evolved.

The minister also stressed the need to distinguish between different forms of digital assets: “A tokenised bank deposit remains a claim on a bank. A stablecoin's risk depends on its issuer, backing, and redemption arrangements. An unbacked cryptoasset carries a different set of risks."

“A regulatory approach therefore must reflect these differences and the economic activity behind each product,” he added.

Aurangzeb said Pakistan had established a statutory framework through the Virtual Assets Act 2026, with the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) responsible for licensing and supervising virtual asset service providers.

“The task now is to make that framework effective in practice through capable supervision and clear coordination among institutions,” he said.

He credited PVARA's chairman with helping move the country from prohibition and regulatory ambiguity towards a statutory framework for supervised participation. He also acknowledged the roles played by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) in developing the regulatory framework.

Aurangzeb said the SBP had provided a conditional route for banking services to businesses licensed by PVARA, subject to due diligence and the segregation of client funds. Accounts for holders of no-objection certificates had a more limited purpose while licensing formalities were completed, he added.

“The restrictions on banks investing, trading, or holding virtual assets using their own funds or customer deposits also remain in place,” he said.

“You bring the customer relationships, operational experience, and risk management capabilities that this work requires,” he said, addressing banking leaders. “Please invest in the expertise to assess these technologies and work with relevant regulators on the activities permitted within your mandates and of course with the support of your respective boards,” he added.

Aurangzeb also warned of growing cybersecurity threats, saying that one needed to acknowledge that "we are under attack 24/7" by state and non-state actors and that therefore there was "no room" for complacency.

He urged banks and the SBP to follow through on measures to address emerging cybersecurity risks as the financial sector adopted digital technologies.

The minister also referred to Pakistan's engagement with international discussions on blockchain and tokenisation, including a dialogue co-convened with the United Nations Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies in New York in late September.

He said Pakistan's assumption of the G-24 chairmanship would provide another opportunity to contribute to the global discussion, particularly by bringing the perspectives of developing economies to the debate.

Aurangzeb concluded by calling for practical recommendations from the banking sector and other stakeholders to guide the country's approach to digital assets.

Tokenisation involves creating digital representations of assets, such as government bonds, on a blockchain, allowing ownership to be recorded and potentially transferred digitally. In December 2025, the government signed a memorandum of understanding with Binance to explore tokenising up to $2 billion worth of government assets, including sovereign bonds, treasury bills and commodity reserves.

Pakistan raised funds from international investors through Eurobonds, which are government debt securities issued in foreign currencies, usually US dollars. Investors lend money to the government in return for regular interest payments, with the principal repaid when the bonds mature. Pakistan used these borrowings to meet external financing requirements and build foreign exchange reserves. In September 2026, the government raised $3 billion through a dual-tranche Eurobond issue, offering bonds with maturities of five-and-a-half and 10 years.

The government had also been working towards regulating virtual assets, including cryptocurrencies and digital asset service providers. The Virtual Assets Act 2026 established the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA), which is responsible for licensing and supervising virtual asset businesses. The framework covers activities such as exchanges, custody services and asset management. The Express Tribune reported in August 2026 that the authorities had launched the virtual assets licensing system.

In a separate initiative, PVARA and the State Bank have been examining the possibility of issuing tokenised sovereign notes to improve access to investment for overseas Pakistanis, speed up settlements, and make securities ownership more transparent,

article_html:
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Monday said that the government was reviewing the possibility of tokenising Pakistan’s existing Eurobond debt and was seeking cabinet approval before inviting proposals for the initiative.

“We are in discussions at this point in time, and we are looking forward to the Cabinet approval on this before we move ahead with issuing the RFP on this front,” he said while delivering a virtual keynote address at the “Dialogue on Digital Assets and the Future of Banking”, organised by the Pakistan Banks’ Association (PBA) in collaboration with LUMS.

Aurangzeb also identified remittances as another potential use of tokenisation, saying Pakistan had received $41.6 billion in remittances during the previous fiscal year, while inflows in the first quarter of the current fiscal year suggested the figure could exceed $44 billion this year.

“Therefore, having this as a use case makes a lot of sense from a tokenisation perspective,” he said.

The finance minister said Pakistan needed "financial innovation" that reduced the "cost of doing business and brings more people into the formal economy," adding that digital assets should be assessed based on the economic benefits they could deliver.

“Can a family receive money from abroad at a lower cost? Can a business get paid sooner? Can an entrepreneur obtain financing on reasonable terms? Can we attract productive investment while protecting the stability of our financial system?” he asked. “These are the outcomes that I would suggest should guide this discussion,” he added.

Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue, Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, delivering a virtual keynote address at the “Dialogue on Digital Assets and the Future of Banking”, organised by the Pakistan Banks’ Association (PBA) in collaboration with LUMS, today. pic.twitter.com/wXQy1IvCHE

— Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan (@Financegovpk) November 2, 2026

Aurangzeb said Pakistan was moving from macroeconomic stability towards sustainable growth, a transition that required fiscal discipline, stronger exports and greater private investment.

“Digital innovation should therefore support these priorities with its value demonstrated through results and impact,” he said.

Referring to international developments, he cited JPMorgan's use of deposit tokens to facilitate money transfers for institutional clients over blockchain networks and the Bank for International Settlements' Project Agora, which is examining how tokenised commercial bank deposits and central bank reserves could improve cross-border settlements.

He said banks had a critical role in the development of digital finance, as their responsibilities for safeguarding money, managing risk and serving customers would remain central as technology evolved.

The minister also stressed the need to distinguish between different forms of digital assets: “A tokenised bank deposit remains a claim on a bank. A stablecoin's risk depends on its issuer, backing, and redemption arrangements. An unbacked cryptoasset carries a different set of risks."

“A regulatory approach therefore must reflect these differences and the economic activity behind each product,” he added.

Aurangzeb said Pakistan had established a statutory framework through the Virtual Assets Act 2026, with the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) responsible for licensing and supervising virtual asset service providers.

“The task now is to make that framework effective in practice through capable supervision and clear coordination among institutions,” he said.

Read: Hackers steal $6.3b from Binance

He credited PVARA's chairman with helping move the country from prohibition and regulatory ambiguity towards a statutory framework for supervised participation. He also acknowledged the roles played by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) in developing the regulatory framework.

Aurangzeb said the SBP had provided a conditional route for banking services to businesses licensed by PVARA, subject to due diligence and the segregation of client funds. Accounts for holders of no-objection certificates had a more limited purpose while licensing formalities were completed, he added.

“The restrictions on banks investing, trading, or holding virtual assets using their own funds or customer deposits also remain in place,” he said.

“You bring the customer relationships, operational experience, and risk management capabilities that this work requires,” he said, addressing banking leaders. “Please invest in the expertise to assess these technologies and work with relevant regulators on the activities permitted within your mandates and of course with the support of your respective boards,” he added.

Aurangzeb also warned of growing cybersecurity threats, saying that one needed to acknowledge that "we are under attack 24/7" by state and non-state actors and that therefore there was "no room" for complacency.

He urged banks and the SBP to follow through on measures to address emerging cybersecurity risks as the financial sector adopted digital technologies.

The minister also referred to Pakistan's engagement with international discussions on blockchain and tokenisation, including a dialogue co-convened with the United Nations Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies in New York in late September.

Read more: Pakistan raises $3b through Eurobond

He said Pakistan's assumption of the G-24 chairmanship would provide another opportunity to contribute to the global discussion, particularly by bringing the perspectives of developing economies to the debate.

Aurangzeb concluded by calling for practical recommendations from the banking sector and other stakeholders to guide the country's approach to digital assets.

Tokenisation involves creating digital representations of assets, such as government bonds, on a blockchain, allowing ownership to be recorded and potentially transferred digitally. In December 2025, the government signed a memorandum of understanding with Binance to explore tokenising up to $2 billion worth of government assets, including sovereign bonds, treasury bills and commodity reserves.

Pakistan raised funds from international investors through Eurobonds, which are government debt securities issued in foreign currencies, usually US dollars. Investors lend money to the government in return for regular interest payments, with the principal repaid when the bonds mature. Pakistan used these borrowings to meet external financing requirements and build foreign exchange reserves. In September 2026, the government raised $3 billion through a dual-tranche Eurobond issue, offering bonds with maturities of five-and-a-half and 10 years.

The government had also been working towards regulating virtual assets, including cryptocurrencies and digital asset service providers. The Virtual Assets Act 2026 established the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA), which is responsible for licensing and supervising virtual asset businesses. The framework covers activities such as exchanges, custody services and asset management. The Express Tribune reported in August 2026 that the authorities had launched the virtual assets licensing system.

In a separate initiative, PVARA and the State Bank have been examining the possibility of issuing tokenised sovereign notes to improve access to investment for overseas Pakistanis, speed up settlements, and make securities ownership more transparent,

Aurangzeb also identified remittances as another potential use of tokenisation, saying Pakistan had received $41.6 billion in remittances during the previous fiscal year, while inflows in the first quarter of the current fiscal year suggested the figure could exceed $44 billion this year.
