headline: Hilary Duff reveals she was ‘f***ing done’ with Lizzie McGuire after show ended
description: The singer says she struggled to establish her identity beyond the Disney character after becoming a household name
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Hilary Duff has opened up about feeling exhausted by her Lizzie McGuire fame after the hit Disney Channel series ended, admitting she once wanted nothing to do with the character or its most famous song.

In an interview with Paper magazine, Duff reflected on filming The Lizzie McGuire Movie, which followed the television series and featured the memorable track “What Dreams Are Made Of”.

The singer said the demanding production schedule had taken a toll on her. She filmed 30 episodes during one year and another 35 the following year, while her growing popularity meant audiences increasingly identified her exclusively with Lizzie.

“I was pretty done with Lizzie at that time,” Duff said, explaining that she wanted people to recognise her as an individual rather than constantly associate her with the Disney character.

The experience also affected her relationship with “What Dreams Are Made Of”. Duff recalled reaching a point when she felt she would never perform the song again, partly because she did not own it and wanted to move beyond her television persona.

However, her perspective has changed over time. Duff recently re-recorded the track for her *(Mine)* EP and performed it live for the first time during her Small Rooms, Big Nerves Tour.

She said singing it now feels different because she can appreciate what the song means to fans while also embracing it as part of her own musical history.

Duff also admitted that looking back, she would welcome the opportunity to revisit parts of that period. Although she remains grateful that audiences connected with the show and film, she said she was not fully comfortable with the experience at the time.

Lizzie McGuire premiered in January 2001 and ran for two seasons, ending in 2004 after 65 episodes. The film helped cement the character’s lasting place in pop culture.

headline: Savannah Guthrie makes emotional plea for answers as mother Nancy remains missing
description: Nancy disappeared from her Tucson, Arizona, home after reportedly being last seen at around 9:30pm on January 31
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Savannah Guthrie has made another emotional public appeal for information about her missing mother, Nancy Guthrie, saying her family cannot move forward without answers.

The Today show presenter shared a photograph of an old drawing made by her 12-year-old daughter, Vale, on Instagram on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

The drawing featured a blue umbrella and the handwritten message: “I know it might not seem like it, but I really need my mommy.”

Reflecting on the illustration, Savannah wrote: “Found this old drawing from my daughter today. It says so much about how I feel. The world goes on, things appear ‘normal’ — as we try to keep going and be strong, especially for our young kids — but it’s not and it never will be.”

View this post on Instagram

The 54-year-old journalist said her family continues to ache for Nancy, 84, and desperately wants information about her whereabouts.

“We cannot move forward,” she wrote. “We need someone to help us, tell us what you know.”

Savannah also described her mother as “a light in this world” and appealed to the public to help bring her home.

“We want to celebrate her and give her the dignity she deserves,” she added. “The reward is still available. Please. We are begging you. Please help us.”

Nancy disappeared from her Tucson, Arizona, home after reportedly being last seen at around 9:30pm on January 31.

The FBI subsequently released footage showing a masked individual outside her property.

The family is offering a $1 million reward for information leading to Nancy. Several alleged ransom notes have also emerged during the investigation.

Savannah previously acknowledged the possibility that her mother might no longer be alive, while emphasising that the family still needs answers and wants her home.

headline: Matt Damon and David Letterman make brief cameos in 'The Gilded Age' season 4 premiere
description: Matt Damon and David Letterman appear briefly in opening episode of 'The Gilded Age’s' fourth season
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Matt Damon and David Letterman made unexpected appearances in the season four premiere of HBO’s The Gilded Age, although viewers could easily have missed their brief cameos.

The pair appear at approximately eight minutes and 33 seconds into the episode, crossing a street together without speaking.

Damon wears a top hat, an ascot, a long coat and distinctive sideburns with a moustache, while Letterman appears in a bowler hat and an all-black outfit, retaining his familiar beard.

Neither actor has any dialogue, and their appearance is limited to the short scene. Their presence is one of several surprises in the season premiere, which also introduces significant developments for the show's central characters.

Among the episode's major storylines is the wedding of Oscar van Rhijn (Blake Ritson) and Enid Turner (Kelley Curran). The pair enter a lavender marriage, which appears to be a mutually understood arrangement.

Enid later reveals to Agnes van Rhijn (Christine Baranski) that both she and Oscar entered the marriage fully aware of his sexuality. She also expresses her intention to support his interests in the arts and Agnes' charitable work.

Meanwhile, Marian (Louisa Jacobson) reunites with her former fiancé Larry Russell (Harry Richardson) at an after-hours gathering following the wedding.

After an incident forces them to take shelter at a hotel, the former couple spend the night together. Marian becomes concerned about the potential damage to her reputation the following morning.

Elsewhere, Peggy celebrates the publication of her book, while her future mother-in-law, Elizabeth Kirkland (Phylicia Rashad), appears to have plans involving her and her mother.

In another major development, Gladys (Taissa Farmiga) survives a life-threatening childbirth emergency, but undergoes a hysterectomy to save her life.

New episodes of The Gilded Age season four air on Sunday nights at 9pm ET/PT on HBO.

Matt Damon and David Letterman made unexpected appearances in the season four premiere of HBO’s The Gilded Age, although viewers could easily have missed their brief cameos.

The pair appear at approximately eight minutes and 33 seconds into the episode, crossing a street together without speaking.

Damon wears a top hat, an ascot, a long coat and distinctive sideburns with a moustache, while Letterman appears in a bowler hat and an all-black outfit, retaining his familiar beard.

Neither actor has any dialogue, and their appearance is limited to the short scene. Their presence is one of several surprises in the season premiere, which also introduces significant developments for the show's central characters.

Among the episode's major storylines is the wedding of Oscar van Rhijn (Blake Ritson) and Enid Turner (Kelley Curran). The pair enter a lavender marriage, which appears to be a mutually understood arrangement.

Enid later reveals to Agnes van Rhijn (Christine Baranski) that both she and Oscar entered the marriage fully aware of his sexuality. She also expresses her intention to support his interests in the arts and Agnes' charitable work.

Meanwhile, Marian (Louisa Jacobson) reunites with her former fiancé Larry Russell (Harry Richardson) at an after-hours gathering following the wedding.

After an incident forces them to take shelter at a hotel, the former couple spend the night together. Marian becomes concerned about the potential damage to her reputation the following morning.

Elsewhere, Peggy celebrates the publication of her book, while her future mother-in-law, Elizabeth Kirkland (Phylicia Rashad), appears to have plans involving her and her mother.

In another major development, Gladys (Taissa Farmiga) survives a life-threatening childbirth emergency, but undergoes a hysterectomy to save her life.

New episodes of The Gilded Age season four air on Sunday nights at 9pm ET/PT on HBO.

headline: PM Shehbaz directs SBP, FBR to resolve tax issues faced by SMEs, exporters
description: Calls for comprehensive risk-coverage mechanism to make it easier for businesses to obtain loans
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to work together to resolve tax-related issues faced by Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs) and exporters, as part of efforts to expand access to financing for priority sectors, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.

According to a statement issued by the PMO, the prime minister, chairing a meeting to review lending facilities for SMEs, housing and agriculture, directed the Finance Ministry to address financing-related problems faced by stakeholders in these sectors and formulate a comprehensive strategy.

He called for a comprehensive risk-coverage mechanism to make it easier for small and medium-sized businesses to obtain loans.

PM Shehbaz said the development of SMEs, housing and agriculture was among the government's foremost priorities, as these sectors could support economic growth and create employment opportunities for young people.

He praised banks that had performed well in extending loans to the three priority sectors under government initiatives. However, he directed the SBP and finance ministry not to extend concessions to banks that were slow in providing financing to farmers, SMEs and beneficiaries of the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar Scheme.

"Banks are of key importance for the development of the private sector," he said, adding that he expected them to extend the same cooperation in financing priority sectors as the government and its institutions provided to banks.

The prime minister said SMEs had significant potential to contribute to economic growth, promote exports and create employment opportunities. He described agriculture as the backbone of the national economy and said the government was working to increase exports through value addition of agricultural produce.

He added that the Apna Ghar Scheme would promote several industries linked to the housing and construction sectors.

The PMO said that during the meeting, officials briefed the prime minister that the SBP was working on three main pillars to increase lending to priority sectors: improving regulations, sharing risks and costs between the government and banks, and expanding digital facilities.

As part of these efforts, the SBP had recently launched the SME Connect digital portal, which allows business owners to apply for loans and track the progress of their applications.

The meeting was informed that, as of October 23, loans worth Rs511 billion had been approved under the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar Programme, covering 86,899 applications. Loans amounting to Rs91 billion had been disbursed to 15,584 applicants, the PMO said.

The total volume of housing finance had reached Rs455 billion, benefiting 187,317 borrowers. In the agriculture sector, lending had reached Rs1,329 billion, benefiting approximately 3.5 million people. Meanwhile, SME financing had reached Rs1,148 billion, with 342,458 businesses receiving loans.

The government had set a target of increasing lending to both the agriculture and SME sectors to Rs1,500 billion by the end of fiscal year 2027, officials said.

The meeting was also informed that the government had introduced risk-sharing and credit-guarantee measures for the housing, agriculture and SME sectors. Work was underway to simplify loan procedures, reduce documentation requirements and improve access to financing through digital systems.

Officials also presented performance indicators for commercial banks across the three priority sectors. The prime minister praised banks that had demonstrated good performance.

Federal ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Rana Tanveer Hussain, Dr Musadik Malik, Mian Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Muhammad Aurangzeb, Attaullah Tarar and Shaza Fatima Khawaja attended the meeting, along with the Prime Minister's Adviser Haroon Akhtar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kiani, SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad, MNAs Hafizuddin and Chaudhry Iftikhar Nazir, and senior officials. Heads and representatives of leading commercial banks were also present.

headline: James McAvoy reveals movie that continues to earn him 'bonkers' royalties
description: James McAvoy says 2016 horror film 'Split' remains his most consistent source of residual income
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
James McAvoy has revealed that Split, the 2016 psychological horror film directed by M. Night Shyamalan, continues to earn him regular residual payments nearly a decade after its release.

The actor, 47, played a man with dissociative identity disorder in the film, which was produced by Blumhouse Productions. Made on a reported budget of $9 million (£6.7 million), Split went on to gross $278 million (£207 million) worldwide, becoming a major commercial success.

Speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, McAvoy explained that although actors sometimes receive small residual cheques from previous projects, Split is the one film that consistently generates payments for him.

"You get the odd cheque for, you know, a couple 100 quid here or sometimes you get checks for, like, 25 cents and you're like, 'It literally costs more to post this than it did for me to cash it,'" he said. "But the only one that really consistently pays me is Split."

McAvoy also recalled the film's financial performance shortly after its release, describing how quickly it began generating returns.

"I think it was made for like $6 million or something like that? And let's say they spent 30 advertising it. In our first weekend, we made 40, so we were in profit," he said. "Our first residual cheque came at the end of the first weekend. It was bonkers."

The actor also discussed what he learned from working with Shyamalan on Split and its sequel, Glass. He credited the filmmaker's preparation and ability to communicate his plans effectively with the crew.

"The thing I took away from him is his preparedness," McAvoy said, explaining that Shyamalan made both films on modest budgets while carefully maximising shooting time and resources.

headline: AI models mostly smarter than top scientists, OpenAI's Altman says
description: CEO says AI models capable of performing white-collar work but people must 'remain in control of the future'
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models have progressed to become mostly smarter than the brightest scientists and capable of performing significant portions of white-collar work, OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said on Monday.

Speaking at the opening ceremony of the Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference in the United Arab Emirates, Altman highlighted the dramatic leap in AI capabilities over the past year. "At the start of this year, AI was mostly not as smart as our smartest scientist, and now it's mostly smarter than them," Altman said.

"AI was mostly not able to do a lot of white-collar jobs, and now it mostly can do a lot of parts of that," he added.

Altman stressed that despite the disruptive impact on global economies and employment, human judgement, creativity and accountability must remain central to the technology's deployment. "We think it is absolutely critical that people remain in control of the future; there should not be a handoff to AI, there should not be a gradual 'we are going to let AI decide what is best for us,'" he said.

"AI needs to be a tool built for people and needs to serve people, not the other way around," Altman noted.

Addressing concerns surrounding the massive electricity demands of computing infrastructure, he described physical power supply as the single biggest bottleneck for the sector. "Everything else we're going to make huge progress on, except atoms are still atoms and the physical world that has to power this is going to be the dominant factor of the cost and the abundance," he said.

Altman also noted that global per capita token consumption has surged from near zero six years ago to roughly 100,000 tokens a month, while top institutional users consume about 500 billion tokens monthly.

Highlighting the host nation's rapid adoption of technology, he pointed out that around 80% of young people in the UAE use ChatGPT on a weekly basis.

During the event, OpenAI announced partnerships with Emirati technology group G42 and state oil producer Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, marking the first global deployment of OpenAI's frontier models by an energy company.

headline: Kelly Osbourne reportedly hurt after Sharon and Jack meet estranged sister Aimee
description: Kelly Osbourne is reportedly upset after Sharon and Jack met with her estranged sister shortly before her birthday
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Kelly Osbourne was reportedly hurt after her mother, Sharon Osbourne, and brother, Jack Osbourne, met with her estranged older sister, Aimee, shortly before Kelly's 42nd birthday.

According to unnamed sources quoted by The Sun, the meeting took place on October 26 outside Jack's Los Angeles home.

Photographs reportedly showed Jack, 40, hugging Aimee, 43, while Sharon was also present. Kelly was not pictured at the gathering.

The sources claimed Kelly was surprised by the meeting but respected her family's right to maintain relationships with Aimee.

They added that she would not allow the visit to affect her relationships with her mother or brother. The report suggested Sharon and Jack had reached out to support Aimee following the death of their father, Ozzy Osbourne, in July 2025.

A source claimed Aimee had withdrawn while grieving and found photographs and videos of her father difficult to watch.

The reported meeting comes weeks after Kelly discussed her estrangement from Aimee during a September 15 appearance on Paul C.

Brunson's We Need to Talk podcast. She explained that Aimee had largely kept to herself during their childhood, while Kelly and Jack developed a closer relationship.

Kelly also discussed feeling that her older sister had been embarrassed by the family, although she acknowledged she could not speak for Aimee. Asked whether reconciliation was possible, Kelly said, "I respect her. I accept her. But we're different. And that's OK."

The Sun's report suggested Kelly might be open to hearing from Aimee if she made the first move, although this was attributed to a source rather than a new public statement from Kelly.

Jack previously described his relationship with Aimee as distant, saying in July 2025: "We're not close at all."

Aimee has also spoken about her decision not to appear on the family's MTV reality series, The Osbournes, explaining in a 2015 interview that she wanted to protect her privacy.

They added that she would not allow the visit to affect her relationships with her mother or brother. The report suggested Sharon and Jack had reached out to support Aimee following the death of their father, Ozzy Osbourne, in July 2025.
A source claimed Aimee had withdrawn while grieving and found photographs and videos of her father difficult to watch.
The reported meeting comes weeks after Kelly discussed her estrangement from Aimee during a September 15 appearance on Paul C.
Brunson's We Need to Talk podcast. She explained that Aimee had largely kept to herself during their childhood, while Kelly and Jack developed a closer relationship.

Kelly also discussed feeling that her older sister had been embarrassed by the family, although she acknowledged she could not speak for Aimee. Asked whether reconciliation was possible, Kelly said, "I respect her. I accept her. But we're different. And that's OK."
The Sun's report suggested Kelly might be open to hearing from Aimee if she made the first move, although this was attributed to a source rather than a new public statement from Kelly.
Jack previously described his relationship with Aimee as distant, saying in July 2025: "We're not close at all."
Aimee has also spoken about her decision not to appear on the family's MTV reality series, The Osbournes, explaining in a 2015 interview that she wanted to protect her privacy.

headline: Taylor Swift reveals childhood habit her husband Travis Kelce has to tolerate
description: Taylor Swift shares long-running inside joke she still enjoys with childhood friend Abigail Anderson
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Taylor Swift has revealed that she still shares an unusual childhood tradition with her best friend, Abigail Anderson Berard, more than two decades after they first met, and it is something their husbands have learnt to tolerate.

The singer discussed the habit during a Toy Story 5 screening and question-and-answer session in New York City on Sunday, November 1.

Speaking alongside filmmaker Andrew Stanton, Swift explained how the film's portrayal of friendship reminded her of her longstanding relationship with Abigail.

The pair met when Swift moved to Nashville at the age of 14 and started at a new school. They soon discovered a shared love of impersonating characters from the 2004 comedy Napoleon Dynamite.

Their running joke has continued into adulthood, with the two still speaking to each other in voices from the film.

"We still do this," Taylor admitted. "It's something our husbands have to put up with."

The comment was also a reference to Swift's husband, Kansas City Chiefs player Travis Kelce. Abigail married Charles Berard in 2022.

Their friendship has previously influenced Swift's music. Abigail inspired the singer's 2008 song "Fifteen", from her album Fearless, which reflects on the experiences of starting high school. She also appeared in the track's music video.

Abigail has remained part of Swift's life as her career has developed, accompanying her to the 2015 Grammy Awards and appearing in the 2020 Netflix documentary Miss Americana. Swift also celebrated when her friend welcomed her first child in 2024.

Swift attended Sunday's event to discuss Toy Story 5, for which she co-wrote and produced the song "I Knew It, I Knew You" with Jack Antonoff. The track was inspired by Jessie, the cowgirl character introduced in Toy Story 2.

Reflecting on the film's friendship themes, Swift said, "That hit me so hard watching the film."

headline: Michael Jackson’s ‘Thriller’ breaks streaming record with 6.6m Halloween streams reaching Global Spotify No. 1
description: The 1982 hit more than doubled its daily streams as Halloween listeners sent it soaring up the charts
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Michael Jackson has secured another remarkable milestone as his iconic song Thriller reached the top of Spotify’s Global chart for the first time since its release in 1982.

The legendary Halloween anthem claimed the No. 1 position on October 31, recording an impressive 6.606 million streams worldwide. The achievement came almost 44 years after the song first captivated audiences, demonstrating its enduring appeal across generations.

The streaming surge was closely tied to Halloween celebrations, with listeners returning to the classic track as part of the season’s musical traditions. Its daily streams more than doubled from October 30, when Thriller received 3.09 million plays and ranked at No. 8 on the Global chart.

The milestone also followed another major achievement for the song, which reportedly reached No. 1 on Apple Music’s US chart during the same Halloween period. Together, the results highlight the continued popularity of Jackson’s music across major streaming platforms.

The latest chart success marks Jackson’s second Global Spotify No. 1 in 2026. His song “Billie Jean” previously returned to the summit in June, adding another significant moment to the late singer’s enduring musical legacy.

Thriller also experienced renewed success on the Billboard Hot 100 following Halloween celebrations last year, when it returned to the chart’s top 10. Its latest streaming performance could offer further momentum for its position on the next chart update.

Originally released in 1982, Thriller remains one of Jackson’s most recognisable songs.

headline: Suki Waterhouse adresses secret Robert Pattinson marriage rumours
description: Suki Waterhouse and Robert Pattinson are considering 'massive' wedding after busy year, amid secret event rumours
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Suki Waterhouse has confirmed that she and Robert Pattinson have not married yet, putting an end to speculation that the couple secretly tied the knot. However, the singer and actress has hinted that they could eventually celebrate with a large wedding.

In an interview with The Sunday Times, published on November 1, Waterhouse, 34, discussed her plans with Pattinson, 40, explaining that they have considered holding a substantial celebration rather than opting for a small ceremony.

"It would either be all or nothing," she said of their wedding. "If we were going to go for it we'd have a massive party, blow it out."

Waterhouse added that their wedding plans are currently on hold until after the end of the year because of their demanding work schedules.

Rumours that the couple had already married began in January 2025, when actress Sharon Stone referred to Pattinson as Waterhouse's "husband".

The comment prompted speculation that the pair had secretly exchanged vows, although Waterhouse has now clarified that they are still engaged.

The couple began dating in 2018 and have been together for nearly a decade. Reflecting on their relationship, Waterhouse spoke about how happy she feels with Pattinson.

"It is almost a decade and that is a beautiful thing," she shared. "It's a thing that I go, 'I can't believe I have this in my life and I can't believe that I'm so happy.'"

The couple also share a two-year-old daughter, who was born in March 2024. Waterhouse said she feels confident about their approach to parenting, despite describing their circumstances as an "abnormal life".

"I feel good about how we're doing it and we are both just so connected to her," she said. "She's such a wonderful, happy girl."

headline: Sydney Sweeney backed by former Bond girl for potential role in next 007 film
description: Trina Parks says Sydney Sweeney has qualities to become next leading lady in James Bond franchise
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Sydney Sweeney has received support from a former James Bond actress as speculation continues over the future of the long-running film franchise and its next leading man.

Trina Parks, who played Thumper opposite Sean Connery in the 1971 film Diamonds Are Forever, has said Sweeney would make a suitable Bond girl in the upcoming era of 007. Parks made history as the first Black actress to portray a Bond girl in the series.

Speaking to The Telegraph, Parks praised Sweeney's acting range, confidence and screen presence, suggesting that her approach to her public image would suit the franchise's changing portrayal of female characters.

"She has done quite a range of acting things and basically has got ownership of her sexual identity," she said. "Not only is she a talented actress, but has this Hollywood classic kind of style and poise, which really works for her projects and brand."

Parks also discussed how the role of women in Bond films has evolved, arguing that modern audiences expect female characters to have greater independence.

"I feel for modern cinema and film-making and the future of Bond, audiences want to see a woman opposite Bond who is independent and has ownership of her sexuality — Sydney has those qualities," she added.

The comments come as producers reportedly begin the search for Daniel Craig's successor following his departure from the franchise in 2021's No Time To Die.

Actors Callum Turner and Jack Lowden have been linked to the final audition stages, although no replacement has been officially confirmed.

Producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson are reportedly considering a significant reinvention of the franchise for a new generation.

Sydney Sweeney has received support from a former James Bond actress as speculation continues over the future of the long-running film franchise and its next leading man.

Trina Parks, who played Thumper opposite Sean Connery in the 1971 film Diamonds Are Forever, has said Sweeney would make a suitable Bond girl in the upcoming era of 007. Parks made history as the first Black actress to portray a Bond girl in the series.

Speaking to The Telegraph, Parks praised Sweeney's acting range, confidence and screen presence, suggesting that her approach to her public image would suit the franchise's changing portrayal of female characters.

"She has done quite a range of acting things and basically has got ownership of her sexual identity," she said. "Not only is she a talented actress, but has this Hollywood classic kind of style and poise, which really works for her projects and brand."

Parks also discussed how the role of women in Bond films has evolved, arguing that modern audiences expect female characters to have greater independence.

"I feel for modern cinema and film-making and the future of Bond, audiences want to see a woman opposite Bond who is independent and has ownership of her sexuality — Sydney has those qualities," she added.

The comments come as producers reportedly begin the search for Daniel Craig's successor following his departure from the franchise in 2021's No Time To Die.

Actors Callum Turner and Jack Lowden have been linked to the final audition stages, although no replacement has been officially confirmed.

Producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson are reportedly considering a significant reinvention of the franchise for a new generation.

headline: Candice Swanepoel sparks Tom Brady engagement rumours after being spotted with mysterious ring
description: The sighting sparked buzz about the model and the NFL star taking their reported relationship to the next level
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel have fuelled engagement speculation after the supermodel was photographed wearing a gold band on her left ring finger in Florida.

The 37-year-old Victoria’s Secret Angel was spotted in Surfside, Florida, in late October 2026, wearing the jewellery with an all-black outfit.

The sighting prompted questions about whether the model and the retired NFL star had taken their reported relationship to the next level.

However, there is currently no confirmed engagement, and neither Brady nor Swanepoel has publicly acknowledged being a couple.

According to reports, the ring could simply be a personal jewellery choice, with no evidence linking it to a proposal.

Dating rumours involving the pair first emerged through Us Weekly and were subsequently reported by People.

Sources cited by TMZ claimed their relationship began in June, with the two reportedly favouring private locations around Miami.

Swanepoel, a South African supermodel, became internationally recognised through her work with Victoria’s Secret. She also founded sustainable swimwear brand Tropic of C in 2018.

She shares two sons, Anacan and Ariel, with her former fiancé, Hermann Nicoli. The pair ended their relationship in 2018 after more than a decade together.

Meanwhile, Page Six reported alleged tension between Swanepoel and fellow model Joan Smalls, who was previously linked to Brady.

“She and Joan share a longstanding history and a friendship that Candice will always respect,” Swanepoel’s representative told Us Weekly.

For now, the engagement rumours remain unconfirmed, with the gold ring offering no definitive indication of a proposal.

headline: Warriors continue unbeaten streak
description: Muneeba Ali’s side register a comfortable 24-run win over team Champions
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Muneeba Ali’s Warriors registered their third consecutive win the PCB Women’s Super-3 T20 Tournament as they beat Tuba Hassan’s Champions by 24 runs in the fifth match here at the Iqbal Stadium, Faisalabad on Monday.

Chasing a target of 155 runs, Champions were dismissed for 130 in 19.2 overs with left-arm spinner Ayesha Bilal taking four for 15. Warriors have now won three matches on the trot and will face Incredibles in their fourth match on Tuesday.

Incredibles have lost all of their three matches and are out of the race for the final as the Champions have managed two wins out of their four matches and have secured the berth.

On Monday, Ayesha showcased her prowess with the ball as she cut through Champions’ batting by taking wickets of Saira Jabeen, Najiha Alvi and Tuba (18, 16b, 2x4s) at a time when the game would have easily tilted away. Ayesha later pinned no.10 Tayyaba Imdad leg-before to return figures of 4-0-15-4.

Warriors’ spinners Zunash Abdul Sattar and Rameen Shamim also contributed as the former picked up 2-27 with her leg-spin and the latter 1-17 including the wicket of the aggressive opener Komal Khan (18, 12b, 2x4s, 1x6).

Natalia Parvaiz (31, 27b, 2x4s, 1x6) and Shawaal Zulfiqar (22, 12b, 3x4s, 1x6) were the two other batters who showed some resistance, striking boundaries regularly but couldn’t convert their innings. Pacer Diana Baig picked up two wickets, while Humna Bilal dismissed Shawaal.

Earlier, Champions inserted Warriors in after winning the toss. No.4 Hafsa Khalid (47, 36b, 5x4s, 2x6s) and no.6 Rameen (29, 24b, 4x4s) rescued the Warriors’ innings with a 65-run stand after they were 66-4. Diana put the finishing touch towards the end as she contributed valuable 19 runs off 14 balls hitting two fours and one six.

For Champion, Tayyaba picked up two wickets, Tuba, Momina Riasat, Fatima Khan and Ayesha Rehman dismissed one batter each. Tuba had also run out Hafsa as Warriors posted 154-8 in 20 overs.

Scores in brief

Match 5 – Warriors beat Champions by 24 runs at Iqbal Stadium, Faisalabad

Warriors 154-8, 20 overs (Hafsa Khalid 47, Rameen Shamim 29, Sadaf Shamas 22, Diana Baig 19; Tayyaba Imdad 2-27)

Champions 130 all out, 19.2 overs (Natalia Parvaiz 31, Shawaal Zulfiqar 22; Ayesha Bilal 4-15, Diana Baig 2-19, Zunash Abdul Sattar 2-27)

Player of the match – Ayesha Bilal (Warriors)

Chasing a target of 155 runs, Champions were dismissed for 130 in 19.2 overs with left-arm spinner Ayesha Bilal taking four for 15. Warriors have now won three matches on the trot and will face Incredibles in their fourth match on Tuesday.
Incredibles have lost all of their three matches and are out of the race for the final as the Champions have managed two wins out of their four matches and have secured the berth.

On Monday, Ayesha showcased her prowess with the ball as she cut through Champions’ batting by taking wickets of Saira Jabeen, Najiha Alvi and Tuba (18, 16b, 2x4s) at a time when the game would have easily tilted away. Ayesha later pinned no.10 Tayyaba Imdad leg-before to return figures of 4-0-15-4.

Natalia Parvaiz (31, 27b, 2x4s, 1x6) and Shawaal Zulfiqar (22, 12b, 3x4s, 1x6) were the two other batters who showed some resistance, striking boundaries regularly but couldn’t convert their innings. Pacer Diana Baig picked up two wickets, while Humna Bilal dismissed Shawaal.

Diana put the finishing touch towards the end as she contributed valuable 19 runs off 14 balls hitting two fours and one six.
For Champion, Tayyaba picked up two wickets, Tuba, Momina Riasat, Fatima Khan and Ayesha Rehman dismissed one batter each. Tuba had also run out Hafsa as Warriors posted 154-8 in 20 overs.

headline: Saad Baig targets bigger scores after promising Pakistan debut
description: 20-year-old scores 185 runs in five matches ODI tri-series
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Pakistan’s emerging wicketkeeper-batter Saad Baig says he is determined to turn promising starts into bigger scores and establish himself as a dependable performer after an encouraging debut ODI series.

The 20-year-old scored 185 runs in five matches during the recently concluded tri-nation series, including his maiden half-century, and helped Pakistan defeat Sri Lanka by three wickets in Saturday’s final at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium.

Baig made 74 in the title-deciding match as Pakistan chased down a target of 326 to lift the trophy. He also took three catches behind the stumps during the tournament.

Speaking on the Pakistan Cricket Board’s digital programme Straight Drive with Salman Butt, Baig reflected on his first international series, adapting to different batting positions and managing pressure situations.

“My plan was simple. I wanted to carry the confidence and belief I had developed in domestic cricket into international cricket,” he said.

“Whatever the situation, whether early wickets had fallen or a partnership was developing, I wanted to back my skills, play my natural game and trust my abilities.”

Baig said he also learned the importance of adjusting his approach according to the match situation.

“Sometimes you have to control your natural instincts and build a partnership according to the situation. I tried to do that while communicating with my batting partner,” he said. “I am thankful to have contributed to the team’s success.”

The left-hander progressed through Pakistan’s age-group system, representing the country at under-13, under-16 and under-19 levels before captaining the side at the 2024 ICC Men’s Under-19 World Cup.

Pakistan reached the semi-finals of that tournament, losing to Australia by one wicket.

Baig said making the transition from age-group cricket to the senior national team was particularly rewarding, especially as several members of his under-19 batch have also reached the international level.

“It is a very good feeling to have come through a proper pathway, from age-group cricket to captaining Pakistan in the U19 World Cup and then representing the senior national side,” he said.

“I am grateful to have made a positive start, but this is only the beginning. My focus is to keep learning, identify areas where I can improve and develop my game further so that I can perform consistently for Pakistan.”
